title: Can I Send A Mass Email Campaign Using Brilliant Directories?
content:
The built-in email system is designed for emailing active members who have requested to receive emails from the site. A common example would be sending a monthly newsletter to members who have opted in to receive updates.
The email system also sends transactional emails, such as new member signup notifications, credit card update notices, lead emails, and other system-generated messages related to member activity.
Sending mass unsolicited emails to Claim Listings or an imported contact list may be considered spam. This can violate email compliance laws, damage the sending reputation of your domain, and result in future emails being blocked or blacklisted.
In some cases, sending spam messages can also negatively impact other sites on the same server and may lead to account restrictions or termination with Brilliant Directories.

title: Email Forwarders
content:
Email Forwarders Not Supported
IMPORTANT:
The Email Forwarders functionality has been removed from our implementation of cPanel as of June, 2024.
Due to the way this functionality works in cPanel, it caused several issues for users. Some of these issue included:
Not all emails being forwarded properly based on the domain settings of the email sender and the receiver of the forwarded email
Sendgrid blocking emails from being sent to accounts hosted in cPanel, preventing the Admins of sites from getting notification emails
The domain reputation and reputation of the server being harmed when SPAM emails are forwarded through this system
While email forwarders can no longer be added or modified, any existing email forwarders will remain in place.  If an email forwarder needs to be removed from a site, please submit a ticket to our Support Team for assistance.
Recommendations to Replace Email Forwarders
The recommended alternative for using email forwarders is to use an email app that can send and receive emails from multiple email accounts in one place:
Gmail
Paid
Google Workspace
email accounts can connect to 3rd party email accounts to send and receive emails.  For this, the MX record would need to be pointed to Google workspace, for more information:
How To Change Email MX Records
Thunderbird
This is a free desktop email application from Mozilla, the makers of the FireFox browser. Thunderbird offers an app for Windows, MacOS, and Linux operating systems.
Apple Mail
Apple includes a free email client that can connect to 3rd party email accounts for all of their devices and operating systems.
Microsoft
Windows Mail
and
Microsoft Outlook
- Microsoft includes the Windows Mail and Outlook for Windows applications for free on devices using Windows 10 or newer. Both of these applications can connect to 3rd party email accounts.

title: How To Import Members Via CSV File
content:
Overview
Importing members can be a bit of a tricky process due to the fact that all of the data entered must be simple, clean text (no formatting, line breaks, or other things that can break a CSV file), and the data must all be in the proper columns in order to import properly.
To start, here are some files that will help with understanding how the import process works:
Import template with ALL fields and explanations of each field
Import template with only the simple / basic required fields
Example of a completed import file with ALL fields
Example of a completed simple / basic import file
The template and example files that have "
ALL fields
" included show all of the different fields that can be filled out for a member during import.
However, not all imports will need to make use of all of these fields, so we also included a simple / basic version of each that has the most commonly used fields. Importing custom variables is also possible.
Downloading the File
Download one of the CSV import templates shown above.
In
row 1
of this file, one will see all of the headers required to import the data.
Make sure not to edit the spelling of any of these headers
, as doing so will cause the import to fail. In
rows 2 to 4
of this file, one will see an explanation of what kind of text should be added into each column (in the
listing_type
column, rows 2 and 3 show its only two values,
Company
and
Individual
).
Once the required content for each column is understood,
delete rows 2 to 4
from the spreadsheet (if they are not removed, the explanations will be imported as members of the site!)
Enter all of the member data into the correct columns
Delete any empty columns from the spreadsheet - for example, if no data is entered in the Twitter column, that column can be deleted from the spreadsheet completely. This will reduce the size of the import file and speed up the import process.
Add Categories to a CSV Import Spreadsheet
Categories go in 2 columns near the right side of the spreadsheet (columns AM and AN in the template with ALL fields) - "
profession_name
" and "
services
":
Top Categories
Under "
profession_name
" put the Top Level Category for the listing to be imported into. For example, if we were doing this for the Local Dessert Shops Directory then I could add “
Ice Cream Shop
” in this column.
The Membership Plan Settings also allow to pre-assign the Top level category to all profiles in that membership plan. For more information on how to do this, refer to
step 2
in the following
article
.
Sub Categories + Sub-Sub Categories
In the "
services
" column, add a comma-separated list of
Sub Level Categories
and
Sub-Sub Level Categories
one would like the listing added into.
For example, for the listing added into the Top Level Category “Ice Cream Shop”, one could add the Sub Level Categories "Ice Cream,Ice Cream Cake,Ice Cream Cupcake" (since these are all Sub Level Categories of “Ice Cream Shop” that apply to this listing). If one would like a listing imported into ALL Sub Level Categories under the Top Level Category it is being imported into (as designated in the profession_name column), then one could simply put "all" under the services column.
note that all of the Top Level Categories and Sub Level Categories entered into this spreadsheet must be spelled exactly the same as they are in the category structure in the Directory Planner.
If there are several sub or sub-sub-categories with the same name,
it is possible to select which specific sub-category to assign the member to.
1) Specify the sub-category first followed by this sign:
=>
2) Specify the sub-sub category, following this example:
sub level=>sub-sub level (Ice Cream Cake=>Vanilla Cake)
NOTE: Both Sub and Sub-Sub Level Categories should be entered under the "services" column, separated by a comma.
Helpful Tips
Automatically generated member URLs use the current name-formatting rules. Straight or curly apostrophes are removed, most other punctuation and spaces become hyphens, and underscores are preserved. For example, a member name of Ruby’s Clay Studio produces rubys-clay-studio in the name portion of the URL. These rules format the generated URL; the CSV file must still meet the import requirements in this article. See
How To Customize The Member Profile URL Structure
for the complete URL structure.
If any columns are blank in the import file, it is always best to delete the entire column. This is also mentioned above, but is a very common issue that people run into! For example, if none of the members which are going to import have any data for the "fees" column, it is best to delete this column entirely before import.
Some US zip codes begin with a zero or multiple zeros, which Excel and other spreadsheet programs sometimes remove automatically. Make sure all of the zip_codes are formatted as text and have all of the required 0’s at the beginning of the zipcode
If one is entering data for the logo, profile_photo, website, twitter, facebook, linkedin, or google_plus fields, be sure to use full URLs including the http:// (EG: http://www.google.com/image.jpg)
Make sure all listings have something entered into either the company or name field (or first_name and last_name fields) to insure that there will be a title for each listing.
Make sure to enter either
C
ompany
or
I
ndividual
into the
listing_type
field for each listing (Entering "Company" will make the company name more prominent in the listing; entering "Individual" will make the name of the person more prominent in the listing) *Our variables are case sensitive so make sure to capitalize the first letter for these.
Add the Top Level category for each listing into the profession_name column. Note that this must be spelled exactly the same as the category is spelled in the directory, or they will not import correctly. (See the section of this article above titled "How to Add Categories to a CSV Import Spreadsheet" for more tips)
(OPTIONAL) Add a comma-separated list of Sub Level Categories in each listing imported into in the services column (See the section of this article above titled "How to Add Categories to a CSV Import Spreadsheet" for more tips).
For best results, it is recommended to first create the Category Structure in your site before importing your members into these categories. For more information on how to create categories for members.
The fields "name" and " first_name + last_name" will create a conflict if they are both populated in the file.
Simply make sure that only "name" or "first_name + last_name" are populated. Either one will import the name of the listing successfully.
Import Existing Subscription & Billing Information
When importing members whose subscriptions are already established, their existing subscription information can also be included in the CSV file. This is especially useful when migrating members from another platform.
MPORTANT:
These fields are not required for standard member imports. However, if importing subscription information, both
subscription_start_date
and
billing_cycle
must be included together.
Stripe Customer ID
Field Variable:
stripe_customer_id
This field is intended for members who already have an existing Stripe Customer ID, such as when migrating members from another platform that was previously connected to Stripe. Adding the existing Stripe Customer ID allows it to be associated with the imported member.
Accepted format:
cus_
followed by alphanumeric characters only (eg:
cus_ABC123xyz789
)
The
billing_cycle
and
subscription_start_date
fields allow the Billing Cycle and Start Billing On information to be included during the member import, removing the need to manually create this subscription information for each imported member.
Subscription Start Date
Field Variable:
subscription_start_date
This field defines the subscription start date for the imported member. It is available for paid membership plans only and must be provided together with the
billing_cycle
field.
Accepted date formats:
YYYY-MM-DD (example: 2024-06-15)
YYYYMMDD (example: 20240615)
The website's configured date format (e.g. MM/DD/YYYY or DD/MM/YYYY)
The subscription start date cannot be more than one billing cycle in the past or more than 10 years in the future.
Billing Cycle
Field Variable:
billing_cycle
This field defines the billing cycle for the imported member's subscription. It is available for paid membership plans only and must be provided together with the
subscription_start_date
field.
The corresponding billing amount in the selected Membership Plan must be greater than 0. For example, if the billing cycle is Monthly, the plan's monthly amount must be greater than 0.
Available billing cycles depend on the billing options and prices configured for the selected Membership Plan.
Import the File
Navigate to the Search Members section of the admin. On the right side of the page, open the
List Actions
menu and select
Import Members via CSV File
. The import page opens; the numbers in the second screenshot below match the steps that follow.
The Import settings will allow the user to select the membership plan the new listings will belong to. This is required to begin the import.
A second option will allow the admin to determine the status of the listings upon import:
Set as ACTIVE Members
or
Set as NOT ACTIVE Members
.
An option to create a
Member Tag and assign a Tag Group
will show, the system will automatically fill out the tag name with the date and time of the import, the information can be edited and the tag can be assigned to any of the available Tag Groups:
The Advanced Options will allow the import to:
- Pass unique email checks
- Create new categories from the file if they have not been added to the admin yet.
- Geocode the users based on the location added to the CSV file. To use this function, add the "Pretty URLS API Key":
Set Up Pretty URLs with Google Maps
. A status line under the Geocode option shows whether the server key works, with a
Test
button to check it again and a button to add or fix the key (
Add a server key
or
Fix the server key
); a key Google refuses there is not saved.
- Auto import profile photo and logo images -
Member Images: Importing Members with Profile Photos, Logos & Cover Photos
"
Step 2. Upload CSV File Here
" will allow the user to select a CSV import file from the computer.
Once the file is selected, simply select "
Begin File Import
" for the upload to begin.
The
Import Members Data Map
will display on screen, listing each column header from the file with a preview of its first value and the directory property it will be imported into (1). When using the default import templates without any type of variable modification, we recommend to perform the import as is and click
Continue with Import
(2).
If the import file includes custom variables which may have been added to forms prior to the import, the same module will display them on the left side of the columns with an example of a value next to it. A column that does not match an existing property shows
Choose or create a property
in its
Directory Property
dropdown (1). Click that dropdown to choose the property the column should be imported into:
The dropdown lists the existing properties (1): every standard member field, plus any custom field that already has a value saved for at least one member. Should the new variable be missing from the list, click
Create new property
(2) at the bottom of the dropdown to create the variable name for a successful import:
Type the new property name and click
Add
(1) to add it to the dropdown. Use lowercase letters, numbers, underscores or hyphens: uppercase letters are changed to lowercase and spaces to underscores, and a name with any other character, or one already in the list, is not accepted:
Then open the dropdown again, type the new property name in the search box at the top, and click it to choose it for the column.
To leave a column out of the import, open its dropdown and click
Don't import column
(1):
Click
Continue with Import
. One last verification asks "Are you sure you want to run this Import Members File?": click
Yes, Continue
(1) for the file to be imported.
Important Note:
An error message titled
Import File Exceeds Member Limi
t will display in place of the Data Map when the number of members in the file plus the members already on the site is more than the site's member limit:
Once the import is completed a message is going to pop up to
Sync the members with Google Maps
:
"It is recommended to sync all newly imported members with Google Maps so they are searchable by location. Sync members now?" Click
Sync Members
(1) to open the geocoding page now, or
Cancel
to do it later.
To learn more information regarding member limits, refer to the article down below:
100,000 Member Limit Boost
Geocode Members
After importing the members, follow these steps in the link below:
Geocoding Members After A CSV Import
Import Profile Images (optional)
To complete the import of member images and logos, refer to the link below:
Member Images: Importing Members With Profile Photos, Logos & Cover Photos
For the Cover Photo to appear on the profile this Add-on must be active on the website
Profile Cover Photo
.
Get Personal Assistance
We understand that this can be a challenging process, even for some users that are more technically inclined. If one would prefer that someone on our team assists with the import of the members, we have Training Sessions covering importing members. Use the link below to purchase this service: Training Sessions
Important Notes
The files below should be downloaded to the computer and viewed in a spreadsheet application like Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets or another similar application.
Service Areas
can't be imported at this time, this might be something we add in the future.
The system checks default URL fields (website, booking link, social, etc) and only imports them if they’re in a valid URL format - otherwise, they’re skipped. Valid formats are: https://website.com or https://www.website.com.

title: How to Override and Edit Default CSS stylesheets
content:
The
Additional CSS
field applies custom CSS to every page of the website. It is useful for changing the header, the footer, the page background, or any other area that should look the same on all pages. CSS added here overrides the default CSS of the template.
Adding Custom CSS
Go to
Settings >> Design Settings
and open the
Custom CSS / HEAD
tab (1).
Add the custom CSS rules to the
Additional CSS
editor (2).
Check the status line under the editor (3). It should read
CSS looks valid.
(see
Live CSS Checker
below).
Click
Save Changes
.
Important: there is no need to include <style> tags.
Enter the CSS rules only. The website already places the contents of this field inside a style block.
To go back to the default styles, delete the CSS from this field and save. The styles reset to the template defaults.
NOTE:
Be careful when removing CSS from this field, as the custom CSS will be permanently deleted and cannot be retrieved.
Live CSS Checker
The Additional CSS editor checks the CSS while it is typed. A single missing closing brace (
}
) can break the layout of every page, because the custom CSS is placed in the same style block as the page’s other CSS, so the checker catches these mistakes before they are saved.
The checker reports in two places:
The status line
under the editor. It shows
✓ CSS looks valid.
in green when nothing is wrong, or a count of the problems found with the line number and description of the first one.
A marker in the editor margin
next to the line with the problem: red for an error, amber for a warning.
The clip below types a rule with a missing closing brace, shows the red error appear, then adds the brace so the status line returns to
CSS looks valid.
Errors (Saving Is Blocked)
Errors are problems that break the CSS that follows them. They are marked in red (1) and the status line turns red (2), for example
1 error (first on line 1: Unclosed rule — missing closing '}'.)
. The checker reports these errors:
Unclosed rule — missing closing '}'.
A rule or
@media
block was opened with
{
and never closed.
Unexpected '}' with no matching '{'.
There is an extra closing brace.
Unclosed comment — missing closing comment delimiter.
A comment was started with
/*
and never ended with
*/
.
While the Additional CSS has an error, clicking
Save Changes
does not save. A popup titled
Additional CSS has syntax errors
(1) names the line to fix, and the
Custom CSS / HEAD
tab opens so the error is in view. Fix the line, confirm the status line no longer shows an error, then save again.
The block applies to the whole Design Settings page.
The
Save Changes
button saves every Design Settings tab together, so an error in Additional CSS also stops changes on the other tabs from saving until it is fixed.
Warnings (Saving Still Allowed)
Warnings point at CSS that the browser will skip, but they never stop a save. They are marked in amber (1), and the status line ends with
saves still allowed
(2). The checker warns about:
Declaration outside a rule
, such as
color: red;
typed outside any
{ }
. The browser drops it and the rule after it.
Invalid value
for a property, such as
display: blok;
, or an
Unknown property
. The browser ignores that line.
Unclosed '(' or '['
, such as an unfinished
calc(
or
url(
. The browser ignores the CSS after it.
Warnings are worth fixing because the browser skips that CSS, but vendor prefixes (such as
-webkit-
), CSS custom properties (
--my-color
) and other valid modern CSS do not trigger them.
Bracket Matching
Placing the cursor next to a brace highlights the matching brace, which makes it easier to see which rule a closing brace belongs to. A brace with no partner is marked instead.
What the Checker Covers
Only the
Additional CSS
field is checked.
Additional HEAD Code
and
Additional Footer Code
are not checked and save as entered.
The checker runs in the admin editor. CSS that is already broken when the page loads is flagged as soon as the tab opens.

title: How To Access Webmail Through the Admin Area
content:
Webmail reads and sends a mailbox's email in the browser, with no mail program to set up. The admin opens it from
Settings > Domain Manager > Mailboxes
, and for administrators whose role can open the website's cPanel it signs in to the mailbox without asking for the mailbox password.
Before starting
The website must use a custom domain with at least one mailbox on its hosting. See
Settings » Domain Manager » Mailboxes and Email Routing
to create one.
Allow pop-ups for the admin, because webmail opens in a new browser window.
Open a mailbox in webmail
Open
Emails > Email Accounts
, or
Settings > Domain Manager
and select
Mailboxes
.
Find the mailbox in the
Mailboxes
list.
Click
Open webmail
.
The mailbox's inbox opens in a new window, already signed in.
Open webmail (2) on a mailbox row. The Catch-all label (1) marks the mailbox that receives mail sent to addresses that do not exist.
If the password is requested
The administrator's role cannot open cPanel.
Signing in without the password is limited to administrators who can already open the website's cPanel, where cPanel's own Check Email does the same. For other administrators,
Open webmail
opens the webmail sign-in page; enter the full email address and the mailbox password there. A forgotten mailbox password can be replaced with
More > Change the password
on the mailbox row.
The mail server could not sign in.
The new window shows the webmail sign-in page instead, and a message explains that the mailbox password is needed there.
The browser blocked the window.
A message asks to allow pop-ups for the page. Allow them, then click
Open webmail
again.
Catch-all mail
Mail sent to addresses at the domain that do not exist can be kept in the account's own mailbox (
Keep in the catch-all mailbox
). That mailbox is then listed as
The account's own mailbox
with the
Catch-all
label, and
Open webmail
is the way to read its mail.
Additional notes
Each signed-in opening is recorded in the website's notifications as
Webmail opened for
the mailbox.
For administrators without cPanel access,
Open webmail
links to the website's address followed by
/webmail
, such as
https://www.example.com/webmail
, which is the webmail sign-in page and asks for the mailbox password.
For help using the webmail program itself, see the
cPanel documentation
.

title: How Do I Cancel Payment Subscriptions - Orders
content:
An admin can end (cancel) a member's subscription from three places in the admin area. Ending a subscription stops all future payments for it and cancels its unpaid invoices. Each route asks for confirmation first and offers an optional box to record why the subscription is being cancelled.
Transaction History
The member's Payment History, Subscriptions tab
The member's Payment History, Transactions tab
Important:
Ending a subscription from the admin dashboard does not deactivate the member’s account. To completely remove a member so they no longer appear on the website’s front end, the site admin must manually update the member’s status.
Quick edit to modify member status
.
Transaction History
1. In the admin area, go to
Finance » Transaction History
.
2. Search for the member by name or ID in the
Search User Name or ID #
field (1 in the image below), then open the tab that holds the member's invoice:
Payments Received
,
Upcoming Payments
,
Past Due
,
Refunded
or
Stopped
(2).
3. On the invoice's row, hover over
Actions
and click
End Subscription
. The option only appears when the invoice belongs to an active subscription.
4. The
Confirm End Subscription
window opens. Optionally type the reason for the cancellation in the
Reason for cancelling
box (see
Recording a Reason for Cancelling
below), then click
Yes, continue
. Click
No, cancel
to close the window without ending the subscription.
The subscription ends, its unpaid invoices are cancelled, and no further payments are collected for it.
Member's Payment History: "Subscriptions" Tab
Subscriptions can also be ended from the member's own billing page.
1. Go to
My Members » Search Members
and find the member. Hover over
Actions
on the member's row and click
Payment History
.
2. Open the
Subscriptions
tab (1). On the subscription's row, hover over
Actions
(2) and click
End Subscription
(3).
3. The
Cancel Subscription?
window opens. Optionally type the reason in the
Reason for cancelling
box, then click
Yes, continue
. Click
No, cancel
to close the window without ending the subscription.
This is the same window that opens from
Actions » End Subscription
on the
Finance » Search Subscriptions
page. After the subscription ends, its row shows
Ended
, and any reason entered appears as a
Reason:
line in the
History
column.
Member's Payment History: "Transactions" Tab
The member's
Transactions
tab lists the same invoices as
Finance » Transaction History
, filtered to that member. Ending a subscription from here also cancels its unpaid invoices, including an unpaid invoice the system has already created for the next due date (invoices are created 13 days before the due date).
1. Go to
My Members » Search Members
, find the member, hover over
Actions
and click
Payment History
(as in the previous section).
2. Open the
Transactions
tab (1) and the tab that holds the invoice, then hover over
Actions
on the invoice's row (2) and click
End Subscription
.
3. The
Confirm End Subscription
window opens, the same one used on the Transaction History page. Optionally type the reason in the

title: Mandatory Fields For Member Imports
content:
If there are any issues during the import process, it may be caused by one of the following mandatory fields missing.
Name or Company (name, company)
Field Variable: name, company
Include either the "name" or "company" fields. It is also possible to include both.
Name: Combines the first and last name.
Company: Company name
Listing Type (listing_type)
Field Variable: listing_type
Company: Will display the company name in search results
Individual: Displays the individual's name in search results (commonly used for medical or professional directories).
Country Code (country_code)
Field Variable: country_code
Two-letter
country codes
are assigned to each listing. Although only the country_code is strictly required, omitting the zip_code and city fields prevents accurate geo-coding, resulting in an incomplete user experience.
Profession Name (profession_name)
Field Variable: profession_name
Top-level categories associated with each member. This is the minimum required to have members import and display properly.
Subscription & Billing Fields
The following fields are optional for standard member imports. However, when importing existing subscription information, both fields must be provided together.
IMPORTANT:
Subscription and billing fields are optional and are not required for standard member imports. However, if importing subscription information, both
subscription_start_date
and
billing_cycle
must be included together.
Subscription Start Date
Field Variable:
subscription_start_date
Defines the subscription start date for an imported member on a paid membership plan. This field must be provided together with
billing_cycle
.
Accepted date formats:
YYYY-MM-DD (example: 2024-06-15)
YYYYMMDD (example: 20240615)
The website's configured date format (e.g. MM/DD/YYYY or DD/MM/YYYY)
The subscription start date cannot be more than one billing cycle in the past or more than 10 years in the future.
Billing Cycle
Field Variable:
billing_cycle
Defines the billing cycle for the imported member's subscription. This field must be provided together with
subscription_start_date
. The corresponding billing amount configured in the selected Membership Plan must be greater than 0.
Available billing cycles depend on the billing options and prices configured for the selected Membership Plan. The corresponding billing amount for the selected cycle must be greater than 0. For example, if the billing cycle is Monthly, the plan's monthly amount must be greater than 0.

title: Member Profile Analytics
content: The Member Profile Analytics add-on is a click tracking tool, provides insights for admins and members with valuable data such as profile views, clicks to their website, visits to their social media profiles and member posts – all broken down by day, month and year. Use these statistics to show the members how they are analytically benefiting from the website. How To Get This Add-On Websites with the VIP Add-Ons Club automatically have this add-on available: Join The VIP Add-Ons Club Purchase Individually: Member Profile Analytics Add-On Enabling the Add-On Select which membership plan is allowed to view Profile Stats in Finance > Membership Plans : Click Edit to enable the statistics inside the plan settings: Open the Member's Dashboard tab: Scroll down to the option for "Enable Profile Statistics" and select the option that the admin wishes to have: Enable Only For Admin Enable For Member And Admin Disabled Tracked Links Here is a list of the links that the website tracks in the Profile Analytics for members. Member Profile Clicks Profile Visit Phone Number Member Website URL Member Social Media Links Contact Form (Send Message): counted once per submission, whichever option the form uses under What Happens After Form Submitted (Display Success Pop-Up Message, Display Success Alert Message or Redirect to Another Page). Private Chat Messages (first interaction) The option that decides what happens after a contact form is submitted is set per form in Toolbox > Form Manager, by clicking Edit Form Settings on the form. Contact Form submissions are counted with any of the three options in the What Happens After Form Submitted dropdown: Multi-Image Post Clicks Photo Albums Products + External Link (Web URL that will link visitors to more details) Digital Products Properties + External Link (Web URL that will link visitors to more details) Classifieds + External Link (Web URL that will link visitors to more details) Single Image Post Clicks Videos Articles Jobs + External Link (Web URL that will link visitors to more details) Events + External Link (Web URL that will link visitors to more details) Coupons + External Link (Web URL that will link visitors to more details) Audios Discussions Tracking Custom Links A custom link or button added to a member’s listing, such as a booking button that opens an outside booking service, can be tracked too. Its clicks are counted in Profile Analytics under a name chosen for the link. A tracked custom link needs two things in its HTML: the weblink class and a data-click-type attribute holding the name that should appear in the statistics: Copy Book a Visit To add a tracked link to a member’s listing: Go to My Members >> Search Members and open the member. Click Edit Status to open the Quick Edit window, then open the Advanced Options tab (1). Paste the link HTML into Listing Custom FOOTER Code (2), changing the name, address and button text as needed. Click Save Changes . Once the link has been clicked at least once, its name appears as its own column on the member’s Profile Analytics tab (1, 2): Rules for tracked custom links: The link must be saved on the member’s own record , for example in Listing Custom FOOTER Code . A click is only counted when a link with the same data-click-type name is stored on that member. Links added another way, such as through site-wide header or footer code or a widget, are not counted. Names can use letters in any language, numbers, spaces, hyphens and underscores, up to 64 characters. Upper and lower case are treated as the same name. Names containing combining marks (some vowel signs in scripts such as Hindi or Thai) are not accepted. Built-in statistic names cannot be used , such as Website , Phone , Profile Views , Contact Form , Facebook or Instagram , so a custom link never adds to a built-in count. The link address can be anything , including an outside website. A link that is not a full web address (such as #book or /contact-us ) still counts; the click is stored with the address of the profile page it came from. A link without data-click-type is not counted when it points somewhere other than the member’s own website or social media profile fields. Adding the weblink class alone is not enough. Test while logged out. As with profile views, clicks made by the website admin or by the member while logged in are not counted. Notes All page loads are counted. However, views generated by the profile owner while logged in, as well as views by the website admin, are excluded. Clicks won't be tracked if the page content is set to Members-Only Content , or if the member is inactive. Viewing Profile Analytics Admins can monitor profile analytics from the Admin Dashboard and Member Dashboard , including search result views, daily and monthly profile visits, and recorded clicks on social media and website links. Detailed insights are available when profile statistics are enabled for a membership plan. Admin Dashboard The admins will be able to see the amount of views in the member search results, as well as in the member's Profile Analytics tab (opened from Actions » Account Details) if the profile statistics are enabled for the membership plan : Top Views Dashboard Modules The admin dashboard shows three modules for this: Most Viewed Profiles (1), Most Viewed Posts (2) and Visitor Activity (3), each with its own date range. Admin Dashboard Modules Member Dashboard Also the admin can login as any member in that specific Membership Level, on the left sidebar look for Profile Statistics click on it and the profile views per month will be shown: Click on the month to check more detailed stats, it will display the views per day: Social media clicks and website link clicks will also be recorded and added to the report. They will not show up if no clicks have been registered. The Visual Chart can be placed anywhere in the Member Dashboard. For example, adding [widget=Bootstrap Theme - Account - Listing Statistics Chart] per Membership Plan under Member's Dashboard » Custom Dashboard Content » Dashboard Header Content : set the dropdown to Use Text Editor (1), paste the shortcode into the editor (2) and save the plan: Post Views Posts will display how many views they have received in total: Notes Currently, there is no Download Report functionality for this tool; the content is viewable only. This article outlines the format, shows the default variables available in the editor toolbar, lists all supported date options, and explains how to create custom variables. title: Don't Activate All Of The Post Types Prior To the Website Launch
content:
It's completely understandable why many website owners want to launch with all of the post types available to them out of the gate. There are many cool post types to choose from, such as coupons, videos, classifieds, articles, properties, photos, and more. It would seem only logical to make all of these post types available on the website for visitors to see from day one.
The only drawback to activating all post types prior to the launch of the website is that the admin will be painting itself into a corner by having to spend countless hours creating content for all of these post types.
It is better to choose one or two post types that have a ton of member content, which provides an excellent user experience, than to have 10 post types with just a few posts on each. When a visitor clicks on the "coupons" link, they should land on a results page with dozens, if not hundreds, of results. They should be able to search for coupons in San Francisco and get results. If the admin is not delivering this to the public, then the overall experience is poor.
The best practice is to select one or two post types that bring to the industry the most value and do a fantastic job creating content for these. If the site is a Real Estate site, then focus on adding hundreds of properties.  This way, when selling the site to prospects, they will see the value of joining. Potential members don't want to join a site that is in "Beta mode".
So  we recommend starting out on this amazing journey by picking one or two post types for the initial launch!

title: How Search Result Ordering and Distance Sorting Work
content:
Overview
The following explains three search result behaviors that are commonly misunderstood. Each section describes how the system is designed to work and why.
1 — Searching by State, Country, or Region Does Not Produce Distance-Sorted Results
When a visitor searches using a
state, country, province, or county name,
for example, "Texas," "California," or "United Kingdom", the system does not sort results by distance. This is by design.
Distance sorting only activates when the searched location resolves to a
specific point on a map,
such as a
city name
,
zip code
,
postal code
, or
street address
. These location types have a precise latitude and longitude coordinate, which the system uses as the reference point for calculating member distances.
⚠ NOTE — If Distance Sorting Is Not Appearing for City or Zip Code Searches:
If distance is not calculating correctly even when a specific city or zip code is searched, verify that the members in the results have been geocoded. Members without geocoded coordinates will not have distance values and will not sort correctly by distance, regardless of the location searched.
Reference:
How To Geocode Members
2 — Results Are Sorted by Distance from the Searched Location, Not the Visitor's Physical Location
When a visitor searches for a location, the system returns members sorted by their proximity to the
searched location,
not by their proximity to the visitor's current physical position.
For example, a visitor located in Chicago who searches for
"90210"
will see members sorted by their distance from the Beverly Hills area, not from Chicago. This is the intended behavior.
This design allows a visitor to search for businesses or listings near a hotel, a client's office, or any location other than their own. Sorting by the visitor's physical location instead would make location-based searching impractical for any use case where the visitor and the searched area are not in the same place.
3 — Members on Higher-Priority Plans with Service Areas Can Rank Ahead of Geographically Closer Members
When a Membership Plan is configured to allow members to select service areas, those members will appear in search results for their selected service area locations regardless of where they are physically located. If that plan also carries a higher search result priority than another plan on the site, its members will rank above geographically closer members on the lower-priority plan.
Example:
A member physically located in California and New York, as a selected service area. This member will appear in the New York search results. If that member's plan has a higher search priority than a member who is physically located in New York on a lower-tier plan, the California-based member will rank above them.
This behavior is the result of two deliberate configuration choices on the site:
The Membership Plan has
service area
selection enabled.
The Membership Plan has a higher
search result priority
than the plan being outranked.

title: SSL / HTTPS FAQ
content:
Why would I want to secure my site with SSL / HTTPS?
There are many benefits to securing the website with an SSL Certificate / HTTPS:
All payment pages can use their own domain name, rather than the default secured "securemypayment.com" domain name that processes payments by default
Increased confidence from the site's member's and visitors
Potentially higher rankings from Google and other search engines (more information about
Google's use of HTTPS as a ranking signal
here)
Overall increased security for all non-billing information submitted on the site (all billing information is already secured by SSL / HTTPS by default for all sites)
The Admin area of the site is automatically secured with HTTPS
If the admin would like the site to receive all of the benefits above, we offer an
SSL Security Add-On
.
What do I get when I order the SSL / HTTPS Add-On?
When purchasing this service, the admin will receive the following:
One-click configuration and Installation of the SSL certificate on the website
An update to the entire website to enable the use HTTPS for all pages, including the Member Dashboard and Admin area
If the site has the SSL add-on enabled, the system will automatically proceed with SSL installation after a domain name change without prompting the user, ensuring the website has a secure connection
Setup of the billing pages of the site to use their own domain instead of SecureMyPayment.com
An update to the server files to redirect all old HTTP pages to the new HTTPS pages
The SSL Certificate costs $95 per year to keep the SSL / HTTPS security active
.  If the admin provided and installed their own 3rd party SSL Certificate through cPanel, the admin would only need to pay $39 per year for the ongoing maintenance of the service.
How to order the SSL / HTTPS installation service for the site
Order the SSL Security Add-On here:
https://www.brilliantdirectories.com/ssl-secure-website
FAQ
I already purchased an SSL Certificate from another provider, can I use this one instead?
Yes!  The can install their own certificate through cPanel (Admin area >> Developers >> cPanel Dashboard).  Once the admin has successfully installed their own certificate, simply
submit a ticket
requesting that we enable all of the settings for their site to route traffic to HTTPS.
If I provide my own SSL Certificate, does this change the cost in any way?
There is no charge if the admin purchase and install their 3rd party SSL Certificate on theirown.  Please note that we cannot provide support for the self-installation of 3rd party SSL Certificates, but our Support Team is able to assist with any issues encountered with the
SSL Security Add-On
purchased directly through Brilliant Directories.
The domain has CAA records. Does anything need to change for the SSL certificate to install?
A CAA record is an optional DNS record that lists which certificate authorities are allowed to issue SSL certificates for a domain. Most domains have none, and nothing needs to be done. If the domain has any CAA records, one of them must allow
sectigo.com
, the certificate authority behind the certificates installed by the SSL Security Add-On. Without it, the certificate cannot be issued and the site stays on HTTP.
To fix this, add one more CAA record at the domain's DNS host, alongside the existing CAA records. Do not delete the existing ones:
Type:
CAA
Name:
@ (the root domain)
Flag:
0
Tag:
issue
Value:
sectigo.com
Once the record is saved, the certificate is issued automatically during the next nightly certificate check.
Can I use Brilliant Directories Credits for this service?
Yes, credits may be used to purchase this or any full-priced Add-On.

title: What Access Do I Get With My Brilliant Directories License?
content:
One of the most common questions during the pre-sales process is whether Brilliant Directories is a SaaS (Software as a Service) platform or a self-hosted solution.
Many website owners want to know how much control they will have over the functionality, design, and data behind their website. While many SaaS platforms limit access to core functionality and server-level settings, Brilliant Directories provides significantly more flexibility than a traditional SaaS solution.
Although Brilliant Directories is delivered as a managed SaaS platform, website owners receive extensive access to their website's data, hosting environment, and customizable functionality.
This article highlights four key areas where Brilliant Directories provides that flexibility.
1. Access to the Website Database
Every Brilliant Directories license includes full access to the website's database.
The database stores website content, member information, custom widgets, design settings, and other data unique to the website. As members interact with the website—such as updating profiles, publishing posts, uploading media, or sending messages—that information is stored within the database.
Database access allows developers to:
Read stored data
Create custom integrations
Build APIs
Insert, update, or delete records
Interact directly with website data using standard database tools
2. Access to the cPanel Account
Each website includes direct access to its cPanel account.
This provides access to many of the same hosting tools typically available with traditional self-hosted environments, including:
Email account management
DNS Zone Editor (A, CNAME, MX, TXT, SPF, etc.)
Subdomain creation
Additional database users
Website backups
Other cPanel management tools
This level of access gives website owners greater control over their hosting configuration while still benefiting from a managed platform.
3. Access to Website Widgets
Brilliant Directories provides access to nearly all of the website's widget code.
By enabling
Show Widgets
, administrators can inspect and edit the widgets used throughout the website. For example, editing the
Member Results
widget allows developers to customize both the appearance and functionality of member search results.
Most widgets support custom development using:
PHP
HTML
CSS
JavaScript
A small portion of the core software remains protected to ensure platform stability, security, and compatibility across future updates.
4. Lifetime Software Updates
Every active Brilliant Directories license includes ongoing software and security updates.
New features, improvements, bug fixes, and security enhancements are continuously released without requiring manual upgrades or plugin maintenance.
This allows websites to remain current with the latest platform improvements while avoiding the maintenance commonly associated with self-hosted software.

title: How To Enable Remote MySQL Access
content:
Advanced users with experience in databases, programming, and security may want to enable remote MySQL access for reasons such as faster development, easier external access, or other development-related tasks. However, it’s important to understand the risks associated with enabling this feature.
Allowing remote access to the database bypasses several built-in security layers that are designed to protect the site and its data. While it may offer flexibility, it also introduces potential vulnerabilities. Some of the common issues reported in the past from enabling remote access include:
Accidental access or misuse by third parties using the authorized computer (e.g., family members or colleagues)
Running incorrect SQL commands with full privileges (e.g., using DELETE, UPDATE, or REPLACE commands improperly)
Mistakes in queries that unintentionally affect large portions of the database (e.g., updating multiple rows without using unique identifiers)
Data corruption during long transactions if the connection is interrupted (due to local network issues, ISP outages, power loss, etc.)
Conflicts during simultaneous access (e.g., editing tables while maintenance or optimization tasks are in progress)
Man-in-the-middle attacks that intercept sensitive data, including passwords
Malware or viruses affecting the database through vulnerable third-party software or infected systems
Unauthorized access or manipulation of customer data, accounts, or credentials
Brilliant Directories is not responsible for any issues that arise from enabling remote MySQL access, including database corruption, loss, or unauthorized changes. If remote access is still preferred, it is strongly recommended to make regular backups to mitigate potential data loss.
Important Notes
Before enabling remote access, contact the Brilliant Directories support team with the static IP address that will be connecting. The IP must be whitelisted to allow full access. Please note that Brilliant Directories does not offer database support or assistance with any issues that may result from enabling remote access.

title: Service Areas in Australia - City vs Suburb
content:
The Service Areas functionality of the software, just like all other location-based features of the platform, is powered by Google Maps.
Google Maps treats Australian 'suburbs' the same as 'cities' in the rest of the world. Australian "cities" (Brisbane, for example), are treated as both a suburb and what they call a "Colloquial Area" (IE an unofficial name for a region that contains multiple suburbs).
For example, if 'Brisbane' is added as a service area, Google Maps treats it as a "city":
And when searching for "Banksia Beach" (a suburb in Brisbane), it will also treat this as a "city":
Smaller regions within cities (North Brisbane, for example), are not recognized by Google Maps.
When searching for a region like this, Google Maps will simply return results for 'Brisbane' by default:
Since Google Maps treats Australian suburbs and cities this way, the recommended way to allow members to add additional Service Areas is to allow them to add "suburbs" (Suggestion: Change to "(which are referred to as 'city' in both the Brilliant Directories system and Google Maps).
To allow members to add suburbs as service areas, sset the 'Maximum Number of Locations' to a value greater than 0 and select "City" as an option in the "Location Types Member Can Select"  in the Membership Plan Settings:

title: Can I Get A Backup Of My Website Data?
content:
Yes. Our servers automatically backup all the unique data of your website (including uploaded files and images) once a month and once every morning.
Our servers also automatically backup your website's databases (which is the element most likely to require to be restored if something should go wrong) every morning, and a copy of the databases as they were each morning over the last 14 days is kept on file.
While a site can be restored from a backup made on our server in the past, it is a process that requires the time of a developer on our staff to complete.
Downloading Your Own Backup
While not required (as we keep backups of your full website automatically as mentioned above), some may wish to perform their own backups as well.
The items that would needed to complete a full restoration of your site are the
uploaded files in your file structure
and your
databases
.
To create a backup of these items, first login to cPanel from the Admin area of your website, and click on the "Backup" item in cPanel:
You will then see a screen that looks something like this:
To download a copy of all of the uploaded files in your Home Directory, click on the "Home Directory" button in the "Download a Home Directory Backup" section.
You can then restore a Home Directory backup using the "Restore a Home Directory Backup" section.
To download a copy of each database, click on the names of the Databases in the "Download a MySQL Database Backup" section.
You can then restore a database from backup by using the "Restore a MySQL Database Backup" section.

title: 301 Redirects
content:
A 301 redirect permanently sends visitors and search engines from an old address on the website to a new one. The
301 Redirect Rules
page lists every redirect on the website and is where redirects are added, edited, tested and deleted.
When member profile details are updated, such as changes to URL structure, business name, or address, the system automatically creates redirects. This ensures that existing links continue to resolve correctly and point to the updated profile.
Opening the 301 Redirect Rules Page
Go to
Developer Hub
.
On the
301 Redirect Rules
card, click
Manage Redirects
.
The 301 Redirect Rules Page
The page shows each redirect as one row: the old address (Source URL) in green, with the new address (Destination URL) beneath it, followed by the redirect's
Type
and the date it was last
Updated
.
Import CSV
: adds many redirects at once from a CSV file. See
Import 301 Redirects via CSV file
.
New Redirect Rule
: opens a drawer for adding one or more redirects.
Search
: finds redirects by text. The menu beside the search box limits the search to
All fields
,
Source URL
,
Destination URL
,
Admin notes
or
ID
. A full address on the website can be pasted in; it is searched by its path.
Date updated
: shows only redirects updated on one day or within a date range.
All types
: shows only redirects of the selected types, EG
Member Profile
redirects created automatically, or redirects added by an admin.
All redirects / Broken redirects
: switches to the list of broken redirects (see below).
Export CSV
: downloads the redirects currently shown, with the active search and filters applied, in the same columns the CSV import uses.
Show or hide columns
: chooses which columns appear in the table.
Actions
: the menu for a single redirect.
Hovering over a row shows copy buttons beside the Source URL and the Destination URL. Clicking anywhere else on a row opens that redirect for editing.
Tables show 25 rows per page by default. The
Rows per page
menu below the table switches between 10, 25, 50 and 100 rows, and the browser remembers the last size picked.
Adding 301 Redirects
Click
New Redirect Rule
. The New Redirect Rule drawer opens.
In
Source URL
, enter the old address as a path on the website, without the domain or a leading slash. EG
about/contact
.
In
Destination URL
, enter the new address: a path on the website (EG
about/contact-us
) or a full address on another website (EG
https://example.com
). To send visitors to the homepage, enter a single
/
.
To add more redirects at the same time, click
Add Another Redirect
and fill in the new row. The
X
at the end of a row removes it.
Click
Save
. A confirmation appears and the new redirects are added to the top of the list.
The reminder at the top of the drawer: the Source is a path on the website, the Destination is a path on the website or a full address, and a single
/
as Destination redirects to the homepage.
Source URL
: the old address.
Destination URL
: the new address.
Add Another Redirect
: adds another Source and Destination row.
Cancel
and
Save
. If anything was typed, Cancel asks before discarding it.
The drawer checks each row before saving and shows the problem under the field. EG a Source URL that starts with
http
,
www.
or a slash is refused with a request to enter the path only, a Destination that matches its Source is refused, and quotes, angle brackets and backslashes are not accepted in either field.
Note.
The Source URL must be an address on this website. The Destination URL can be a page on this website or an address on any other website.
Editing a Redirect
Click a row, or choose
Edit
from its
Actions
menu, to open the Edit Redirect drawer.
Source URL
: the old address, with a button to copy its full address.
Destination URL
: the new address, with a copy button. A single
/
redirects to the homepage.
Admin notes
: an internal note about the purpose of the redirect. Notes are searchable and appear under the rule in the list.
Test Redirect
: opens the Source URL in a new browser tab to confirm it lands on the Destination.
Cancel
and
Save
.
The drawer also shows the redirect's type and when it was last updated.
The Actions Menu
Edit
: opens the Edit Redirect drawer.
Copy Source URL
and
Copy Destination URL
: copy the full address.
Test Redirect
: opens the Source URL in a new browser tab.
Delete Redirect Rule
: asks for confirmation, then deletes the redirect. Its Source URL stops redirecting and the deletion cannot be undone.
Deleting Several Redirects
Tick the checkbox beside each redirect to delete. The checkbox in the header selects every row on the page, and
Select All
in the bar that appears selects every matching redirect.
In the bar above the table, choose
Delete
from
Select Action
and click
Apply
.
When two or more redirects are selected, type the number of selected redirects to confirm, then click
Delete Records
.
The bulk action bar: the number selected,
Cancel
,
Select Action
and
Apply
.
The confirmation field.
Delete Records
stays disabled until the number is typed.
Finding Broken Redirects
Choose
Broken redirects
in the filter menu to list only redirects whose destination is a page that does not exist on the website. Chains of redirects are followed to their last step, so a redirect that points at another redirect is broken when the end of the chain is missing. Destinations on other websites are not checked.
The
Broken redirects
filter.
The note explaining what counts as broken.
Review the list and either edit each broken redirect to point at a page that exists, or delete the redirects that are no longer needed. Typing in the search box switches the list back to
All redirects
.
Importing 301 Redirects
For bulk redirect creation, a CSV file listing Source URLs and their Destination URLs can be imported with
Import CSV
.
>>
Import 301 Redirects via CSV file

title: Google Maps API: Features, Functions, and Key Considerations
content:
The Google Maps API plays an essential role in powering location-based features on Brilliant Directories websites. By integrating directly with Google’s mapping technology, it provides members and visitors with accurate, flexible, and dynamic location search options that go far beyond simple address lookups.
From handling multiple spellings and landmarks to displaying real-time map results and offering advanced geocoding controls, the API brings significant functionality to any directory site.
At the same time, there are important requirements and limitations to be aware of, ensuring site owners understand both the advantages and the boundaries of this integration.
Benefits
The API offers a range of benefits for website owners who connect their site to Google Maps, making it easier for members to find locations and access relevant map-based features.
One of the powerful parts of BD, as users generate content, or join from different locations; all the profiles pages and search result pages are all automatically created and dynamically populated.
Location Flexibility
Search for any type of location, including street addresses:
Landmarks
Search for landmarks:
Location Spelling
Search using different spellings of the same location (Montreal vs. Montréal), even using accents and other special characters:
Robust handling of misspellings / imperfect matches:
Map Display
Search results are displayed on a Google Map:
Additional Information:
»
Google Map Search Results Add-On
Geocoding
New manual geocoding module gives the website administrator full control over correcting the latitude and longitude assigned to each member:
Additional Information:
»
How To Geocode Members
Latitude and Longitude
Members will use Google Maps when filling out their profile information to provide an exact latitude and longitude for their listing (even if Google Maps does not recognize their written address):
Additional Benefits
Location auto-suggestions are lightning-fast, as they are delivered directly from the Google Maps API.
Location data is pulled in real time from the Google Map's location database, meaning your locations always use the latest location data available from Google.
Location searches are automatically tailored to your users' likely behavior. For example, if a user is located in India, the system will read their IP address and provide them with location suggestions that are most likely to fit their needs.
Gain unprecedented control over how searches behave on your site.  For example, choose between having bounding-box search results or radius search results for every type of location search. For example, if a user searches for "90210", you will be able to restrict results to the northeast and southwest points of that specific zip code, providing incredible local results, OR choose to provide results within a set radius from the center of that zip code.
Requirements
You must provide your own (free) Google Maps Javascript API key.
Getting an API key:
Google Maps Javascript API Key
Limitations
The auto-suggest module when users are entering location information has limited customization options. Since it is directly returning results from the Google Maps API, the suggestions provided are not editable.
Using the mouse wheel to zoom in and out on the map is not available for the integration.
For Kosovo, searches cannot be performed using the “bounds” search type. Only radius-based searches are supported. This limitation occurs because locations within Kosovo are not consistently recognized as cities or other locality types in the underlying data, preventing bounds-based queries from returning results. This limitation is due to how Google Maps classifies locations in the region.
Location search results cannot be strictly limited to specific geographic regions. Since the Google Maps API is built to return results intuitively, it will know where a user is located, and likely matches to their search are given precedence. If the search is ambiguous and could refer to several different locations, it will provide additional location suggestions, which CAN be controlled through your Admin settings.  However, the initial search a user enters may not provide results within your preferred countries if Google believes the search is most likely for a location outside of your preferred countries.
Most websites and applications may use the Google Maps API free of charge. However, if you consistently generate a high amount of traffic, you may be required to pay for additional usage of the API. If your site or application generates 25,000 or more map loads each day for more than 90 consecutive days, Google may contact you to upgrade from the free API. But don’t worry!  If you go over the limits, Google will not immediately shut off your API access or display error messages on your site.  And if you are generating more than 25,000 map loads per day consistently, your website is already a major success!
Places (New) API
To ensure more accurate searches, websites that use the Google Maps “
PLACES (NEW) API
”  require visitors to select an option from the dropdown suggestions. In the past, users could type free-form text and attempt a search without confirming a recognized location, which often led to incomplete or invalid results. With this update in place, the search will not continue unless a valid suggestion has been chosen, making the process clearer and more reliable for everyone using the site.
When a visitor tries to search without selecting a suggestion, a small banner appears at the top of the results with the message “
REQUIRED: Select Location
”.
Next to it, an exclamation point icon provides additional context when hovered over, displaying “
Please select a location from the suggestions dropdown to continue.
”
This approach makes it immediately obvious what action is needed and reduces confusion or errors during the search process.
Text Labels
The banner message and tooltip are both standard text labels in the system. This means they can be fully customized, translated, or removed from the admin area if desired. Editing these labels allows administrators to match the exact language or terminology used on their website.
Google Suggestion Require Text
Google Suggestion Require Text Popover
While removing the text is possible, it is not recommended since doing so would reduce clarity for visitors and may lead to repeated search errors. The default labels provide helpful guidance and are intended to create a smoother, more user-friendly search experience.

Default on-page SEO is pre-configured for all pages of the site. Advanced configuration is available for the SEO settings of dynamic pages, primarily search results pages and member profile pages, for administrators who wish to customize them further.
CAUTION:
These are
dynamic pages

Identifying an SEO Template

or

SEO Settings
tab contains the editable fields.
Editing SEO Meta Tags

Page Meta Title
,
Meta Description
, and
Meta Keywords
fields as needed.
Click
Save SEO Template
to apply the changes.
NOTE:
Default pages already include optimized SEO information, including default SEO variables. Existing values should be reviewed before being overwritten.
Dynamic Page Types
Dynamic SEO templates correspond to different combinations of category and location. Commonly edited templates include:
Template
Path pattern
Profile page
%filename%
Top-level category search results
%profession%
Sub-level category search results
%service_name%
,
%sub_category_name%
,
%sub_sub_category_name%

Variable
Description

Website
>
Website Settings

Variables

Website

Variables
Formatting Variables
Pluralizing:
Surround the variable with double percent signs —
%%profession%%

Capitalizing:

%Profession%

title: Content » SEO Templates
content:
Overview
SEO settings, variables, and related data can be managed across both dynamic and static features of the site. All SEO settings are optimized by default, but the system supports customization at multiple levels to adapt SEO behavior to specific needs.
Not all SEO variables apply to every page, some are only available on specific page types (e.g., content pages, category pages, profile pages), since availability depends on the page type. Because of this, tracking which variables apply to which pages, membership features, content pages, or profiles can be complex. This article outlines the three levels at which SEO can be managed.
The Three Levels of SEO Management
NOTE — Priority order:
When settings overlap, more specific levels override more general ones.
Member SEO
settings take priority over
Page SEO
settings, and
Page SEO
settings take priority over the
SEO Template
.
1st Level: SEO Template
The broadest level. Changes made here affect the overall SEO template for all members, categories, pages, and other dynamic content system-wide.
Further detail is available in the "
How To Edit The SEO Settings Of Dynamic (Search Results) Pages
" article.
2nd Level: SEO Pages (Web Page SEO Settings)
Affects the SEO of a specific static page and its contents.
Web Page SEO settings have higher priority than the SEO Template.
Further detail is available in the "
How To Edit The SEO & Social Media Elements Of A Static Web Page
" article.
3rd Level: SEO Members (Member SEO Settings)
Affects only the specified member — for example, how a profile page displays, which SEO settings are enabled or disabled for that profile, and the member's custom URL.
Member SEO settings have higher priority than both Page SEO and the SEO Template.
To access these settings:
Navigate to
My Members
>
Search Members
.
Locate the member.
Hover over
Actions
, then click
Quick Edit
.
Further detail is available in the "
How To Edit The SEO & Social Media Elements Of A Member's Profile Page
" article.
Troubleshooting: Changes Not Taking Effect
If changes do not appear to work correctly after being made, clearing the site cache is recommended:
How To Refresh The Cache Of The Website
SEO Variable Syntax
CRITICAL:
All SEO variables must be wrapped in percent signs. A variable written as
%variable_name%
is read correctly by the system. The same text written as
variable_name
, without the percent signs, is treated as plain text and will not function as a variable.
Percent signs are reserved exclusively for SEO variables. Custom text that is not a variable should not be wrapped in percent signs.
Related Reading
Additional detail on available variables is covered in the "
Understanding SEO Variables
" article.

title: Editing The SEO Of Member Search Results Pages
content:
What are Member Search Results Pages?
Member Search Results pages are what a visitor to the website will see when they search for members on the site. These searches can be done by keyword, category, and/or location.
For example, to see a search results page that contains all of the searchable members of the site, go the /search_results page (EG:
http://www.demobootstrap.com/search_results
).
"Pretty" URLs and "Not So Pretty" URLs
When a visitor to the site searches for a member by keyword, category, and/or location, the search results page will have a "Not So Pretty" URL.  It will look something like this (this is a search for members in the category "Restaurants" in the location "Las Vegas, Nevada"):
http://www.demobootstrap.com/search_results?sid=2&tid=&location_value=Las+Vegas%2C+NV%2C+United+States&city=Las+Vegas&county_sn=Clark+County&adm_lvl_1_sn=NV&country_sn=US&location_type=locality&swlat=36.1296229&nelat=36.380623&swlng=-115.414625&nelng=-115.062072&lat=36.1699412&lng=-115.13982959999998&faddress=Las+Vegas%2C+NV%2C+USA&place_id=ChIJ0X31pIK3voARo3mz1ebVzDo
For comparison sake, a search on Google.com for "Restaurants in Las Vegas, Nevada", can look something like this:
https://www.google.com/?gws_rd=ssl#q=restaurants+in+las+vegas,+nevada&tbs=bkv:p,bkt:b,sbd:1,cdr:1,cd_min:1800,cd_max:1899&tbm=bks
As we can see, the URL that the visitor sees in both cases is "Not So Pretty".

However, a "Not So Pretty" URL like this is not as desirable for sharing on social media, sending in an email, or for SEO purposes.
The system automatically creates a "Pretty" URL version of member search results pages for all of the reasons listed above.
We created the advanced setting:
"Enable All Location Features For "Pretty URL" Search Results Pages (Additional Google Maps API Cost)"

Pretty

title: Google Sitemap Generator
content:
Overview
The Google Sitemap Generator add-on greatly improves the directory website’s SEO by creating XML sitemaps. These sitemaps help search engines like Google and Bing better index all of the pages that make up the membership website.
NOTE: Keep in mind that submitting your sitemap to the Google Console doesn't ensure that all pages will get indexed by Google. This article explains more about this:
https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/sitemaps/overview
Not all pages in a sitemap have value to Google. Learn more about thin pages here:
https://developers.google.com/search/docs/advanced/guidelines/thin-content
This add-on will update the sitemap dynamically so search engines are automatically notified when the site has been updated.
How To Get This Add-On
Websites with the VIP Add-Ons Club automatically have this add-on available:
Join The VIP Add-Ons Club
Purchase Individually:
Google Sitemap Generator Add-On
Enabling the Add-On
For most users, following the instructions in this section will accomplish exactly what they need - create a new XML sitemap that can be submitted to search engines so they are aware of all of the pages of the website.
If the admin wants to have more granular control over each individual sitemap that is created or updated, please see the section below called "Advanced Sitemap Generation". Below are the steps to find the sitemap generator settings.
Create Sitemap File
Login to the Admin area of the site for the Sitemap Generator settings.
Navigate to
Toolbox
»
Sitemap Generator
Click on the "
Generate
Sitemap
" button:
The admin will see a message that a sitemap is being generated.  Depending on the size of the site and how many members it might have, this could take anywhere from a few seconds to a few minutes to complete.  Please do not navigate away from this page while it is processing.
Once it is complete, the admin will see a success message.  Click on "Close Window":
The admin will now see a link for the XML sitemap that they can submit to search engines.  They can copy this link directly or click on the "Copy to Clipboard" button to copy the link to the clipboard:
The admin can now create a cron job that automatically updates the sitemap of the site:
The admin will have these different options for how often the sitemap is automatically regenerated: every day, every 7 days, or every 30 days:
Submit the sitemap to the search engines
Here are instructions to submit the XML sitemap link to 2 of the most popular search engines:
Submit a sitemap to Google
Submit a sitemap to Bing
Advanced Sitemap Generation
If the admin would like to have more control of which kinds of URLs are included in the XML sitemap, we have some advanced controls available.  In order to understand how to best use these, it is first necessary to understand a bit about how the Sitemap Generator works.
How the Sitemap Generator works:
The Sitemap Generator will create a record of every page of the website in a formatted XML sitemap file that can be submitted to search engines.
The Sitemap Generator does this by creating separate XML files based on each of the
SEO Templates
(note: there are a few SEO Templates that no sitemap file is created for, such as the payment pages for example), and a separate file for all of the
Static Pages
on the website, this last one will also include any
member category
or
post category page that has been converted into a static page.
However, search engines will generally only accept a single XML sitemap file to be submitted for a website. Since a separate XML file is created for each SEO Template and a separate one for static pages, a total of 40+ separate sitemap files will be created.  In order to submit all of these individual XMLS sitemap files, the Sitemap Generator also creates what is called a "Sitemap Index File", which is the actual file that is submitted to search engines.
Exclusions to the Sitemap:
Any Web Page with the "Apply NoIndex, NoFollow" setting checked is not included in the sitemap:
If "Add "NOFOLLOW" to Member Web Links?" and "Hide Member Profile from Search Engines?" are set to "YES" within the Membership Plans:
If the
Noindex Review & Connect Pages
setting is turned on (Settings >> Advanced Settings >> URL Rules tab), the members' write-a-review pages and connect (contact) pages are left out of the sitemap, including pages that use a custom URL for either one. Those pages already tell search engines not to index them, so leaving them out keeps the sitemap limited to pages that can appear in search results.
The change takes effect the next time the sitemap is generated. In Advanced Controls, the Write a Review and Contact Form SEO Templates are still listed, but with no Sitemap File.
If the site has the Hidden Member Profiles add-on (
click here for add-on information
), it will hide all Non-Searchable members:
Sitemap Index File
As of the writing of this article, search engines generally allow up to 50,000 URLs to be in a single sitemap file.  However, since many sites on the platform can have many more than 50,000 URLs, the Sitemap Generator will create several smaller XML sitemap files and one master file called a "sitemap index file".
The sitemap index file is a single XML file that contains links to all of the smaller sitemap files which contain the URLs of the website.  When submitting the sitemap to search engines, the admin will submit the sitemap index file. For more information, please see this
article from Google on the topic
.
Advanced Controls
To display all of the individual sitemap files that can be generated and added to the Sitemap Index File, click on the "Advanced Controls" button:
Clicking this button will display a list of all of the SEO Templates that sitemap files can be generated from, along with some additional information and actions:
Generate or Update a Sitemap File for a Single SEO Template
To generate or update the sitemap file for a single SEO Template, locate the SEO Template the admin would like to generate for, and click on the "Add / Update Sitemap" button next to it:
After doing this, the system will generate a sitemap file for just that SEO Template and add the updated sitemap file to the Sitemap Index File.  A link to the sitemap file for that SEO Template will then appear:
Generate or Update Sitemap Files for Multiple Selected SEO Templates
To generate or update the sitemap files for more that one SEO Template at a time, simply check the box next to all of the chosen SEO Templates:
After checking these boxes, scroll down and click on the "Bulk Add / Update" button:
After the system finishes processing the request, the admin will then see a link for each file here:
Doing this will update the sitemaps for those SEO templates and update the Sitemap Index File with the latest URLs as well.
Once the admin has generated or updated the sitemap files of their choice, they can submit the sitemap file shown at the top of the page to search engines:
SEO Templates That Will Generate More Than 50,000 URLs
As mentioned above, search engines will generally accept a sitemap file that has a maximum of 50,000 URLs per file.  For larger sites, there can be more than 50,000 URLs generated for a single SEO Template.  If this is the case, the system will generate a file for the first 50,000 URLs, and then continue generating another file for the next 50,000 URLs, and so on.
If this happens for an SEO Template, the admin will see multiple sitemap file links for the SEO Template (Sitemap File 1, Sitemap File 2, etc), instead of seeing a single sitemap file link as shown below:
All of these additional sitemap files are automatically added to the Sitemap Index File as soon as they are generated.

content:
The
Domain Manager
brings together the website address, domain connection, SSL certificate, email authentication, DNS records, and hosting information. Open
Settings > Domain Manager
to check the site's status or connect a different address.
Example: a free website address
Example on a free directoryup.com address: the tab row (1) shows
Domain
,
SSL
,
Cloudflare
,
Diagnostics
,
Speed
, and
Usage
. Additional tabs appear when a custom domain and its services are available.
Example: a custom domain with Brilliant Directories DNS

selfautomated.com
