title: The Email Variables Used with the  Leads Module
content: The Leads Module includes several variables that can be used when creating or customizing lead-related email templates. These variables allow you to automatically insert lead information, member details, login links, and other dynamic content into your emails. The following variables power the Basic Lead Module, and can be used when creating custom lead emails. Important note: When using lead variables, make sure to enter them exactly as shown below. Some variables require a single percentage sign (%variable%), while others require three percentage signs (%%%variable%%%). Using the wrong format may prevent the variable from displaying correctly in the email. For more information about variables, please see: » Understanding Variables Variables Member Access Variables These variables help members quickly access their account or view a lead. %member_login_link% Automatically logs the member into their dashboard without requiring them to enter their username or password. %member_lead_match_link% Takes the member directly to the specific lead associated with the email without requiring them to log in manually. This is the recommended variable for lead notification emails because it provides the fastest way for members to review, accept, or purchase leads. Lead Information Variables These variables display information submitted by the website visitor when creating the lead. %%%details%%% Displays the lead information fields configured in the Get Matched form. The information displayed by this variable can be customized by editing the fields included in the Get Matched form. %%%lead_id%%% Displays the Lead ID number. This is commonly used in administrative notifications to make it easier to locate a specific lead within the admin area. %%%lead_name%%% Displays the name of the website visitor who submitted the lead. %%%lead_email%%% Displays the email address entered by the website visitor. Important: This variable will display the visitor's email address even if the lead is configured as a Preview Lead. For this reason, it is typically only used in emails sent to the website visitor and is not included in member lead notification emails by default. %%%lead_phone%%% Displays the phone number entered by the website visitor. Like the lead email variable, this will display the phone number regardless of whether the lead is set to Preview or Complete. %%%lead_location%%% Displays the location entered by the website visitor when submitting the lead. Member Information Variables These variables display information about the member who was matched with the lead. %%%full_name%%% Displays the member's name. For Individual Accounts, the member's first and last name will be displayed. For Company Accounts, the company name will be displayed. %%%user_id%%% Displays the member's User ID number. %%%location%%% Displays the location of the matched member. Website Variables %%%website_name%%% Displays the website name. This variable is commonly used in email subject lines and email signatures to reinforce branding and recognition. Security Token Variables These variables return secure system tokens that can be used when creating custom links or integrations. %token% Displays the secure token associated with the lead. %user_token% Displays the secure token associated with the matched member. Custom Login Link Example The following link automatically logs the member into their account and takes them directly to the lead details page: Login to your account to view this lead Additional Information: » How to Edit Email Templates » Emails » Email Templates » New Email Template

title: How to Turn The Brilliant Directories Directory Website into a Mobile Application for Apple & Android
content:
The video below shows how to convert a Brilliant Directories website into a mobile app in less than 5 minutes using third-party, no-code app building platforms. The website users will have the same familiar experience on the mobile app as they do on the main Brilliant Directories website. This approach displays your live website inside an app using WebView technology.
Starting with a mobile-friendly website saves time and makes the entire app-building process easier.
Video Note
The app builder shown in the video (Como) was acquired and later shut down. The same WebView-based approach shown in the video still applies to modern no-code app builders.
No-Code Method
The easiest way to turn a Brilliant Directories website into a mobile app is by using a no-code app builder that supports loading your website inside the app using a WebView.
No-code app builders are third-party services and operate independently from Brilliant Directories. They have their own plans, pricing, and publishing requirements.
How It Works
Your live Brilliant Directories site is displayed inside a mobile app shell. Your homepage loads first, and all navigation, logins, forms, listings, and features work exactly as they do on your website. No content needs to be rebuilt and no code is required.
Set your website URL as the app’s homepage, or
Add your website as a navigation item within the app
Some app builders may show optional menus, screens, or layout tools in their interface. These are not required when using your website as the primary WebView.
Limitations
This method creates a WebView-based app (a website inside an app). It does not generate a fully custom native mobile app interface.
Popular No-Code App Builders
Appy Pie
Convert your website into Android and iOS apps by entering your site URL.
https://www.appypie.com/convert-website-to-mobile-apps
BuildFire
Embed your website inside the app using the WebView plugin.
https://buildfire.com/plugin/webview-2/
GoodBarber
Display your website in the app using a URL-based WebView section.
https://www.goodbarber.com/help/web-view-sections-r33/url-section-web-view-a27/
NOTE:
Any no-code app builder that supports loading a website URL as the app homepage or as a navigation item follows this same general methodology.
Advanced Option
A fully native mobile app can be built using custom development and the Brilliant Directories API. This approach requires development resources and is outside the scope of no-code app builders.
Developer Accounts
Publishing a mobile app requires developer accounts with the app stores. These accounts, review processes, and any associated fees are managed directly between you and the app store provider.
Apple
An Apple Developer account is required to publish apps to the App Store.
https://developer.apple.com/support/compare-memberships
Google
A Google Developer account is required to publish apps to Google Play.
http://developer.android.com/distribute/googleplay/start.html

title: How To Manually Bill A Member / Create A Subscription For A Member
content:
At any moment, the site can create a subscription (recurring or one-time payment) for a member of the directory. Keep in mind that when someone signs up from the /join page, the system will create the subscription automatically.
However, sometimes the owner wants to change the subscription's amount or create a new subscription.
This is also very beneficial if the site is taking external payments (bank transfers, checks, etc.,) instead of accepting direct payments on the site.
Create a "New Order"
Log in to the admin area and navigate to Members » Search Members. Locate the member and click on Actions » Payment History:
At the top right, click on the "New Order" button:
Fill out the new order form with the subscription details:
Membership Plan:
Select the membership plan of this specific order.
Billing Cycle:
Monthly, Quarterly, Semi-Yearly, and Yearly. (this will depend on the configuration set up in the membership plan)
Price Override:
Type the new amount for this specific order. Leave this option blank if the membership plan doesn't need to be overridden. Enter a
price greater than 0.
Start Billing On:
By default, the system will show today's date. However, it can be modified to any date in the future.
Admin Notes
: Add notes for the internal team (See example below).
Create Order
: The system will save and create the order.
Confirm the order by clicking on the "Submit Order" button:
The page should load automatically and the message "New Order Created" will appear with an order summary:
Card on File
If the member had a credit card on file and the date selected was today, then the system should collect the payment.
To verify if the money was taken successfully, click on the "Transactions" tab and make sure the status of the order says "Paid".
This payment can also be verified under Finance » Transaction History:
If the charge couldn't be attempted or there was no card registered to begin with, this means that the credit on file needs to be updated. The unpaid invoice will appear in the "Past Due" tab.
When the member updates the credit card on file, the unpaid invoice can be attempted manually. There is no need to create a new order.
Manually Collect Payment
To attempt the payment manually, click on Actions » Collect Payment:

title: Embed Conversion Tracking and Affiliate Tracking Codes On Sign Up Pages
content:
There are many 3rd party tools that require placing a tracking code on "success pages" in order to track sales, sign-ups, conversions, and more.
With Brilliant Directories, it is possible to place tracking code widget for the "success pages" into each membership plan or in a specific widget that will apply to all membership plans.
Membership Plans Method
There is a setting on each membership plan where the widget with the code can be placed.
It can be found under
Finance
>>
Membership Plans
>> find the membership where the code needs to be added and click on
Edit
.
Navigate to the "
Sign-Ups & Upgrades
" tab and scroll down to "
Sign Ups / Upgrade Conversion Tracking Code
" and select the preferred widget:
*This allows the activation of an additional Tracking Code Widget that will work alongside the default
Bootstrap Theme - Conversion Tracking Codes
,
which will always remain active.
Conversion Tracking Codes Widget and Available Variables to Utilize
Navigate Toolbox >> Widget Manager >>
Bootstrap Theme - Conversion Tracking Codes
An example conversion tracking to add could look like the following:
fbq('track', 'Purchase', {currency: "AUD", value: <?php echo $conversion_tracking['amount']; ?>});
This code should be added below the following comment within this widget:
When adding this code, please make sure to wrap it around the <script> tag, as shown below:
<script type="text/javascript">fbq('track', 'Purchase', {currency: "AUD", value: <?php echo $conversion_tracking['amount']; ?>});</script>
The end result would look like the following:
Some common variables that affiliates and other trackers want to be included in the pixel tracking code are the order amount and order or member ID, etc. These are the variables available with Brilliant Directories:
COMMON VARIABLES AFFILIATE TRACKERS USE:
FIRST PAYMENT AMOUNT
= <?php echo $conversion_tracking['amount']; ?>
RECURRING PAYMENT AMOUNT
= <?php echo $conversion_tracking['recurring_amount']; ?>
ORDER ID / MEMBER ID
= <?php echo $conversion_tracking['user_id']; ?>
COUPON CODE
= <?php echo $conversion_tracking['coupon_code']; ?>
PRODUCT NAME
= <?php echo $conversion_tracking['product_name']; ?>
PRODUCT TYPE
= <?php echo $conversion_tracking['product_type']; ?>
FREE TRIAL
= <?php echo $conversion_tracking['free_trial']; ?>
FREE TRIAL DAYS
= <?php echo $conversion_tracking['free_trial_period']; ?>
FIRST BILL DATE
= <?php echo $conversion_tracking['first_bill_date']; ?>
ADVANCED VARIABLES AFFILIATE TRACKERS USE:
$conversion_tracking['invoice']['variable'];    (Invoice Variables from the tblinvoices table)
$conversion_tracking['product']['variable'];   (Member Subscription Variables from the tblhosting table)
IMPORTANT NOTE:
This widget is where the tracking code for affiliate programs, analytics, and more can be placed.
This widget only loads on pages after a member sign-ups or upgrades, to track successful sign-ups.
Alternative Method: Adding Conversion Tracking to Pop-Up Success Messages
If the conversion action does not load a separate success page (e.g., a pop-up message confirms success on the same page), the conversion tracking code can also be placed in the text label that appears after a successful action. This can be done by navigating the Text Label for the post-success message and embedding the tracking code there.
For this example, let's add a Google Ads conversion tracking setup for a newsletter subscriber pop-up. To accomplish this, first, navigate Toolbox >> Widget Manager and create a new widget:
Name the widget, add the tracking code in the HTML tab, and save the changes:
Then copy the PHP shortcode of the widget:
Next, place the copied shortcode of the widget to the text label:
Alternatively, the code can be inserted directly within the text label. However, we recommend using the widget method for more reliable performance and smoother processing.
The tracking code will now trigger each time a user subscribes to the newsletter.
This option is especially useful for scenarios where confirmation appears as inline text or a pop-up, rather than a new page. Be sure to use this method as an alternative in any scenario where a separate success page is not available.
NOTE
: This method may not be optimal and might not work reliably if the script requires a specific loading sequence or is complex. However, it can be effective in many cases. Be sure to thoroughly test before finalizing any updates.

title: How Does Auto-Matching Work? (Lead Settings » General Settings)
content:
The following documentation is exclusively for the "Auto-Matching or Advanced Leads Package".
Auto-matching relies on the auto-matching settings and the search inputs submitted by the users of the website. Here are some of the core concepts of how auto-matching works:
The engine will only match members that match the criteria. If the member is allowed to select a location, say San Francisco, and only 2 members are located in San Francisco, only those two candidates will be matched (assuming they match the additional criteria set by the user such as categories).
Membership Level Sort Order is taken into consideration. This means if there are three premium members in San Francisco, these three premium members will always be auto-matched ahead of the free members that are also located in San Francisco.
For accurate auto-matching, allowing for category inputs and location inputs is key. Not requiring a location or specialty to be entered limits the engine.
Essentially the auto-matching functionality is the same as the member search functionality on the website. The system runs a search just like the users would, and starts to auto-match leads always going from top to bottom.
Auto-Matching Lead Settings
Edit the auto-matching lead settings by going to
Leads » Manage Lead » General Settings
:
Or within the "
Auto-Match Workflows
" screen:
Data Flows Settings
There are 5 additional settings for the automatic matching functionality.
Search Radius
: Members within this radius are eligible to be automatically matched to leads.
Maximum Matches:
This setting controls how many members can be matched to a single lead. Set this to "3", and a maximum of 3 members will be matched. If no one meets the search criteria, no one will be matched and the lead will be flagged as "Pending".
Maximum Acceptances:
This controls how many members can accept a lead. This is particularly helpful if the maximum matches is set to 5+ members, but don't want the website users to be bombarded with emails from the visitors. Once the maximum lead acceptance is reached, the lead status will change to "Sold Out".
Notify Admin If Member Email Invalid:
Select "Yes" if you would like to send an email notification to the Admin when a lead has been matched to a member that does not have a valid email address.
Admin Notification Email Template:
Select the email template to send to the Admin if a lead is matched to a member that does not have a valid email address.

title: Understanding Actions / Data Flows
content:
This documentation covers features specific to the Automatic Lead Matching add-on.
Automatic Lead Matching Add-On
What Is It?
The Automatic Lead Matching add-on upgrades the default Leads system by introducing customizable Lead Actions—rules that control how leads are handled for different membership levels.
The standard
Basic Leads Package
includes:
Instant delivery for direct lead requests
Limit on how many members can accept a lead
Admin email alerts when new leads come in
With this add-on, custom
Lead Actions
can be created and assigned to individual membership levels, giving full control over how leads are distributed and managed.
Key Features:
Auto-Match Control:
Decide which members can receive leads automatically.
Custom Email Templates per Membership Level
: Send different email content to free vs. paid members—thank paying members and encourage free users to upgrade.
Member Lead Acceptance Alerts
: Get notified when a member accepts a lead—ideal timing to follow up or promote upgrades. Automate a thank-you or upsell email.
Sold-Out Lead Notifications:
Get alerted when a member tries to claim a lead that’s already been sold. Trigger an automatic email explaining what happened and how to avoid it.
These features are exclusive to the Automatic Lead Matching add-on and designed to help automate lead distribution while maximizing upsell opportunities and overall lead management efficiency.
Create New Data Flows

Default Lead Action & Creating New Lead Actions

Understanding Card Type Information (Stripe Only)
When an admin views a member’s saved payment information in the member’s
Account Details
, the dashboard will also display the
type of card
stored for that account.
This information is
only available when when Stripe is used
as the payment gateway. Other gateways do not display these details.
The card type label helps clarify how the card is stored in Stripe and whether it supports recurring subscription payments. Below are the possible types and their meanings:
Legacy
A non-3D Secure card saved as a legacy “card” object in Stripe.
Recurring subscription payments will process normally. If there are any issues collecting payments on this type of card, the member may need to log in to the Member Dashboard and save their credit card information once again so it is saved as a modern "Payment Method" object in Stripe.
Legacy (3DS)
A 3D Secure card
saved as a legacy “card” object in Stripe
.
If there are any issues collecting payments on this type of card, the member may need to log in to the Member Dashboard and save their credit card information once again so it is saved as a modern "Payment Method" object in Stripe.
Payment Method
A non-3D Secure card saved as a modern “payment method” object in Stripe.
This is Stripe's preferred, most up-to-date format. Recurring subscription payments will process normally.
Payment Method (3DS Recurring)
A 3D Secure card saved as a modern “payment method” object in Stripe that supports recurring
subscription
payments.
Recurring subscription payments will process normally.
Payment Method (3DS Manual)
A 3D Secure card saved as a modern “payment method” object in Stripe that requires manual authentication for each transaction.
The member must log in to their Member Dashboard and manually authenticate every payment.
The member may contact the bank to remove this requirement or use a different card.

title: Edit 404 Error Pages
content:
When a requested URL does not correspond to an existing page on the website, the server returns a “404 Not Found” error, indicating that the page cannot be located. Common triggers for this error include:
A visitor clicks a link on another site that leads to a non-existent page on the directory.
A URL that previously existed has been deleted or moved.
A visitor mistypes a URL.
A bot or crawler (such as from Google Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools, etc.) attempts to access a URL in error.
When any of these events occur, the website responds with the 404 error code and displays a designated “404 error page” (the content served when the page cannot be found).
How to Create a Custom 404 Page
Navigate to My Content >> New Web Page
Add a unique Permalink (e.g., "my404")
Set the page type as “
Single Web Page
”.
Save the page.
Once created, the 404 page can be styled and populated with whatever content and links are appropriate for the site.
Alternatively, ask the
BD Butler
to create a unique 404 page design.
Selecting the Default 404 Error Page
Within the platform’s advanced settings, there is an option labelled
Default 404 Error Page
. Using the dropdown menu, select the newly created web page (or any existing page) to serve as the designated 404 error page.
Default 404 Error Page
error_404
How Does a Brilliant Directories Website Handle 404 Error Pages?
Historically, all Brilliant Directories-powered websites used the homepage as the 404 error page. While using the homepage can work for human visitors (because they can potentially find their destination via the homepage), the homepage is typically one of the heaviest pages in terms of bandwidth—often loading multiple megabytes.
When non-human traffic (such as bots or crawlers) triggers 404 errors and is served the homepage each time, this can consume excessive bandwidth and server resources. To mitigate this, the system now uses a minimal default 404 error page that:
Presents a simple notification that the requested page cannot be found.
Includes a link to the homepage for genuine users who may wish to continue browsing.
Uses significantly less bandwidth (on the order of ~1 KB) compared to loading the full homepage.
This change helps reduce unnecessary server load arising from erroneous URL requests while still providing a user-friendly experience for legitimate visitors.

title: How Bandwidth and Storage Usage Is Calculated
content:
In the Dashboard Area of every Brilliant Directories website, there is an indication of the storage that is currently being used and the bandwidth that has been used for the current calendar month:
Our server network utilizes the CentOS / WHM / cPanel stack to manage hosting accounts and calculate bandwidth and storage usage data.
To measure bandwidth, cPanel & WHM combines the amount of bytes of an incoming data request with the outgoing transferred data (the response to that request). cPanel & WHM obtains this data from the Apache logs. These logs include the following amounts of bandwidth:
The total bandwidth that the incoming request that solicited the content used.
The total bandwidth that the complete response used (the sum of the size of the content plus the header).
For more information about how bandwidth usage data is calculated, and why it may differ from data obtained using other tools, please see the full documentation on this topic here:
Apparent Discrepancies in Bandwidth Usage Statistics

title: How To Enable Hotlink Protection
content:
Understanding Hotlink Protection
Hotlinking occurs when another website displays files that are hosted on your website, such as images, by directly linking to their source URL. While the content appears on the third-party website, the files are still being served from your website, which means your website's bandwidth and server resources are being used to deliver that content.
How Hotlink Protection Works
Hotlink protection prevents other websites from directly embedding and displaying files hosted on your website. When enabled, requests originating from unauthorized domains will be blocked from accessing protected content.
This can help reduce unnecessary bandwidth usage and prevent third-party websites from using your hosted images and files without permission.
Important Considerations
Before enabling hotlink protection, keep in mind that some websites and services may no longer be able to display your images if they rely on direct file access.
Many major platforms, including social media networks, use their own methods to preview and cache content, so they are generally not affected. However, smaller websites and applications that directly reference your image URLs may be unable to display those files once hotlink protection is enabled.
Option 1: Enable Hotlink Protection with Cloudflare
If your website is connected to Cloudflare, you can enable Cloudflare's built-in Hotlink Protection feature.
Cloudflare Documentation:
https://support.cloudflare.com/hc/en-us/articles/200170026-Understanding-Cloudflare-Hotlink-Protection
Option 2: Configure Hotlink Protection with an .htaccess File
For websites hosted on servers that support Apache configuration files, hotlink protection can also be implemented using rules added to the website's
.htaccess
file.
Reference Guide:
https://mediatemple.net/community/products/dv/204644230/prevent-hotlinking-with-a-.htaccess-file
Additional Notes
Brilliant Directories does not currently include a built-in hotlink protection setting. If hotlink protection is required, it will need to be configured through a service such as Cloudflare or by implementing server-level rules where supported.

title: Manage Your Website's Email Accounts With Microsoft 365
content:
Manage a Website's Email Accounts with Microsoft 365
Microsoft 365 can host email for a domain connected to a Brilliant Directories website. Microsoft supplies the DNS records that verify the domain and route mail to its service.
1. Add and Verify the Domain in Microsoft 365
Open
Settings > Domains
in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Add the root domain without
www
.
Copy the TXT verification record supplied by Microsoft.
Add that record wherever the domain's live DNS is managed, then complete Microsoft's verification.
Microsoft references:
Add a custom domain
and
add DNS records at a DNS provider
.
2. Find Where DNS Is Managed
If the domain uses Brilliant Directories-managed DNS, open
Settings > Domain Manager
. Hosted email routing is available under
Mailboxes
; see
Manage Mailboxes and Email Routing
. DNS records can also be managed through
Developer Hub > cPanel Dashboard > Zone Editor
when that option is available.
If the domain uses Cloudflare, GoDaddy, Namecheap, or another provider's nameservers, add the Microsoft records at that provider. Records added in cPanel do not affect a domain whose live DNS is hosted elsewhere.
3. Add the Microsoft 365 Records
Copy the exact values from the Microsoft 365 admin center. Common records include:
Type
Common host
Purpose
TXT
@ or root
Verifies domain ownership.
MX
@ or root
Routes incoming mail to Microsoft 365.
CNAME
autodiscover
Helps Outlook locate mailbox settings.
TXT
@ or root
Authorizes Microsoft 365 in SPF.
Microsoft can also require CNAME or SRV records for Teams, device enrollment, and other services. Add only the records displayed for the domain and enabled services. See
Microsoft's external DNS record reference
.
4. Change Mail Routing
Create the Microsoft 365 mailboxes before changing MX. Replace obsolete MX records with the Microsoft value and priority shown in the admin center. Leaving conflicting MX records can split or misdirect incoming mail.
Microsoft 365 requires the exact mail server hostname supplied in its admin center. Opening this form does not change routing.
5. Configure SPF
A domain should publish one SPF TXT record. If SPF already exists, merge the required authorized senders into that record instead of adding a second SPF record. Follow
Microsoft's SPF guidance
.
6. Verify and Test
Use Microsoft's record check, then test sending and receiving. If verification fails, confirm the host/name, destination, priority, spaces, duplicate SPF records, old MX records, and the authoritative DNS provider.
Service Boundaries
Microsoft manages its mailboxes, billing, passwords, and account access. Brilliant Directories provides DNS or routing controls only when the domain uses supported Brilliant Directories-managed services.

title: Setting Up How Member Reviews Are Approved On The Website
content:
To configure how member reviews are approved on your website, go to:
Finance » Membership Plans » Profile Page Tab
.
The review approval workflow is controlled by two settings:
Require All Reviews To Be Approved by Admin First
– Determines whether an administrator must review and approve new reviews before they can be published.
Ability to Accept and Delete Reviews (Member)
– Determines whether members can approve or reject reviews submitted to their profile.
The combination of these two settings determines how every new review is processed. The four possible workflows are explained below.
The combination of these two settings determines how every new review is processed. The four possible workflows are explained below.
Scenario 1
Require All Reviews To be Approved by Admin First:
SET TO NO
Ability to Accept and Delete Reviews (Member):
SET TO NO
By setting both to "NO", all member reviews that are submitted to the website will automatically get published and appear live on the member's profile page and the homepage if the latest reviews are streamed.
Scenario 2
Require All Reviews To be Approved by Admin First:
SET TO NO
Ability to Accept and Delete Reviews (Member):
SET TO YES
Scenario 2 automatically sets all reviews to "WAITING FOR MEMBER". The review will not be published on the website until the member approves the review. The member will also receive an automated notification that there is a pending review in their account.
Scenario 3
Require All Reviews To be Approved by Admin First:
SET TO YES
Ability to Accept and Delete Reviews (Member):
SET TO YES
The third scenario automatically sets all reviews to "WAITING FOR ADMIN". The admin gets an email notification that a review was submitted and must go to the admin area of the website to approve the review manually.
»
Approving Member Reviews from the Admin
Scenario 4
Require All Reviews To be Approved by Admin First:
SET TO YES
Ability to Accept and Delete Reviews (Member):
SET TO NO
Our last scenario automatically sets reviews to "WAITING FOR ADMIN". Since members are not able to accept or delete reviews, the admin only has the choice to accept or delete the review. There is no option to notify the member or set it to "WAITING FOR MEMBER". The ADMIN will see the following pop-up when the setting is changed to "APPROVED"
»
Approving Member Reviews from the Admin
Email Templates Linked To New Review Module

Emails → Email Templates

title: Toolbox » Sidebar Applications
content:
What is a Sidebar
A sidebar is a container that holds widgets, typically displayed to the side of web pages. Common examples of widgets placed in sidebars include banner ads, search modules, and newsletter signup modules. The Brilliant Directories platform comes with a set of predefined sidebars that can be modified and updated according to the website's needs.
Sidebar Examples
Post Details Pages:
Static Pages:
Member Search Results:
Additional Information:
Sidebar Setup Steps For Membership Features/ Post Types
How To Add A Sidebar To A Static Page
How To Create A Sidebar
This is
IMPORTANT INFORMATION
about Sidebars:
Sidebars are containers, not positioning tools.
A sidebar simply wraps around a group of widgets that will be used together. Despite the name, a sidebar does not place its widgets on the left or right side of a page; that placement comes from CSS applied on the page where the sidebar is used.
Any sidebar can be called with a shortcode.
To use a sidebar on a static page, or on any page that does not offer a built-in sidebar option (as the membership features do), add the shortcode with the sidebar's name. For example, for a sidebar named myCustomSidebar, add
[
sidebar
=
name_sidebar
]
to the page, placing the code closest to where the sidebar should appear. If needed, style it with CSS to look correct or to mimic a sidebar on a different page.
The same sidebar can look different on different pages.
Because sidebars carry no positioning CSS of their own, using a sidebar on one page does not guarantee it will look the same on another.

title: "Publish Date" Functionality For The  Admin Blog
content:
What Is A Publish Date?
A publish date allows to set a future post date for the admin blog articles. Some users prefer to add multiple articles to their blog in one session, but do not want the articles to get published at the same time, nor do they want to log back in to "Publish" an article and make it live on their website.
With the "Publish Date" functionality website admins can now set the date they wish articles to be published on their website.
Important:
This functionality is exclusively supported for the "Admin Blog" feature (the feature which uses the "Feature - Blog Articles" form). The primary reason this is not available to the member blog feature is that members would be able to cheat the system and re-publish articles allowing their articles to always show first on the website.
How To Set A Future Publish Date For An Admin Blog Post
To set a future publish date for the admin blog articles please follow these instructions:
Go to My Members - Search Members
"Login" as the admin blog contributor or whichever member has access to the "Blog" post type
Click on "Add Blog Article"
Set the article to "Publish" - "Yes". Remember, if the blog has been set to a future publish date, the article will not go live until the publish date.
To set a Publish Date click on the "Publish Date" field to open up the calendar.
Select the desired date to have the article published on the website:
Add the content of the article
Click on "Save Changes"
How Does The System Allow The Publish Date To Work With The Blog Feature?
The "Publish" functionality works exclusively with the "Blog" feature. The system uses the same variable as "events" and "classifieds". All three forms use "post_status", however the functionality is quite different. For "Events" and "Classifieds", the "post_status" variable will publish the post on the website immediately regardless of the date selected.

title: How to Connect a Domain to a Brilliant Directories Website
content:
Connect a custom domain, a subdomain, or a free
directoryup.com
address from
Settings > Domain Manager
. The connection flow checks the proposed address and shows the pointing instructions before changing the website address.
Example on a free directoryup.com address. Additional tabs appear when a custom domain and its services are available.
About the examples:
The screenshots use Brilliant Directories test websites.
demotailwind.com
is managed in Cloudflare and illustrates the Cloudflare route;
selfautomated.com
uses Brilliant Directories nameservers and illustrates the non-Cloudflare alternative. These are alternative DNS arrangements, not consecutive changes to the same domain.
Before starting
For a custom domain, have access to its DNS provider and registrar.
Record the existing mail provider and preserve its MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and other required records.
For a Cloudflare connection, have permission to authorize the correct account and domain.
For an existing live site, complete the
domain-change checklist
.
Managed SSL installation requires the Managed SSL add-on to be active. A domain change alone does not add that entitlement.
Choose the correct site before starting.
The final switch changes the website address. The former address is no longer the site’s primary address, and an old-domain redirect must be arranged separately if needed.
The wizard has four stages, shown across the top:
Choose An Address
,
Check It
,
Point Domain
, and
Switch Over
. A completed stage can be clicked to return to it until the switch has run.
1. Choose An Address
Open
Settings > Domain Manager > Domain
.
Click
Connect my domain name
or
Change my domain name
.
Select the appropriate option below.
Use a domain from my Cloudflare account
: when available, authorize Cloudflare and select a domain from the account. The screen marks this option
Fastest — nothing to type
.
A domain name I own
: enter a registered domain or a true subdomain and configure its DNS.
A free address from us
: choose the portion before
.directoryup.com
.
Choose the route that matches the domain and DNS provider.
2. Check It
Enter the address without
http://
,
https://
, or a page path.
A root domain can be typed with or without www., as
example.com
or
www.example.com
. The wizard always connects a root domain as
www.example.com
.
A true subdomain is entered exactly, such as
members.example.com
. If
www.
is typed in front of a subdomain, the wizard removes it and checks the subdomain itself.
For a root domain, choose how the address appears under
How should your address appear?
:
With www.
or
Without www.
. The choice appears as soon as a root domain is typed, and its default follows what was typed. Visitors who type the other version are sent to the chosen one.
Without www.
needs the root domain itself to point at the website; see
Point the root domain
.
Click
Check this address
. The box turns green when the address can be checked. A domain extension that does not exist, such as
.come
, is refused with a message naming it.
Resolve any validation message before continuing.
For a free address, enter only the chosen prefix using letters, numbers, and hyphens. For Cloudflare, select the intended domain from the account's domain list; use its filter to locate the correct domain.
The A domain name I own route: a root domain is typed and the With www. / Without www. choice appears under the box. The Cloudflare route selects the domain from a list instead, as shown below.
3. Point Domain
The
Point Domain
stage reports where the address currently points, names the company where the records are added (the domain's DNS provider, or the registrar when no DNS provider is identified), and lists each record with its own
Pointed
or
Not pointed yet
status. Copy the site's own target from this screen; an example address from documentation is not a usable target.
Instructions
opens the step-by-step guide below the records, and
Use a different address
returns to
Check It
.
Add the records at the current DNS provider
Open the DNS provider's record editor.
Add or update the record for the exact host shown in the wizard.
Save the DNS change at the provider.
Return to Domain Manager.
Click
Check again
.
The www record has these fields:
Type:
CNAME
Name:
www
Value:
The site's unique directoryup.com target copied from Domain Manager
For a subdomain such as
members.example.com
, the only record is a CNAME whose name is normally
members
at the DNS provider, pointing to the same target. The root domain is not changed.
For a root domain, the stage lists a second entry for
example.com
itself: a record, or a forwarding setting on GoDaddy with
With www.
. With
With www.
, that entry sends visitors who type example.com on to www.example.com; the website works at www.example.com without it, so
Continue
is offered once the www record is pointed. With
Without www.
, example.com is the main address and must reach the website. The root domain cannot take an ordinary CNAME, so the right record depends on the DNS provider; see
Point the root domain
.
The Point Domain stage for a subdomain of a domain in the connected Cloudflare account. Use the target shown by the website being connected.
Point the root domain (CNAME exception)
DNS does not allow an ordinary CNAME record on the root of a domain (the record named
@
), so the root domain is connected differently depending on the company that runs the domain's DNS. The
Point Domain
stage identifies that company from the domain's nameservers and shows the matching method below: a CNAME on Cloudflare, Domain Forwarding on GoDaddy when the address uses www, an ALIAS record on Namecheap, and an A record for any other DNS provider or when the provider cannot be identified. An A record works everywhere, but it points at a fixed server address; the Cloudflare, GoDaddy, and Namecheap methods keep the domain following the website if it moves to a different server.
Brilliant Directories nameservers
Nothing needs to be added. The
Point Domain
stage reports
We manage the DNS for
the address, and the records are created during the switch.
Cloudflare
Cloudflare flattens a CNAME on the root, so the root takes the same record as www. Delete the existing root and www records first, then add both of these:
Type:
CNAME
Name:
@ (the root domain, example.com)
Value:
The site's unique directoryup.com target
Type:
CNAME
Name:
www
Value:
The site's unique directoryup.com target
When the Cloudflare account is connected to Domain Manager,
Use a domain from my Cloudflare account
or
Add this record for me
creates these records automatically.
GoDaddy
GoDaddy does not allow a CNAME record on the root of a domain. With
With www.
, connect it in two steps:
Edit the existing
www
record so it is a CNAME pointing to the site's unique directoryup.com target.
Turn on
Domain Forwarding
so example.com forwards to
https://www.example.com
: in GoDaddy's DNS settings for the domain, open
Forwarding
, click
Add Forwarding
, choose
https://
, enter
www.example.com
, select
Permanent (301)
, and click
Save
.
GoDaddy's Forwarding settings: forward the root domain to the https www address, permanently (301).
The
Point Domain
stage shows this forwarding in place of a root record, with a link to GoDaddy's guide. Once example.com forwards permanently (301) to https://www.example.com, the root domain reads
Pointed
on the
Point Domain
and
Switch Over
stages.
With
Without www.
, do not turn on Domain Forwarding for the root domain: the website already sends www visitors to example.com, so a forward the other way sends visitors in a circle and the site stops loading. Add an A record for the root instead, alongside the www CNAME:
Type:
A
Name:
@ (the root domain, example.com)
Value:
The server address shown for the root domain on the Point Domain stage
An A record points at a fixed address, so if the website moves to a different server in the future, that one record needs the same update.
Namecheap
Namecheap supports an ALIAS record on the root of a domain. Namecheap does not allow an ALIAS record alongside an existing A, AAAA, CNAME, or redirect record for the same host, so delete the current root domain record first, then use
Add New Record
to create:
Type:
ALIAS
Name:
@ (the root domain, example.com)
Value:
The site's unique directoryup.com target
Type:
CNAME
Name:
www
Value:
The site's unique directoryup.com target
Namecheap's guide:
How to create an ALIAS record
.
Other DNS providers
Add the www CNAME above, and an A record for the root domain:
Type:
A
Name:
@ (the root domain, example.com)
Value:
The server address shown for the root domain on the Point Domain stage
An A record points at a fixed address, so if the website moves to a different server in the future, that one record needs the same update. For the long term, moving the domain's DNS to a free Cloudflare account avoids this, because Cloudflare can hold the site's target on the root domain; see
Connecting a Site to Cloudflare
.
Use a connected Cloudflare account
After Cloudflare authorization, filter the domain list and select the intended domain. Choose its main
www.
address or enter a subdomain, then click
Use this address
. The wizard prepares the DNS records and advances to
Switch Over
, skipping the
Point Domain
stage. To see the record it added, click
Show me the DNS record you added
on the
Switch Over
stage.
Start over
returns to the three choices.
A domain entered through
A domain name I own
can also be on Cloudflare. When the domain is in the Cloudflare zone already connected to the site, the
Point Domain
stage offers
Add this record for me
. When it is on Cloudflare under a different zone or account, the stage offers
Set it up for me
, or
Sign in and set it up for me
when the account holding that domain is not connected yet. Use the offered button, or expand
I would rather add the record myself
to add the record by hand, then click
Check again
. Preparing a record does not complete the website-address switch; the final confirmation is still required. See
Cloudflare in Domain Manager
.
Filter the Cloudflare domain list, select the intended domain, and choose the main address or a subdomain.
Move the entire domain's DNS to Brilliant Directories
The nameserver alternative is appropriate when the whole domain's DNS should be managed by Brilliant Directories. It is not necessary merely to connect one subdomain. On the
Point Domain
stage, select
Nameservers
instead of
DNS record
to show the two nameservers, then replace the domain's nameservers at the registrar with both of them:
Nameserver:
ns1.directorysecure.com
Nameserver:
ns2.directorysecure.com
When the domain already uses these nameservers, the
Point Domain
stage reports
We manage the DNS for
the address. There is nothing to add; the record is created during the switch. A nameserver change can take a few hours to reach everyone.
A nameserver change affects the whole domain.
The wizard warns that this moves all DNS to Brilliant Directories. Preserve and recreate the records required by existing email and other services before changing nameservers. For a single subdomain while the main website or email stays elsewhere, use the subdomain CNAME route.
Free directoryup.com addresses do not need records changed at an external registrar; their flow skips the
Point Domain
stage.
Non-Cloudflare example: selfautomated.com is registered at GoDaddy and uses Brilliant Directories nameservers. The Domain tab confirms that both the main address and the address without www are connected.
4. Switch Over
Click
Continue
after reviewing the pointing result. When the main address is not pointed yet, this button reads
Continue anyway
.
Check
Now
and
After the change
.
After the change
lists the main address first and, for a root domain, the other version with
forwards to
. Each shows its own status:
Pointed
,
Cannot verify
,
Checking…
, or
Not pointed yet
. Click
Not pointed yet
to see what is missing;
Show me what to set up
returns to
Point Domain
.
Read the message above the buttons.
Ready to switch to
the new address appears when it is ready; otherwise
What happens when you switch
describes the change. Both name the current address, which stops loading the website once the switch is done.
Click
Switch to this address
.
Confirm
Yes, switch it
in the confirmation dialog.
Keep the page open until the progress screen completes.
Do not treat a
Not pointed yet
result as a completed connection.
Continue anyway
allows the switch before DNS is ready: the new address does not load the website until its record is in place, and the current address stops working straight away.
If
Without www.
was chosen but the root domain does not reach the website yet, the switch keeps the website on the www version and Domain Manager says so. Change it later under
Web address style
once the root domain points at the website; see
Set Up The WWW or Non-WWW Version Of The Domain
.
Review the current and new addresses and the message above the buttons before confirming the switch.
Confirm the result
The completion screen identifies the new address and the remaining setup tasks. Email authentication is attempted during the switch when the connected DNS service can accept the records. If manual setup is required, follow the
Emails
tab's instructions. Managed SSL installation is attempted when the add-on is active; certificate issuance can finish after the address change. The switch also moves the website's sending address to the new domain when it used the old domain or a placeholder address, keeping the part before the @. An address at another domain, such as a Gmail address, is left unchanged.
The completed switch identifies the new address and the remaining SSL and integration tasks. Website sender authentication is separate from incoming-mail setup.
Open the new website address.
Review the
SSL
tab.
Review
Emails > Sender Authentication
.
Test website forms, login, and any domain-restricted integrations.
DNS changes can take time to become visible everywhere. Use
Check again
and compare the exact host and target if the connection remains unresolved. Contact support with the domain, site ID, and displayed error when the records appear correct but the site still fails.
Free-address testing has separate limitations; see
directoryup.com Subdomain Test Credentials
.

title: Developer Hub » Image Settings » Profile Photos, Logos & Cover
content:
IMPORTANT NOTE: Unless the site has heavy customizations to the underlying code of the website's design, there is no need to touch these settings as they will already be optimized for use around the website.
This article will cover the image settings for the following:
Profile Photo for Website
Profile Photo for Social Media Sharing
Profile Logo for Website
Profile Logo for Social Media Sharing
Profile Cover
On the Image Settings page, these settings are in the
Member Photos
,
Member Logos
and
Cover Photos
sections, listed under
Image Sizes
in the side menu. Changes on the Image Settings page take effect only after
Save
is clicked in the save bar at the top of the page.
1
— the Member Photos, Member Logos and Cover Photos sections in the side menu.
2
— the settings of the selected section.
Additional Information:
Image Settings - Member Post Types- Single Photo
Image Settings - Member Post Types - Multiple Photos
Profile Logo Settings
Here are some things to know regarding editing Profile Logo:
The profile logo can be set to either an
“Open” ratio
or a fixed aspect ratio of
3:4
or
1:1
. More details on how aspect ratios work
can be found here.
When selecting the
“Open”
option, members are not restricted to a specific shape. This means they can upload images that are square, wider than they are tall, or taller than they are wide.
With the ratio set to
“Open”
, the
Width
and
Height
values act as maximum limits rather than fixed dimensions. For example, if both values are set to
200px
and a member uploads a
2000px × 2000px
image, the system will automatically resize it to
200px × 200px
. The image’s original proportions are preserved, but it is scaled down so it does not exceed the defined limits. This resizing helps ensure that images remain optimized for performance, allowing pages to load faster and improving the overall browsing experience across the website.
1
— the Profile Logo setting.
2
— its Ratio, which can be Open, 1:1 or 3:4.
Entering a "Profile Logo" width of less than 162px shows a Warning message, and the width is reset to 162px:
*This is done to make sure that large images are resized to dimensions that will look relatively uniform in the various areas of the website where profile logos are used.
Entering a "Profile Logo Social Media" width or height of less than the required 200px shows a Warning message, and the value is reset to 200px:
Profile Photo Settings
The Profile Photo Settings function much like the Profile Logo Settings, with one key difference; Profile Photos allow you to set an aspect ratio of 3:4 or 1:1.
This helps ensure that profile images fit properly across different areas of the website where they are displayed.
Please note:
Changing the default Aspect Ratios is possible, but not recommended.  Doing so would require customizing the design of the website significantly in order to accommodate a different aspect ratio for these images around the website and should only be requested by Advanced Users of the software that have significant experience in customizing the design of Brilliant Directories websites.
Profile Cover Settings
Here are some things to know regarding editing Profile Cover:
The ratio of the Profile Cover will always be "Open" so members are not forced to upload an image that is a certain shape - wider than it is tall, or taller than it is wide.
Since the ratio is always "Open", the "Width" and "Height" numbers serve as limits for the maximum width and height of the image.  For example, if the Width and height are set to 1200px x 500px, and a member uploads an image that is 2000px wide x 800px tall, the final image will be resized to be 1
200px
wide x
500px
tall, maintaining the same aspect ratio of the original image, but downsizing it to be no more than the
limit.  This helps ensure that the website loads these images as quickly and efficiently as possible, thus reducing the overall time to load all of the website's pages as much as possible.
How To Upload Logo Images As A Member
Login as a member and go to the "Profile Photo" Tab
Click on "Upload Logo" (once a logo has been uploaded, the button reads "Change Logo"):
NOTE: Accepted Image formats are: JPG, PNG, GIF and WEBP
3. Click "Choose Logo" and select an image to upload. It opens in the cropping window:
4. Click "Click to Save Photo". If the logo is not large enough the member will receive the following message, warning them that the current image is smaller than 200px x 200px and will have to be stretched in order to meet the minimum size requirements for sharing on social media websites, and the logo will appear on the website at a smaller size than other Profile Logos. This warning appears only when the
Skip Image Size Warning for Profile Photos and Logos
Advanced Setting (system variable skip_photo_upload_warning_size) is turned off. It is ON by default, so by default the image is uploaded without the warning.
How To Upload Profile Photos As A Member
When uploading the profile photo, they will follow the same process as uploading a Profile Logo.  However, the members will be required to use the built-in cropping tool which will ensure that the final image uses the 3:4 Aspect Ratio specified in the Profile Photo Settings:
If the photo is smaller than 200px x 200px, clicking "Click to Save Photo" shows the following warning, and "Upload and Stretch" uploads it anyway. This warning appears only when the
Skip Image Size Warning for Profile Photos and Logos
Advanced Setting (system variable skip_photo_upload_warning_size) is turned off. It is ON by default, so by default the image is uploaded without the warning.
It is now possible to
zoom in & out
,
rotate
, and
flip
profile photo images while cropping, using the tools below the image:
How To Upload Cover Images As A Member
When uploading the cover photo, they will follow the same process as uploading a Profile Picture/Logo.
However, the members will be required to use the built-in cropping tool which will ensure that the final image uses the dimensions specified in the
Profile Cover Settings
:
Additional Information
The image module is made up of text labels that can be edited:
»
How to locate Text Labels on the Front end of a Website
»
Settings » Text Labels

content:

On the Image Settings page, these settings are in the
Single Photo Posts
section, listed under

1
— Single Photo Posts in the side menu.
2
— the Single Photo Post - Thumbnail and Single Photo Post - Large settings.

Image Settings - Profile Photos & Logos

The recommended default settings are a free (open) ratio, a width of 272, and a height of 160.
The ratio of the Single Photo Post - Thumbnail will always be "Open" so members are not forced to upload an image that is a certain shape - it can be square, wider than it is tall, or taller than it is wide.
Since the ratio is always "Open", the "Width" and "Height" numbers serve as limits for the maximum width and height of the image.  For example, if both the Width and Height are set to 200px, and a member uploads an image that is 2000px wide x 2000px tall, the final image will be resized to be
200px
wide x
200px
tall, maintaining the same aspect ratio of the original image, but downsizing it to be no more than the
200px
x
200px
limit. This helps ensure that the website loads these images as quickly and efficiently as possible, thus reducing the overall time to load all of the website's pages as much as possible.
As another example, if both the Width and height are set to 200px, and a member uploads an image that is 2000px wide x 1000px tall, the image will be resized so that it fits within the limits of 200px x 200px, without changing the aspect ratio.  In this example, the final uploaded image would be 200px wide x 100px tall so it fits within the 200px x 200px limit without changing its aspect ratio or stretching / distorting the image.
If the "Single Photo Post - Thumbnail" width is set to less than 160px, a Warning message appears and the width is reset to 160px:
** This is done to make sure that large images are resized to dimensions that will look relatively uniform in the various areas of the website where single photo member post type thumbnails are used. Even though images can be set to be smaller than the default settings, we do not recommend doing so unless customizing the underlying code of the website's design to accommodate these smaller images.
The Width and Height settings can be set as high as needed, but please note doing this will
not
cause the images to DISPLAY larger around the site,  The image itself will be saved at a larger size, but will be shrunk down to fit into the space available for it when displayed on the website.  In other words, all of the images will take longer and use more bandwidth to load, and will not display any larger on the website.  Making these images larger will only be useful if  heavily customizing the underlying code of the website's design to accommodate these larger images.

The recommended default settings are a free (open) ratio, a width of 375, and a height of 375.  This is also the image used when sharing the Details page of the post on social media.

title: Developer Hub » Image Settings
content:
What are the Image Settings?
The Image Settings of the website determine the final size that images will be saved after being uploaded to the website by members.
The default settings that come with a Brilliant Directories website are designed so that images will fit well in all of the areas of the website in which they display while being optimized for load speed and meeting minimum requirements for social media sharing.
IMPORTANT NOTE: Unless doing heavy customizations to the underlying code of the website's design, there is no need to touch these settings as they will already be optimized for use on a Brilliant Directories website.
How to Access the Image Settings
Go to
ADMIN » DEVELOPER HUB
and click
Edit Image Sizes
on the
Image Settings
card:
Using the Image Settings Page
The page lists every image size in one place, grouped into sections:
Search
— type part of a setting's name to show only the matching settings. The number of results appears below the box, and
Clear
(or the X in the box) shows every setting again.
Side menu
— click a section to jump to it. The
Image Sizes
group holds
Member Photos
,
Member Logos
,
Cover Photos
,
Single Photo Posts
,
Album Posts
and
Text Editor Images
. The
Page Speed
group holds
Lazy Loading
.
Settings
— each section lists its image sizes with a
Width
and
Height
in pixels, plus a
Ratio
for the member photo and logo sizes.
Restore Defaults
— puts every image size and the lazy loading setting back to the platform defaults (see below).
Searching for a setting:
Saving Changes
Changes on this page are not saved until
Save
is clicked. As soon as a value changes, the edited setting is marked with a dot and a save bar appears at the top of the page with the message
Unsaved changes
and two buttons:
Save
— saves every change on the page at once, including the
Lazy Loading
setting. The button briefly shows
Saved
when the save is complete. Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on a Mac) does the same while the save bar is showing.
Discard
— asks
Discard Unsaved Changes?
and, after
Discard Changes
is clicked, puts back the values that were last saved.
Keep Editing
closes the question without losing anything.
Changing a size and then discarding the change:
Some values are checked as they are entered. A width or height below the minimum allowed for that image (EG 162 pixels for the Profile Logo width) shows a
Warning
message and the value is reset to the minimum. The articles linked at the end of this page cover the limits for each image size.
Restore Defaults
Clicking
Restore Defaults
asks for confirmation first. After
Restore Defaults
is clicked in the confirmation, every image size goes back to its recommended size and
Lazy Load Images
goes back to
Load Images After Scroll
. These values are
saved right away
, with no separate Save step, and the website uses the new sizes immediately. Click
Cancel
to leave the settings unchanged.
General Image Settings Information
Lazy Loading
(
Load Images After Scroll
/
Load Images After Page Load
/
Disabled
)
The
Lazy Load Images
setting is in the
Lazy Loading
section, under
Page Speed
in the side menu. Like every other setting on the page, a new choice takes effect only after
Save
is clicked in the save bar.
1
— Lazy Loading in the side menu, under Page Speed.
2
— the Lazy Load Images setting.
Lazy Loading is a set of techniques in web and application development that defers the loading of resources on a page to a later point in time—when those resources are actually needed instead of loading them upfront. These techniques help in improving performance, better utilization of the device’s resources, and reducing associated costs with bandwidth consumption.
Load Images After Scroll:
Images will only start loading once the page scrolls showing new data and images (Best bandwidth consumption efficiency)
Load Images After Page Load:
Once the first images Above the fold are loaded, it starts loading images below the fold (quickly loads pages, but consumes more bandwidth)
Best for Carousels and Streaming Widgets.
Disabled:
Loads all images by default.
Ratio
The "Ratio" refers to the Aspect Ratio of the image, which is how large the height of an image will be relative to the width of the image and vice-versa.
For example, a 1:1 aspect ratio means it will be a square - for every 1 pixel of width, the image will have 1 pixel of height. As another example, the Aspect Ratio of an HD television is 16:9 (a rectangle that is wider than it is tall), meaning the image on the television will have 16 pixels of width for every 9 pixels of height.
An "Open" aspect ratio means there is no set aspect ratio at all, meaning the image can be any shape.
For more information about Aspect Ratios, please see the
Wikipedia article on the topic
.
Width
The maximum width of the final image in pixels.
Height
The maximum height of the final image in pixels.
Social Media Sharing
When uploading an image, two copies of the image will be saved: one that is optimized for display on the website, and one that is optimized for social media sharing. Currently, Facebook and many other popular social media sites require images to be at least 200px x 200px to be shared on their platform.
One copy of the image will be saved to be at least this size, and another will be saved that is optimized for displaying on the website where a smaller size is required.
Adding Images for Members
Users can upload Logos and Profile Photos through the member dashboard:
How to Complete a Profile as a Member
Admins can import members with Logos and Profile Photos through the import file:
Importing Members with Images
These images are added as links into an import file that is uploaded and then added to the corresponding member profile.
Using links to add member Logos and Profile Photos is only available through the member import file.
Specific Image Settings Information
For more information about the settings available on this page as they apply to different areas of the site, check out the following articles:
Developer Hub » Image Settings » Profile Photos, Logos & Cover
Developer Hub » Image Settings » Member Post Types - Single Photo
Developer Hub » Image Settings » Member Post Types - Multiple Photos

title: FROALA Text Editor: Versions and their Upload Functionalities
content:
When creating a post, such as a blog article, there is a Froala Text Editor which allows modifying styles such as the font size, font colors, boldness, and more.
There are different text editor versions available that either restrict or allow for image upload and video embed.
These can be used and applied individually via the
FORM MANAGER
to the respective forms for the members' "ABOUT ME" section and all post types such as coupons, properties, classifieds, member articles, website blog articles, etc.
This form field type is only supported for forms used within the Member Dashboard.
This provides the ability to control if members can add images and video embeds into the text editor input fields of posts and their "ABOUT ME" section.
The Froala Editor currently supports 38 languages
, check which languages are supported:
https://www.froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/languages.
The Froala Editor is going to use the language that is set in the Settings >> General Settings >> Localization tab >> Default Website Language.
How To Enable Froala Editors
There are three built-in versions of the Froala Text Editor. You can add any of them to a form, and each one controls things like whether users can upload images or embed YouTube videos.
For details on where each editor is used throughout the site and what features they include, click the link below:
Everything About WYSIWYG Editors
Available Text Editors

Froala Text Editor - Basic
No image upload, video embed, or source code editor
Basic text editor with limited options to edit font size, colors, styles, and create bullet checklists.

Underline
Font Size
Paragraph Format
Line Height
Text Color
Background Color
Clear Formatting

Unordered List

Insert a Link
The basic editor only provides basic font formatting. The user
CANNOT:
Upload images
Embed videos
Edit source code
Insert a table

Allows image upload, video embed, and source code editor
Allowed image formats: gif, jpeg, jpg, png, JPEG, JPG, SVG, PNG, webp, and pdf.
It includes the same styling options as the Basic Froala Editor
AND
it includes the ability to:

Embed YouTube videos
Insert a Table
Edit source code
Decrease or Increase Indent

It enables the
Pre-Made Elements
module.
It includes the same styling options as the Basic Froala Editor AND it includes the ability to:
Upload images and GIFs
Embed YouTube videos
Edit source code
Insert and style web links
Choose the font type.
Add
Pre-Made Elements

FROALA EDITOR - ACCESS MEDIA MANAGER

* To confirm that the "Access Media Manager - Froala Text Editor" is working as expected, log in as the admin member and click on the "add image" icon. The FOLDER icon should be displayed:

title: How to Add a Facebook Feed to Member Profile Pages
content:
Business accounts can stream their Facebook feed in the sidebar of their profile.
With this functionality, the Facebook Feed streams all of the latest posts and updates from a specific Facebook account.
The Facebook Feed will display the posts in chronological order:
Important
Only Facebook Company Pages or Fan Pages will stream content.
The tool only works with public Facebook company pages. If a member uses their personal Facebook account link, then the feed will show an error or a blank widget.
Facebook does not allow personal Facebook pages from being streamed.*
*
There is nothing that Brilliant Directories can do to change this limitation imposed by Facebook.
Add the Facebook Feed to Member Profile Pages
The Facebook Feed widget is found in the Sidebar Manager. Follow the steps below.
Go to the Toolbox » Sidebar Manager » Member Profile Page sidebar:
Search for "
Member Facebook Feed
" in the Member Profile Page sidebar.
Drag the "
Bootstrap Theme - Module - Member Facebook Feed
" widget into the display position on the Member Profile Page sidebar:
Click on "Save Changes"
Please note that a Facebook Feed will only show on a member's profile page if they have added a proper facebook link in their contact details form:
Facebook Company Page
The tool only works with public Facebook company pages. If a member uses their personal Facebook account link, then the feed will show an error or a blank widget:
These Facebook accounts won't work for the Facebook Feed:
If it's a personal Facebook profile (not a company page).
If it's a company page, but not public (users must be logged into FB to see the timeline)
If it's an invalid Facebook Link
If the company Facebook page is still not published
Is my Facebook account a personal profile or a page?
Facebook pages must be public for the feed to work. When not logged in to Facebook the information will be still accessible.
For example, our Facebook page is a public page:
https://www.facebook.com/BrilliantDirectories
On the other hand, Facebook profiles or private pages are not available unless logged in to the Facebook account, so it will always prompt the user to log in:
If a Facebook link asks for login credentials to continue, that link won't work for the Facebook Feed.
Difference between Profile and Business Page
For more information about the difference between a Facebook profile and a page go to the link below:
»
https://www.facebook.com/help/337881706729661
Note
We updated the Facebook Activity Feed widgets to display the content from this 3rd party site after the rest of the page loads to improve page load times and page speed scores.

title: Guide 9. How to Enable Maps with Google Maps API
content:
In order to use location search and Google Maps features on a Brilliant Directories website, a Google Maps API key must be created in Google Cloud and added to the site admin.
>>
Google Maps API: Features, Functions, and Key Considerations
The Google Maps API key is what lets Google Maps work on the website. The key is created in Google Cloud, which is managed by Google, not Brilliant Directories. Because of this, the setup screens may look a little different for each person depending on their Google account, location, billing setup, or whether they have used Google Cloud before.
Important Notes
The live domain should be connected before completing the Google Maps API setup.
For help connecting a live domain, see:
How To Move A Site To A Live Domain
Google requires billing
to be enabled for Google Maps Platform projects. Google controls billing requirements, credits, limits, and account settings.
If Google Cloud Console opens a blank screen, redirects unexpectedly, or loses the setup session, return to the Google Maps Platform page and select
Get Started
again.
Most of this setup happens inside Google Cloud. The final step happens inside the Brilliant Directories admin.
Step 1 - Create Account
Start by opening Google Maps Platform:
>>
Open Google Maps Platform
Click
Create an account
to get started, or open the Google Cloud Console. Google may ask for account setup, billing information, or project details before continuing.
If Google asks setup questions, answer them based on the website or project being connected. These questions are managed by Google and may vary by account.
Step 2 - Enable Billing
Goal
: The Google Cloud project must have billing enabled before Google Maps can work properly on the website.
Open the Google Cloud Billing page:
Open Google Cloud Billing
[WATCH] How to create a billing account
Select the same Google Cloud project being used for the website and confirm that billing is active.
If billing is not active, follow Google’s prompts to add or connect a billing account.
Google Maps Connect Billing
If Google rejects the payment method, requires identity verification, or shows a billing account error, that issue must be resolved directly inside Google Cloud.
Step 3 - Enable the APIs
Goal
: Enable the required Google Maps APIs for the same Google Cloud project.
Open each API link below and enable it for the Google Cloud project being used for the website.
Enable Maps JavaScript API
Enable Places API (New)
Enable Geocoding API
[WATCH] How to enable Google Maps Platform APIs
Make sure the correct Google Cloud project is selected at the top of the Google Cloud Console before enabling each API.
If Google shows a different screen than expected, focus on the outcome of this step: each of the required APIs should be enabled for the same project.
Google Maps Enabling an API
Step 4 - Create the API Key
Goal
: Create one Google Maps API key that will be added to the Brilliant Directories admin.
Open the Google Cloud Credentials page:
Open Google Cloud Credentials
Click
Create credentials
.
Select
API key
.
The
Create API key
panel opens. The API restrictions (Step 5) and website restrictions (Step 6) can be set here before clicking
Create
, or added later by editing the key.
Copy the new API key.
Google may show slightly different labels depending on the account. The main goal is to create an API key inside the same project where the required APIs were enabled.
Step 5 - Restrict API Access
Goal
: Limit the API key so it can only access the Google Maps APIs needed for the website.
Open the API key from the Google Cloud Credentials page:
Open Google Cloud Credentials
In the
Create API key
panel, or on the
Edit API key
page of an existing key, find the
Select API restrictions
list.
Open the list, select the APIs used by the website, and click
OK
:
Maps JavaScript API
Places API (New)
Geocoding API
If one of these APIs does not appear in the list, return to Step 3 and confirm that the API was enabled for the same Google Cloud project.
When editing an existing key, click
Save
after selecting the APIs. In the
Create API key
panel, finish Step 6 first, then click
Create
.
Step 6 - Restrict the API Key
Goal
: Restrict the API key so it can only be used by the approved website domains.
This step is important because it tells Google which websites are allowed to use the API key.
Under application restrictions, select:
Websites
Then click
Add
under
Website restrictions
and add the allowed website referrers one at a time.
Required Referrers
Use the examples below as a guide. Replace
example.com
with the final domain of the website.
*.directoryup.com/*
*.managemydirectory.com/*
managemydirectory.com
*.example.com/*
example.com
The
directoryup.com
referrer is useful if the site is not live yet.
The
managemydirectory.com
referrers are needed so map-related features can work properly inside the Brilliant Directories admin area.
The custom domain referrers allow the API key to work on the live website domain.
Google Maps: Edit HTTP Referrers
After adding the referrers, click
Create
in the Create API key panel, or
Save
when editing an existing key.
Step 7 - Add the API Key
Goal
: Add the finished Google Maps API key to the Brilliant Directories admin.
Go to
Settings
.
Click
General Settings
.
Click the
Integrations
tab.
Paste the Google Maps API key into the
Google Maps Javascript API Key
field.
Click
Save Changes
.
Optional shortcut: type
Google Maps
in the
Search by Keyword
box at the top right of
General Settings
to show only the matching fields.
After saving, the Google Maps API key is connected to the website.
Step 8 - Check the Result
Goal
: Confirm that Google accepts the key.
Right after
Save Changes
, the
Integrations
tab tests the key with Google and shows the result below the key field:
Website key
: green (
Google Maps key is working
or
Maps work on your website
) means Google accepts the key. A key restricted to the website's domain is tested on the live domain, the way visitors use it.
Server key
: the optional server key, used to geocode members during imports.
No server key saved
in grey is fine for most sites.
A red result names the problem. Click it to see the fix steps and edit the key; a key Google refuses there is not saved. For each possible result, see
Google Maps Issues: Index
.
Google API Usage
Different Brilliant Directories features may use different Google Maps services.
Front-End Website Features
Member profile maps: Maps JavaScript API
Location searches: Places API (New) and Geocoding API
Detect Visitor Location Add-On: Geocoding API
Member Dashboard Features
Contact details forms: Maps JavaScript API, Places API (New), and Geocoding API
Post forms with location fields: Maps JavaScript API, Places API (New), and Geocoding API
Multi-Location Add-On: Maps JavaScript API, Places API (New), and Geocoding API
Admin Dashboard Features
Geocode Members tool: Geocoding API
Location searches in admin tools: Places API (New) and Geocoding API
Enable All Location Features For Pretty URL Search Results Pages advanced setting: Geocoding API
FAQ
Google Cloud Screen Does Not Match This Article
-- Google may update labels, layouts, and setup screens at any time. If the screen looks different, focus on the goal listed in each step.
The main requirements are still the same: billing must be active, the required APIs must be enabled, the API key must be created, and the key must be restricted to the correct website domains.
Google Shows a Questionnaire
-- The questionnaire is part of Google’s setup process. Answer the questions based on the website or project being connected.
Brilliant Directories does not require one specific answer pattern for the Google questionnaire.
SDK Options Appear in Google
-- For a standard Brilliant Directories website setup, SDK options are not needed.
Ignore iOS SDK, Android SDK, Navigation SDK, Fleet Engine, and mobile app setup options unless a separate custom mobile app project specifically requires them.
The API Does Not Appear When Restricting the Key
-- If Maps JavaScript API, Places API (New), or Geocoding API does not appear in the API restrictions list, the API may not be enabled for the selected Google Cloud project.
Return to Step 3, confirm the correct project is selected, and enable the missing API.
When to Contact Brilliant Directories Support
Contact Brilliant Directories Support if:
The API key has been added to the Brilliant Directories admin, but maps are still not loading
The correct APIs appear to be enabled, but the website still shows a map error
There is uncertainty about where to add the API key inside the Brilliant Directories admin
Location features are not working after the Google setup has been completed
When to Contact Google Support
Some issues must be handled directly inside Google Cloud because Google controls the account, billing, verification, project, and API key system.
Contact Google Support or review Google Cloud Help if:
Billing cannot be activated
Google rejects the payment method
The Google Cloud account is locked, suspended, or restricted
Google requires identity verification
The Google Cloud project cannot be accessed
Google shows billing, permissions, or account-level errors
