title: How To Add Members Manually Via The Admin
content:
The Add New
Member form allows administrators to
manually create a member account
directly from within the admin
dashboard without requiring the member
to self-register through the front end
of the site.
Step 1 — Access the Add New Member Form
Navigate to
My Members » Search Members
in the admin dashboard.
Click the
"Add New Member"
button located in the Search Members toolbar.
The Add New Member form will open.
Step 2 — Complete the Add New Member Form
The Add New Member form contains fields for core account setup and optional profile information. Not all fields are required to create the account.
Required Fields
The following four fields are the minimum required to create a member account. The form cannot be submitted until all four are populated:
#
Field
Notes
1
Account Status
Determines whether the account is immediately active or held. See status definitions in the
Quick Edit Module reference
.
2
Membership Plan
Assigns the member to a configured plan under
Finance » Membership Plans
.
3
Email Address
Also serves as the member's login username. Must be unique in the system.
4
Create Login Password
Sets the initial password for the member account.
⚠ CRITICAL CAUTION — Email Is the Login Username:
The email address entered in this field is the credential the member will use to log in to the site. If this email address is changed after account creation, the member's login credentials will change accordingly. The affected member should be informed of any post-creation email address updates.
⚠ CRITICAL CAUTION — Billing Is Not Created by This Form:
Creating a member account manually via this form does NOT create a billing subscription for that member. If the member requires a paid subscription, it must be created separately after the account is saved. The account will exist in the system without any associated payment record until a subscription is added.
Optional Fields
All fields in the form beyond the four required fields are optional. Submitting the form with only the required fields will create a valid member account, but the resulting profile will display minimal public information.
⚠ NOTE — Minimal Profile Appearance:
A member account created with only the four required fields will produce a sparse public-facing profile. No name, address, phone, or profile image will be displayed. It is recommended to populate as many additional fields as possible at the time of creation, or to prompt the member to complete their profile via the member dashboard after account creation.
Step 3 — Submit the Form and Select a Next Action
After the form is submitted successfully, the system displays a confirmation message and presents two action options.
Option A — Login As Member
Selecting
Login As Member
redirects the administrator session to the member's front-end dashboard, logged in as the newly created member. This allows the administrator to verify the member dashboard view or complete additional profile setup on behalf of the member.
Option B — Close Window
Selecting
Close Window
dismisses the confirmation modal and returns the administrator to the Search Members section of the admin dashboard. The newly created member record will be visible in the member list.
Post-Creation Requirements
Two important tasks cannot be completed within the Add New Member form itself and must be handled after the account is created:
1-  Location Data and Geocoding
Location data cannot be assigned to a member account from within the Add New Member form. Member location must be added through one of the following methods after the account is created:
The member can enter their own location information via the member dashboard on the front end of the site.
The administrator can assign and geocode the member's location via
My Members » Search Members
using the geocode tools.
⚠ CRITICAL CAUTION — Members Without Location Data Are Not Searchable by Location:
A manually created member account that has not been geocoded will not appear in location-based search results on the site. Location data must be added and geocoded for the member to be discoverable through location filters.
Reference:
How To Geocode Members
2 - Subscription / Billing Setup
As noted above, the manual account creation form does not generate a subscription or billing record. If the member is on a paid plan, a subscription must be created independently after the account is saved.
Reference:
How To Manually Bill A Member / Create A Subscription For A Member

title: Bulk Actions For Search Members Section
content:
Navigation Path
Admin Dashboard » My Members » Search Members
The Bulk Actions tool
allows administrators to apply
account-level changes to multiple
member records simultaneously. Bulk
actions are initiated from the
Search Members
section and apply to
all members selected within a given
operation.
Part 1 — Selecting Members for a Bulk Action
Before a bulk action can be applied, the target member records must be selected. Two selection methods are available:
Method A — Select All Results on the Current Page
Click the
checkbox
located directly below the Bulk Actions dropdown. This selects all member records currently displayed on the active page of the Search Members results table.
To extend the selection across all records returned by the current search filter (not just the current page), click
"Select All # Results"
after activating the page checkbox.
Method B — Select Members Individually
Click the
checkbox
next to each individual member record in the results table to manually select specific members for the bulk action.
Part 2 — Applying a Bulk Action
Once the target members are selected:
Click the
Bulk Actions
dropdown in the Search Members toolbar.
Select the desired action from the list.
Click
Apply
.
Part 3 — Bulk Actions Reference
The following twelve bulk actions are available in the Search Members Bulk Actions dropdown. Each action applies to all currently selected member records.
1. Update Account Status
Applies a new Account Status value to all selected member records simultaneously.
⚠ CRITICAL CAUTION — Status Change Does Not Affect Billing:
Changing Account Status via bulk action does NOT cancel, pause, or modify any active billing subscriptions for the selected members. Subscription management must be handled independently. Members set to "Not Active" or "Cancelled" via this tool may still be actively billed if their subscriptions are not separately cancelled.
Account Status value definitions:
Quick Edit Module — Account Status
2. Update Verified Status
Applies a verified or unverified status to all selected member records simultaneously. Members with verified status display a verification badge on their public profile.
Reference:
How To Verify A Listing
3. Update Listing Type
Updates the Listing Type designation for all selected member records. Two Listing Type options are available:
Listing Type
Profile Display
URL Format
Individual
Member's first and last name
Based on first and last name (e.g.,
/john-doe
)
Company
Company name
Based on company name (e.g.,
/doe-consulting-group
)
This setting controls both how a member's identity is displayed on their public profile and how the profile URL slug is generated.
URL Update Option
When applying a Listing Type change via bulk action, the system presents an option to
update the profile URLs
to reflect the new Listing Type.
When this option regenerates profile URLs, the current formatting rules apply to the name: apostrophes are removed, most other punctuation and spaces become hyphens, and underscores are preserved. Existing URLs are not rewritten merely because a platform update was released. See
How To Customize The Member Profile URL Structure
for the formatting examples and URL lock behavior.
⚠ CAUTION — URL Change Behavior:
If the URL update option is selected, the system will automatically generate a 301 redirect from each affected member's old profile URL to the new URL. This preserves SEO value and prevents broken links. However, if external systems, marketing materials, or third-party integrations reference the old URLs directly, those references will need to be updated manually. The 301 redirect handles browser and search engine traffic but does not update hardcoded references outside the platform.
⚠ CAUTION — Company Name Field Required for Company Listing Type:
If the Listing Type is changed to Company but the member record does not have a Company Name populated, the URL generation will fail to produce a meaningful slug. Verify that all selected members have a Company Name on file before bulk-updating to Company Listing Type.
4. Update Top-Level Category
Reassigns the top-level member category for all selected member records simultaneously. The available categories are drawn from the list configured under
My Members » Member Categories
.
5. Update All Category Levels
Reass
igns one or more category levels for
all selected member records
simultaneously. When this action is
selected, a configuration module
appears presenting the following three
category fields:
#
Field
Description
1
Top-Level Category
Reassigns the primary top-level category for all selected members.
2
Sub-Category
Reassigns the sub-category for all selected members.
3
Sub-Sub-Category
Reassigns the sub-sub-category for all selected members.
Only the fields that require updating need to be populated. Fields left blank in the module are ignored, the corresponding category level on each selected member record remains unchanged.
6. Update Join Date
Modifies the recorded join date for all selected member records simultaneously.
⚠ NOTE — Applies to All Selected Members:
This action sets a single join date value across all selected records. There is no per-member date assignment within a single bulk action. To assign different join dates to different members, separate bulk action operations must be run for each distinct date value.
7. Update Membership Plan
Reassigns the Membership Plan for all selected member records simultaneously.
⚠ CRITICAL CAUTION — Plan Change Does Not Affect Billing:
Changing the Membership Plan via bulk action does NOT modify or cancel any existing subscription associated with the selected members. The plan designation in the member record will change, but subscription billing continues under the original plan terms unless separately updated in the subscription management system.
8. Add/Remove Tags
Adds or removes
Member Tags
for all selected member records simultaneously. The administrator selects whether the operation is an addition or removal, then selects the specific tag or tags to apply.
9. Add/Remove Credits
Adjusts the credit balance for all selected member records simultaneously. The administrator specifies whether the operation adds or removes credits and enters the credit amount to apply.
10. Change Post Ownership
Reassigns all posts owned by the selected member records to a different specified member. This action transfers content ownership in bulk and does not delete any posts.
11. Change Parent Member
⚠ ADD-ON REQUIRED — Multi-Member Manager:
This action is only available when the
Multi-Member Manager
add-on is active on the site. If this add-on is not active, the Change Parent Member option will not appear in the Bulk Actions dropdown.
When available, this action assigns a new parent member to all selected member records, or removes the existing parent assignment. This converts the selected members into sub-accounts under the designated parent, or returns them to standalone account status.
⚠ CRITICAL CAUTION — Eligibility Restriction for Parent Assignment:
Only Active members who share the same Membership Plan AND have the "Sub Accounts" feature enabled in their plan settings are eligible to be assigned as a parent. Members not meeting both criteria will not appear as assignable parent options.
Reference:
Multi-Member Manager
12. Delete Members
Permanently deletes all selected member records. When the Delete Members action is selected, a configuration modal appears before any deletion is executed. The following options must be reviewed and set before confirming the action:
#
Option
Description
1
Delete Members
Toggle must be enabled to confirm the deletion action.
2
Delete Sub-Accounts Under Members?
If selected members have associated sub-accounts, the administrator chooses whether to delete or retain them.
3
Delete Member Profile Images & Files?
Determines whether images and files attached to the selected member records are also permanently deleted.
4
Delete Member Posts?
Determines whether posts created by the selected members are deleted or retained.
5
Reassign Posts to Another Member
If posts are being retained rather than deleted, this option transfers them to a designated existing member.
After all options are configured, a
final confirmation prompt
is displayed before the deletion is executed.

title: Adding Google Tag Manager and Google Tags
content:
Google Tag Manager is a tag management system (TMS) that can be used to quickly and easily update measurement codes and related code fragments, collectively known as tags, on a website or mobile app. It is not a tracking system itself. To set up data tracking, first
Install Google Analytics 4.
To learn more please refer to the following Google document:
Tag Manager overview
To get started with Google Tag Manager:
https://developers.google.com/tag-manager/quickstart
NOTE: This setup needs a GTM (Google Tag Manager) ID, which can be created by following these instructions:
Set up and install Tag Manager
Creating the Container
In Tag Manager, click on the body to create a container:
Name the container, select the
Web
option, and click
Create
:
This displays the two sections of code that need to be added to the website:
Step 1: Add the Script Code to the HEAD Section
The first part of the code goes in the HEAD section. To add it, go to:
Settings > Design Settings > Custom CSS/HEAD > Additional HEAD Code:
The code looks like this (replace GTM-XXXXXX with the container ID):
<!-- Google Tag Manager -->
<script>(function(w,d,s,l,i){w[l]=w[l]||[];w[l].push({'gtm.start':
new Date().getTime(),event:'gtm.js'});var f=d.getElementsByTagName(s)[0],
j=d.createElement(s),dl=l!='dataLayer'?'&l='+l:'';j.async=true;j.src=
'
https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtm.js?id='+i+dl;f.parentNode.insertBefore(j,f)
;
})(window,document,'script','dataLayer','GTM-XXXXXX');</script>
<!-- End Google Tag Manager -->
Step 2: Add the Noscript Code to the Tag Manager Widget
The second part of the code is added through a widget called
Bootstrap Theme - Google Tag Manager Code
. To edit this widget and add the code, go to:
Toolbox >> Widget Manager >> search for "Bootstrap Theme - Google Tag Manager Code" >> Edit:
The code has the following format (replace GTM-XXXXXX with the container ID):
<!-- Google Tag Manager (noscript) -->
<noscript><iframe src="
https://www.googletagmanager.com/ns.html?id=GTM-XXXXXX
"
height="0" width="0" style="display:none;visibility:hidden"></iframe></noscript>
<!-- End Google Tag Manager (noscript) -->
Publishing the Container
After placing the code, click
Submit
in Tag Manager:
And click on Publish after it:
Troubleshooting
If Google Tag Manager is not working as expected after following these instructions, use
Google Tag Assistant
to check for errors with the Tag Manager code added to the site and review possible solutions.

title: How To Customize The Post URL Structure
content:
By default the URL structure of a post is:
post type / post title
The way to customize this structure is by navigating to Settings >> Advanced Settings and searching for the advanced setting:
Post URL Structure
System Variable:
post_url_structure
To add a new value select the plus sign next to the variable name:
To modify the structure of the URL drag and drop each variable to the desired place:
Once the Post URL structure is customized, click Save to apply it to newly generated post URLs.
Important:
Changing this setting does not immediately rewrite every existing post URL. The structure applies to new posts and when an existing post URL is regenerated through the standard post update process.
How Post Titles Become URLs
When the system generates a URL from a post title, it formats the name or title for use in the URL:
Straight and curly apostrophes are removed.
Most other punctuation, symbols, and spaces become hyphens. Repeated hyphens are combined into a single hyphen.
Underscores are preserved.
Accented and non-Latin letters retain their existing handling. Some characters may appear as percent-encoded values in a copied URL.
Original post title
Generated name or title portion
Ruby’s Clay Studio
rubys-clay-studio
Ruby's Clay Studio
rubys-clay-studio
Art • Studio
art-studio
Studio_Name
studio_name
These examples show only the name or title portion. The full URL also follows the configured URL structure, and a duplicate URL may require an additional identifier.
Existing and Custom Post URLs
The formatting rules apply when a post URL is generated or regenerated. A platform update does not automatically rewrite all stored post URLs.
Automatically generated URLs follow the configured structure. A manually customized post URL is a separate choice; changing the default structure should not be used as a way to replace every custom URL. For individual URL changes and the associated redirect behavior, see
How to Manually Edit the URL / Filename of Posts
.

title: Admin Sessions
content:
This article explains how to view and manage active admin sessions from the
Admin Accounts
section of the admin area.
Admin sessions show when an admin account is currently logged in, when the account was last active, and how many active sessions are connected to that admin account.
Overview
Admin sessions help website owners and authorized admins monitor admin account access. This is useful when an admin password has been changed, an admin account may have been accessed from an unknown device, or an admin should be logged out of all active sessions.
Changing the password from the Account Dashboard's
Change Password
page signs the admin out of every session. A password changed any other way, such as through a
forgot password
email link, may not end sessions that are already signed in. The admin session tools make it possible to log out active sessions for an admin account in that case.
How to Access Admin Sessions
Go to
Settings >> Admin Accounts
.
Find the admin account that should be reviewed.
Use the account information shown in the admin account row to review the admin’s recent activity.
Use the
Actions
dropdown (marked 1 in the screenshot below) to reach the session options (marked 2):
Logout All Sessions
and
Show Active Sessions
.
Admin Account Session Details
The
Admin Accounts
page displays useful account and session details for each admin account. The numbers in the screenshot below match this list. Available details may include:
Status:
Shows whether the admin account is active.
Email Address:
Shows the email address connected to the admin account.
Last Active:
Shows the most recent activity timestamp for the admin account.
Last Active IP:
Shows the IP address from the admin’s most recent activity.
Default Login Website:
Shows the default website connected to the admin account.
Logged In:
Shows how many active sessions the admin currently has on the website.
Admin Role:
Shows the admin role assigned to the account.
Logged In Sessions
The
Logged In
value shows how many active sessions are currently connected to the admin account.
For example:
Logged In: 1 Session
This means the admin account currently has one active session on the website.
If the admin is logged in from multiple browsers, devices, or locations, more than one session may display.
Last Active
The
Last Active
timestamp shows the most recent activity recorded for the admin account. This can help confirm when an admin account was last used in the admin area.
If the timestamp or activity looks unfamiliar, the website owner or authorized admin may want to review the account, change the password, and log out active sessions.
Last Active IP
The
Last Active IP
value shows the IP address connected to the admin’s most recent activity. This can be used as an additional reference when reviewing admin account access.
Note:
IP addresses can change depending on the admin’s network, device, location, VPN, or internet provider.
Show Active Sessions
The
Show Active Sessions
option displays active session details for the selected admin account.
To view active sessions:
Go to
Settings >> Admin Accounts
.
Find the admin account that should be reviewed.
Click the
Actions
dropdown for that admin.
Select
Show Active Sessions
.
The
Logged in Session List
popup opens with the number of active sessions in its title. Each row is one active session, with these columns:
Website:
The Site ID and domain the session is signed in to. The session being used to view the list is highlighted and labelled
Current Session
.
Browser:
The browser the session was opened in, such as Chrome.
IP Address:
The IP address the session signed in from.
Date:
The
Login Date
(when the session signed in) and the
Last Active Date
(the most recent activity in that session).
Log out:
Ends that one session and removes its row from the list.
Session Times and the Website Time Zone
The
Login Date
and
Last Active Date
(1) are shown in the website’s own time zone, followed by the time zone abbreviation, for example
2026-09-23 17:10:16 PDT
on a Pacific Time website or
EDT
on an Eastern Time website. The time zone comes from the
Website Time Zone
setting under
Settings >> General Settings >> Localization
, the same clock shown as
Website Time
at the top of the admin area.
A session’s
Login Date
should match the time the admin actually logged in, converted to the website’s time zone. The
Last Active
value on the Admin Accounts page uses the same clock, so it matches the
Last Active Date
of the most recent session.
Tip: checking an unfamiliar session.
Before treating a session as someone else’s login, compare its
Login Date
with when the admin remembers logging in, keeping in mind the time zone shown after the time, and compare its
Browser
and
IP Address
with the admin’s own devices. If the session is still unexplained, change the admin’s password and use
Log out
(2) or
Logout All Sessions
.
Logout All Sessions
The
Logout All Sessions
option logs the selected admin account out of all active sessions. This is useful when an admin password has been changed, a device should no longer stay logged in, or the admin account may have been accessed by an unwanted user.
To log out all active sessions for an admin:
Go to
Settings >> Admin Accounts
.
Find the admin account that should be logged out.
Click the
Actions
dropdown for that admin.
Select
Logout All Sessions
.
Confirm the action when prompted.
After this action is completed, the selected admin account will be logged out of all active sessions. The admin will need to log in again to access the admin area.
When to Logout All Sessions
Logging out all admin sessions is recommended in situations where access should be reset or secured.
Common examples include:
An admin password was changed after a security concern.
An admin account was accessed from an unfamiliar device or location.
An admin forgot to log out on a shared or public device.
An admin should no longer remain logged in after permissions were changed.
An admin account appears to have more active sessions than expected.
Activity Tracker
Admin session activity can also be reviewed from the Activity Tracker.
Website Notifications / Activity Tracker
To review admin-related activity:
Go to
Dashboard >> Activity Tracker
.
Use the
Admin Area
filter to view admin-related activity.
Use the keyword search to filter by
Admin Account
, when needed.
The Activity Tracker can help review admin activity connected to logins, sessions, and admin-area actions.
Important Notes
Changing the password from the Account Dashboard's
Change Password
page signs the admin out of every session. A password changed another way may not end existing sessions.
Use
Logout All Sessions
to force an admin account to log out of all active sessions.
The
Logged In
value shows how many active sessions are currently connected to the admin account.
The
Last Active
timestamp shows the most recent activity recorded for the admin account.
The
Last Active IP
value can help identify recent access, but IP addresses may change depending on the admin’s network or location.
Admin session activity can also be reviewed from the Activity Tracker.

title: Getting Stripe Credentials - Existing Account
content:
If the Stripe account has been created and the credentials need to be added to the admin, then follow the steps in this article.
When the new Secret Key has been rolled out, go to the admin and navigate to Finance >> Payment Settings >> Stripe and paste the Publishable and Secret keys here:
Important Notes
The name that appears on a member's credit card statement can be edited on the Statement Descriptor section above. Must be between 5 - 22 characters, have at least one letter, and cannot contain the following characters: < > \ ' " *
When adding credentials for Stripe gateway, there will be additional validation on each key field as the valid credentials should be between 25 and 255 characters, and the key cannot include dots (ex: ....).
In the "Secret or Restricted Key" field, you can enter either a standard Secret Key (beginning with sk_) or a Restricted Key (beginning with rk_).
There are two types of API keys: Publishable and Secret.
Publishable API keys
are meant solely to identify the account with Stripe, they aren’t secret.
Secret API keys
should be kept confidential. The account’s secret API key can perform any API request to Stripe without restriction.
Create Stripe Account
If the Stripe account needs to be created for the first time, then follow the steps on this other article:
Setting Up A New Stripe Account
Stripe Test and Live Modes
In
test mode
, payments are not processed by card networks or payment providers, and only Stripe test payment information can be used.
Genuine card information
cannot
be used in
test mode
. Instead, use any of the following test card numbers, valid expiration date in the future, and any random CVC number, to create a successful payment.
Stripe test cards can be found here:
https://stripe.com/docs/testing
Each basic test card’s billing country is set to the U.S. If need to create test card payments using cards for other billing countries, use the
international test cards
.
In
Live mode
, payments are processed by card networks and members can use real cards.
Obtaining the API Keys
The API keys are always available in the
Dashboard
.
In
TEST
mode, secret keys are always visible and you can just copy and paste them in the BD admin.
In order to copy a key, hover over it and click on "Click to copy"
In
LIVE
mode, new secret keys are
only visible the first time
the owner accesses them. After that, the Dashboard redacts the API key.
Roll Key
If the secret key is lost, it cannot be recovered from the Dashboard, so the owner must roll the key or create another one.
In order to roll a new key refer to the article down below:
Stripe Credentials - How To Roll Key
Setting up a Payment Gateway
To learn more about how to complete this process, use the following article for reference:
Finance » Payment Settings - Setting Up A Payment Gateway

title: Set Up The WWW or Non-WWW Version Of The Domain
content:
Set the WWW or Non-WWW Version of a Domain
A live domain can display either
www.example.com
or
example.com
as its preferred public address. Visitors to the other version are redirected to the selected style.
Change the Setting in Domain Manager
Open
Settings > Domain Manager > Domain
.
Find
Web address style
.
Select
Change
.
Choose
With www.
or
Without www.
, then click
Save this style
. Links across the website are rewritten, and the website stays online throughout.
Without www.
can be saved only when the address without www (such as
example.com
) already reaches the website. Until it does, Domain Manager explains what to point first and keeps the www version. A forwarding rule at the registrar does not meet this requirement, because it would send visitors back and forth between the two addresses; point the root domain itself at the website instead.
The connection wizard asks the same question during
Check It
. On the
A domain name I own
route,
How should your address appear?
appears under the address box as soon as a root domain such as
example.com
is typed, with or without www. The domain is always connected as
www.example.com
; the choice decides which version visitors land on. If
Without www.
is chosen but the root domain does not reach the website when the switch runs, the website stays on the www version and Domain Manager says so. A domain selected from a connected Cloudflare account uses its www address; change it here afterwards if needed. The choice is not shown for a true subdomain such as
members.example.com
.
The Web address style dialog offers the www and non-www versions of the connected domain.
Alternative: URL Rules
The preferred version can also be changed from the existing URL Rules setting in Advanced Settings. Search for
WWW or Non-WWW
or the system variable
preferred_domain
, select the preferred style, save the change, and refresh the
HTAccess File
if that screen instructs it.

title: Pay Per Post
content:
The Pay Per Post add-on allows the admin to charge members a set price each time they publish content to the website. Pay-per-post prices can be set per membership level.
Pay Per Post is a great way to grow the site's community while being profitable. The admin can offer free memberships while still generating revenue each time the free members publish content.

Join The VIP Add-Ons Club
Purchase Individually:
Pay Per Post Add-On
Enabling the Add-On
1. Go to
Finance - Membership Plans
:
2. Select the membership level to modify:
3. Click on the Post Publishing tab to see all the available features.
Scroll down to the post type and set a price amount, h
ere the admin can add the price that members will pay per post:
Price/Extra Post: Minimum value must be 1.
Here are the 3 options for the admin:
Free and Paid Posts (to use this option, the
Limit Posts Per Member
add-on is needed)
Only Paid Posts. No Free Posts
Only Free Posts. No Paid Posts
Note
: If the "Only Free Posts. No Paid Posts" option is set, the system won't let the admin select how many free Post can be published.
Purchasing Posts
When users have free post the system will inform them how many they can post:
Once the free post limit has been reached or if all posts are paid, the member will be prompted to purchase the post:
Before the content can be added, the user will be able to
Review Order
:
If the member doesn't have a CC on file, the form to add it will appear:
If the card is on file, click on "
Yes, continue with purchase
" to complete the purchase:
Unpublishing a Post
If a post that has already been paid for is unpublished, the payment remains as a credit and can be used to publish a new post. The credit will appear alongside the “New Article” button.
Admin Moderation
When the
Advanced Post Moderation Add-on
is active on the website, the admin will have the option to override the limit. If the post or posts that are about to be approved go over the member limit, a warning will display to inform the admin about this:

title: Admin Bar
content:
The Admin Bar is a tool that helps the website administrator to easily make updates on the front end of the site. It is also useful to pinpoint important elements like forms, widgets, SEO Templates and sidebars and text labels.
To locate the Admin Bar, login into the admin and click on the
"Visit Website"
button:
This will redirect the admin to the Homepage and the admin bar will show:
Click on the dropdown button to make the bar wider:
Available Tools
The available tools in the bar are described below:
1. Website Dashboard
By clicking on this option, the admin will be redirected to the back-end dashboard:
2. Go To Widget Manager
This option will open up the widget manager section.
More information is available in the following article:
Toolbox » Widget Manager Overview
3. Edit Static P
age / Add Custom Content
The third option in the Admin Bar changes based on the type of page currently active.
Static Pages - Edit Static Page
On a
Static Page
, select “Edit Static Page” to modify the page that’s currently displayed.
Dynamic Pages - Add Custom Content
When viewing a dynamic page like a member search results page or a post  search results page, the Admin Bar will display the option to add custom content to  to the search results page and an option to edit it. This option only appears for dynamic pages, such as search results.
By selecting the option to Add custom content the
Quick Create Wizard - Create Web Page
starts.
More information is available in the following articles:
Adding SEO & Content To A Specific Member Search Results Page - Turn Dynamic Pages Into Static Pages
How to Turn Posts and Post Categories Search Results Pages into Static Pages
4.
S
how Widgets
Click on the magnifying glass icon to see all the widgets that are being used on the current page. This view will also include text labels, forms, menus and sidebars. Default widgets will be highlighted in red and Custom items will appear in blue. Click on awidget to open it on the Widget Manager.
More information is available in the following article:
How to Locate Widgets, Sidebars, Menus, and Forms Via Admin Bar
5. Show Text Labels
This option will highlight the text labels and allow the admin to edit them.
More information is available in the following article:
How to Locate Text Labels on the Front End of a Website
6. Design View
This tool allows to make edits on the go! With this new tool make design changes and see them right away!
More information is available in the following article:
Front End Live Design Tool
7. Edit Listing
While looking a member profile, the admin can choose this option and it will be redirect to the member dashboard.
8. Refresh Live Website
Use this option to make sure that recent changes that have been made to widgets, forms, and other elements of the website through the Admin Area are reflected in the website's cache.
More information is available in the following article:
Refresh Live Website: How To Refresh The Cache Of The Website
9. Exit Admin View
Select this to close the admin bar.
10. Edit Post
When viewing a post details page, the admin bar displays an additional option to "
Edit Post
".
This button redirects the admin to the member’s profile, landing directly on the post form for quicker access.
Admin Role Permissions
Role Permissions
will be reflected when using the Admin Bar. This applies for all Admin Bar options, the permission needs to be enabled in order to access/see the button.
In this example the
Web Page
,
SEO Template
,
Text Labels
and
Design Settings
options are missing.

title: Account Dashboard: Activate Site
content:
When logged into the Account Dashboard, all licenses that have been purchased but are not yet activated, will display on the
Ready to Activate
tab.
Inactive / Archived Sites Section
– Displays websites that are not currently active and require activation or restoration.
Site ID Badge
– Displays the unique Site ID assigned to the website.
Status Label
– Displays the current site status (e.g., Archived) along with the archive date when applicable.
Website Name
– Displays the internal website name.
Website URL
– Displays the primary domain associated with the website (if available).
Plan Label
– Displays the associated subscription plan (e.g., Lifetime Plan).
Add-Ons Indicators
– Displays active add-ons associated with the website (e.g., VIP Add-Ons Club, Instant Business Records).
Creation Date
– Displays the original website creation date when available.
Activate Site Section
Activate Site Button
– Initiates the site activation process for websites eligible for activation (e.g., Lifetime Plan sites).
Activation Process
– Re-enables the website and makes it accessible under the associated plan configuration.
Restore Site Section
Restore Button (Dropdown)
– Initiates the restoration process for archived websites.
Restore Process
– Reinstates the archived website to active status, preserving previous configuration and associated data where applicable.
There are two reasons an account will have
Websites to Activate
. The first reason is it's a brand new, recently purchase license that has not yet been activated.
The second reason is a previously-active website has been converted into a credit because it has not been actively used for a long time, or the license owner requested it be converted to a credit.
Activate Site
Credits related to a license that has never been used for an active website will not have a backup of a previous website associated with it.  In these cases, the purple button will have a single option: "Activate Site":
*Clicking on this button will launch a new website.
Credits Related to a Previously Active Website
When a previously active website is converted to a credit, a full backup of the site is made first, and will be available for up to one year from the date it was converted to a credit.
If a credit is related to one of these websites, the green button will be a dropdown with the following options:
Restore Website from Backup
Choosing this option will re-launch the website exactly as it was before it was converted to a credit.
Launch New Site
Choosing this option will delete the backup of the previous website and launch a brand new website. Select this option if the previous site is no longer needed and a brand new website should be launched instead.
Upgrade Existing Site
This will use any back up saved on file.
Launch New Website
Select from any of the available themes (optional).
Contact Support
Choosing this option will allow the site owner to submit a support ticket for additional assistance.

title: Difference Between On-Site and Off-Site Payment Gateways
content:
Brilliant Directories platform offers several integrated payment gateways including the most popular and globally accepted – PayPal, Stripe, 2Checkout, Authorize.NET, & more.
These gateways can be separated into two groups;
On-Site Payment Gateways
and
Off-Site Payment Gateways
.
Functionality Differences
Here's how On-Site and Off-Site Payment Gateways differ in terms of functionality and user experience:
On-Site Gateways allow all transactions to be completed without leaving the website, while Off-Site Gateways require the user to be redirected to the payment gateway's website to complete transactions.
On-Site Gateways
will automatically bill member credit cards for recurring subscriptions, while Off-Site Gateways require members to manually pay for each invoice.
On-site Gateways allow the Admin of a site to manually attempt to collect on invoices, while Off-Site Gateways do not allow for this functionality.
On-Site Gateways allow a member to store a credit card on file with the site, while Off-Site Gateways do not.

title: Beginner’s Guide to Troubleshooting Website Errors
content:
In this article, we will be going over the most common troubleshooting steps a site owner can follow in case experiencing an issue or when updates are not displaying on the front-end right away.
Most of these errors can be solved by following these troubleshooting steps:
Refresh The Live Website
To make sure the website is not serving a cached version, utilize the built-in
Refresh Live Website
tool that every Brilliant Directories site offer. Refreshing the cache of the website makes sure that recent changes that have been made to widgets, forms, and other elements of the website through the Admin Area are reflected in the website's cache.
Important Note:
We highly recommend refreshing the live website after following any of the troubleshooting steps specified down below.
Clear Browser Cache
The browsers may not realize the changes made on the website right away and this might cause them to display an older version of the website.
In these instances, clearing the cache of the browser will ensure users that they are seeing the latest version of the website.
To learn how to clear cache for browsers, refer to the article down below:
Clearing Cache & Cookies for Browsers
Disable Browser Plugins
In instances where the issue can be experienced on one browser but not on others, the issue might be caused by the browser extensions that may be active. One of the most common extensions that are known to cause issues on Brilliant Directories sites would be Grammarly.
To learn how to disable the browser plugins, refer to the 3rd party article down below:
How To Disable Plugins/Add-Ons/Extensions In Multiple Browsers
Disable All Custom Widgets
It is often that the issue being reported may be caused by a default widget that is customized or a brand new widget created by a site owner.
To make sure if a custom widget(s) is causing the issue or not, follow the steps down below to learn how to disable them:
How To Disable/Enable A Widget
The above documentation shows how to disable/enable a widget one by one which can be helpful in the instances where there are not many custom widgets. If there are pages of custom widgets, the best approach would be taking bulk action on them:
Bulk Actions For Widgets
To learn more detailed information about how to troubleshoot widgets, refer to the article down below:
Steps To Identify Which Custom Widget/Code Is Causing An Issue
Remove Any Code From Custom CSS / HEAD Section Temporarily
The Custom CSS / HEAD section is part of the design settings where custom CSS, HEAD and Footer code can be added to the website.
There may be instances where the issue is caused due the to code added in this area. To troubleshoot this, temporarily remove all the code added to each of these sections and save the changes. Make sure to save the code added to a text editor before deleting them.
Backup and Delete .htaccess File
A bad .htaccess file may cause server issues on websites. To troubleshoot this, access to the
.htaccess
file under Developer Hub and temporarily delete all the code added:
After deleting the code, click on the Restore Default and Save Changes.
How to Get Better Support
If following the steps specified above do not resolve the issue, we highly recommend submitting a ticket to
support@brilliantdirectories.com
or via
HERE
.  Here is how to write a better support request:
Always be polite and no matter how upset or frustrated the situation may be, do not use harsh language
Provide step by step guide on how to replicate the issue
Include an URL of the pages where the issue can be experienced
Include screenshots or screen recordings showing and explaining the issue
Describe the troubleshooting steps taken so far
When the problem cannot be reproduced by the support team (EG a button that does nothing or a save that silently fails), attach a HAR file and a Console screenshot from the affected browser, as explained in
How to Capture a HAR File and Console Screenshot for Support

title: How to Display Additional Member Information in the Member Search Results (Position, Top Category & Sub Categories)
content:
Overview
By default,
each member card in the search results
displays the following information:
Star Rating
— displayed when the
member has received at least one
rating.
Short Description or About Snippet
— a brief text summary pulled from the
member's profile.
Phone Number
—
displayed when the member's Membership
Plan is configured to show it.
Badges
— displayed when the member
is verified, has a plan-level search
results badge, or is listed in all
locations.
Three additional fields can
be enabled through Advanced Settings to
display further member information
within each search result card:
Position
— the member's job title
or role.
Top-Level Category
—
the member's primary category.
Sub-Categories
— the member's
specialties or sub-level categories.
Part 1 — Default Search Result Fields
Star Rating
A star rating is displayed on the member's search result card when the member has received at least one review rating. If no ratings exist for the member, this field does not appear.
Short Description or About Snippet
The
Short Description
field is available within the member's Contact Details form. When populated, its content is displayed in the member's search result card.
If the
Short Description
field is left blank, the system automatically falls back to displaying a snippet from the member's
About
section instead.
If both the Short Description and About fields are empty, no text snippet is displayed in the search result card.
Phone Number
The phone number is displayed on the search result card when the member's Membership Plan is configured to show it. Clicking the phone number button initiates a call attempt on the visitor's device.
⚠ NOTE — Phone Number Visibility Is Controlled by Membership Plan:
The phone number field will not appear in search results unless the member's assigned Membership Plan has the phone number display setting enabled. This is configured at the plan level, not at the individual member level.
Badges
Badges are displayed on a member's search result card under any of the following conditions:
The member has been set to
Verified
status.
The member's Membership Plan has a
Search Results Badge
configured.
The member is set to be
Listed in All Locations
.
References:
How to Verify a Listing
·
Member Profile Badges
·
All Locations Badge Image
Part 2 — Enabling Additional Fields in Advanced Settings
Three additional fields can be enabled to display further member information in search result cards. These settings are managed from
Advanced Settings
.
Navigation Path:
Admin Dashboard » Settings » Advanced Settings
The three settings and their system variables are:
Show Member Position In Member Search Results
Displays the member's Position (job title or role) on their search result card.
System Variable:
member_position_in_results
Show Top Category In Member Search Results
Displays the member's assigned Top-Level Category on their search result card.
System Variable:
top_category_in_results
Show Sub-Categories In Member Search Results
Displays the member's assigned Sub-Categories (Specialties) on their search result card.
System Variable:
sub_category_in_results
Part 3 — Text Labels
The text labels below control the display names used for each of the three additional fields in the search results. These are editable under Settings » Text Labels.
Reference:
Settings » Text Labels
Member Position Label
Controls the label displayed before the member's position value in the search result card.
System Variable:
search_results_position_label
Member Search Results Category Label
Controls the label displayed before the member's top-level category value in the search result card.
System Variable:
search_results_category_label
Sub-Category Labels (Specialties)
Two text labels control the display of sub-category values in the search result card, one for singular and one for plural usage.
Label
System Variable
Usage
Service
[service]
Singular label — used when one sub-category is displayed.
Service Plural
service_plural
Plural label — used when more than one sub-category is displayed.
Part 4 — If the Additional Fields Are Not Displaying
If the three additional fields enabled in Advanced Settings are not appearing in the search results, the search results code template may need to be reset to its default state.
⚠ CRITICAL CAUTION — Resetting Post Types Code:
The Reset to Default Post Types Code action restores the search results code template to its original default state. Any custom modifications previously made to the search results post type code will be overwritten. This action should only be taken after confirming that no intentional customizations exist in the current search results code, or after those customizations have been backed up.
Reference:
How to Reset to Default Post Types Code

title: Developer Hub - Webhooks
content:
Overview
Webhooks
are one of the methods that allow web applications to communicate with each other. They enable real-time data transfer between applications whenever a specific event occurs.
They also allow data to be sent to any URL endpoint. This makes it possible to send data to intermediary platforms such as Zapier, Pabbly Connect, Workato and APIFuse, to API endpoints on other platforms, or to custom endpoints configured to receive data.
On the website, a
webhook event
is the action that triggers the data to be sent, such as a form being submitted or a member changing plans. Each event has an on/off switch and a
Webhook Link
: the full address the data is sent to when the event happens.
Connections and Advanced Settings
To learn how to connect a webhook through Zapier see:
Connecting Webhook Events With Zapier
For Smart List webhooks and how to connect them see:
How To Create Smart List Webhooks
To include the member login token in outgoing webhook payloads for member-related events (new member registrations, member additions, updates, deletions, and member self-service form submissions), the advanced setting
Include Login Token in Member Webhook Payloads
must be enabled.
For the fields each webhook sends, see the
List of Variables Per Webhook
.
Opening the Webhooks Page
Go to
Developer Hub
.
On the
Manage Webhooks
card, click
Manage Webhooks
.
All / On / Off
and
Search
: the menu shows every webhook, only the ones switched on, or only the ones switched off. The search box finds webhooks by the words typed. While either is in use, a line under the search box counts the matches and offers
Clear
.
The section list. Webhooks are grouped into sections under
Default Webhooks
, and under
Custom Webhooks
once any custom webhook exists. Clicking a section jumps to it.
New Webhook
: creates a custom webhook for a specific form or Smart List. See
How To Create A Custom Webhook
.
A section with its webhooks. Each row shows the event's name, what triggers it and, for form events, the form's name.
Turning a Webhook On
The switch turns the webhook on or off.
Webhook Link
: the full address (starting with
https://
or
http://
) the data is sent to.
The copy button copies the Webhook Link. Form events also have a copy button beside the form name.
To turn a webhook on:
Switch the webhook on.
Paste the endpoint address into its
Webhook Link
.
Click
Save
in the
Unsaved changes
bar at the top of the page.
Discard
in the same bar undoes the changes instead.
A webhook that is switched on must have a Webhook Link. If the link is empty or is not a full web address, the page does not save and shows the problem under the field.
The
Unsaved changes
bar, with
Discard
and
Save
. A dot also marks each webhook that has unsaved changes.
A webhook switched on without a link:
Add a Webhook Link, or turn this webhook off.
Default Webhook Events
Here is the full list of the default webhooks on the page, by section. Where a form name is shown on the page, it is listed in brackets.
Chat Messages
Chat Message Actions
: a member chat is started, replied to or closed using the
Private Member Chat Add-On
.
Member Accounts
About Me Form Submitted
: a member submits the About Me form in the Member Dashboard [form=about].
Additional Details Form Submitted
: a member submits the Additional Details form in the Member Dashboard [form=member_listing_details].
Contact Details Form Submitted
: a member submits the Contact Details form in the Member Dashboard [form=member_contact_details].
Member Accepts / Declines Lead
: a member accepts or declines a lead in the Member Dashboard.
Members Imported / Added / Updated / Deleted Via Admin
: a member is imported by CSV file in the Admin, imported with the
Instant Business Data tool
, added manually in the Admin, updated through the
Quick Edit form
in the Admin, or deleted in the Admin.
Profile Photos Form Submitted
: a member uploads or edits their profile photo, logo or cover photo in the Member Dashboard.
Sub-Account Form Submitted
: a member creates a sub-account using the
Multi-Member Manager Add-On
[form=sub_accounts_form].
Member Posts
Photo Album Post Deleted
: a member or admin deletes a post of a Multi-Image Post Type (Photo Albums, Digital Products, Products, Classifieds, Properties).
Photo Album Post Saved
: a member adds or edits a post of a Multi-Image Post Type.
Post Comment Submitted
: a member submits a comment on a post.
Standard Post Deleted
: a member or admin deletes a post of a Single Image Post Type (Videos, Articles, Blog Articles, Jobs, Events, Coupons, Audios, Discussions).
Standard Post Saved
: a member adds or edits a post of a Single Image Post Type.
Payments & Invoices
Admin Subscription / Invoice Action
: an admin creates, updates, cancels or deletes an invoice or subscription in the Admin area.
Automatic Invoice Payment Succeeded / Failed
: the system collects, or fails to collect, a recurring subscription payment during the daily scheduled run.
Manual Invoice Payment Succeeded / Failed
: a member pays a pending or past due invoice from the Member Dashboard.
One-Time Purchase
: a member buys a Lead, a Digital Product or a Pay Per Post credit.
Sign Ups & Plan Changes
Member Account Cancelled
: a member cancels their account from the Member Dashboard.
Member Plan Changed
: a member upgrades or downgrades their Membership Plan in the Member Dashboard.
Sign Up: Email Verification Link Clicked
: a member clicks the verification link sent in the
basic-validation
email template, typically after signing up for a free plan (email variable
%confirm_link%
).
Sign Up: Free Plan
: a member signs up for a free Membership Plan on the website [form=signup_free].
Sign Up: Paid Plan (Off-Site Payment)
: a member signs up for a paid Membership Plan using an
Off-Site Payment Gateway
[form=whmcs_signup_external].
Sign Up: Paid Plan (On-Site Payment)
: a member signs up for a paid Membership Plan using an
On-Site Payment Gateway
[form=whmcs_signup_paid].
Smart Lists by Type
These webhooks send the records of every Smart List of that type when
Sync Webhook Now
is clicked on a Smart List or its schedule runs. To send one specific Smart List to its own link, create a custom webhook for it instead.
All Form Inquiries Lists
All Leads Lists
All Members Lists
All Reviews Lists
All Transactions Lists
Standard Forms
Contact Us Form Submitted
: a visitor submits the website's Contact Us form [form=contact_form].
Get Matched Lead Form Submitted
: a visitor submits the Get Matched lead form [form=bootstrap_get_match].
Member Review Form Submitted
: a visitor submits a review for a member [form=member_review].
Newsletter Form Submitted
: a visitor submits the Newsletter Signup form [form=newsletter_modal_signup].

: a visitor submits the Newsletter Unsubscribe form [form=unsubscribe_email].
Custom Webhooks
A custom webhook sends the data of one specific form, or of one specific Smart List, to its own Webhook Link. Custom versions of the member forms (EG a copy of the Contact Details, Additional Details or About forms under a different name) and custom forms are connected this way. Custom webhooks are listed under
Custom Webhooks

Forms
section and a
Smart Lists
section, and each has a menu with
Edit
and
Delete Webhook
.

title: Stripe Credentials - How to Rotate Key
content:
This article outlines the steps to roll an API key in a Stripe account. Rolling a key involves replacing the current API key with a new one to enhance security. The process includes generating a new key in the Stripe Dashboard, updating the application with the new key, and deactivating the old key once functionality is confirmed. This practice safeguards the account from unauthorized access.
Login to Your Account
Let's begin by
logging into the Stripe account first
. Look for the "Developers" view under Settings >> Developers >> Manage API Keys. Then, follow the steps below:
Step 1: Click on the three dots next to the key and click Rotate Key
Step 2: Select the time to rotate the key
We recommend selecting "
now
" if you are not using the previous API key in another application.
Step 3: Stripe will display the new API Key
VERY IMPORTANT NOTE:
This API Key must be copied from Stripe into the Brilliant Directories
Admin >> Payment Settings
or to a safe place. Stripe, for security purposes, will only display this key once. If failed to save the key as suggested, the same steps need to be repeated.

title: Connecting a Site to Cloudflare
content:
Connecting a Site to Cloudflare
Cloudflare can manage a domain's DNS while also providing caching, traffic filtering, and other performance and security services. Two connection paths are available: the guided Domain Manager option, when offered for the website, and the manual Cloudflare setup described below.
Guided Connection in Domain Manager
Open
Settings > Domain Manager
and start the domain connection flow. When
Use a domain from my Cloudflare account
appears, the flow can sign in to Cloudflare, select a domain, check it, and prepare the required record.
See
Connect and Manage Cloudflare in Domain Manager
for the guided workflow.
Select the intended Cloudflare domain and choose the main address or a subdomain before preparing the DNS records.
Manual Cloudflare Setup
Create or sign in to a Cloudflare account and add the domain.
Use Cloudflare's scan to import existing DNS records. Review every imported record before continuing, especially MX, TXT, and CNAME records used by email or other services.
Select the appropriate Cloudflare plan. The Free plan is sufficient for the basic DNS connection.
At the domain registrar, replace the current nameservers with the two nameservers assigned by Cloudflare.
Wait for Cloudflare to confirm that the zone is active.
Add the Website Records
Open
Settings > Domain Manager
. The
Domain
area and its connection guide display the exact destination required by the website. Add the root and
www
records shown by the guide. Record types can differ by provider: Cloudflare can flatten a root CNAME, while some configurations use an ALIAS-compatible root record.
Existing mail records must also remain present. These can include MX records, SPF TXT records, and sender-authentication CNAME records. Open
Emails > Sender Authentication
in Domain Manager for the website-specific authentication values. Sender-authentication records in Cloudflare must be set to
DNS only
.
Do not copy sample values from screenshots.
Every website can have a different destination and sender-authentication records. Use only the values displayed in its Domain Manager and email provider.
Review Cloudflare Settings
For a connected Domain Manager account, review the
Cloudflare
tab and its
Set recommended defaults
action. The panel brings together HTTPS, encryption, security, and page-caching controls. Review any existing custom configuration before applying defaults.
For manual changes, confirm the website's certificate and redirect behavior before changing Cloudflare encryption or HTTPS settings. Test forms, login, images, and payment pages after changes. See
Cloudflare Connection and Settings
for the Domain Manager controls.

title: Optimizing Website Performance
content:
Here at Brilliant Directories, we're continuously optimizing the software to make pages load as fast as possible without affecting functionality.  As our development team continues to release 100 - 150 new updates each month to add new functionality, make the platform easier to use, and maximize security, we always have an eye on site speed and suggestions.
We have projects on our immediate roadmap that are focused on optimizing database queries and minimizing the server response time to make pages load faster than ever and improve those scores even more. This is an aspect of the software we are always iterating on and will continue to make it a priority moving forward.
Here are some of the strategies we have implemented to optimize the performance of our sites.
Built-In Performance Measures
The platform implements several performance strategies at the core level:
Compression
: Gzip compression is enabled to reduce asset sizes.
Asset minification
: JavaScript and CSS files stored on Brilliant Directories servers are minified.
Efficient routing
: Redirects and rewrites are kept to a minimum to streamline page-load paths.
Browser caching
: Static assets are cached so that fewer resources need to be downloaded on repeat visits.
Backend optimization
: SQL queries and PHP code are refined to lower server response times.
Code refactoring
: Non-critical JavaScript is deferred where possible, reducing initial load times.
Key Factors That Influence Performance
These are some of the factors that we should have in mind when analyzing the site loading speed and a few recommendations to improve the scores if needed:
There will always be a relationship between the size and number of images on a page and the speed in which that page will load.  This can be seen in the example above, our all-in-one demo site uses a homepage slider, having several HD images that are rotating instead of just one, like the yellow pages demo to the right will impact the site loading speed. Try to always keep images within the
recommended sizes.
The more features and functionality is present, the longer the page will take to load.  Going back to the example above, our
all-in-one demo site
has more homepage streaming widgets on the homepage than our
yellow pages demo site
, this will also impact the speed at which this page loads.
Try adding and removing features or
streaming widgets
to find the right balance between page load times and the content on the page that fits the needs of the website.
Check with support to see if the website is using PHP 7 or 5.4.  Moving to PHP 7 will help with speed. This is a very seamless transition, if the site's custom widgets are compatible we recommend upgrading to the latest version of PHP.
If the site is already using PHP 7, there is one more option to optimize the site speed, which is PHP-FPM. PHP-FPM (FastCGI Process Manager) is a web tool used to speed up the performance of a website. It is much faster than traditional CGI-based methods and has the ability to handle tremendous loads simultaneously. This is still in a
beta version
, but we offer this as an option to test it out.
Let's take the last two sites we compared and add a couple of our demo sites as an example:
To better understand the comparison image here is a breakdown of what each of these sites includes.
Newly Launched Site
This site's homepage has a single static hero image, a Keyword + Location Search, and the About Website / Join Offer homepage widget.
Yellow Pages Demo
In addition to that content, the Newly Launched Site has on the homepage, this site also has the following:
Streaming Members Homepage widget
All-In-One Demo
In addition to that content, the Newly Launched Site has on the homepage, this site also has the following:
Streaming Members Homepage widget
Streaming Top Categories Homepage widget
Streaming Blog Articles with Sidebar
Optional Performance Enhancement Settings
For sites that are not performing as quickly as desired, the following strategies can provide further improvement.
Resource CDN
The advanced setting
Front-End Optimization: Enable Resource Delivery Via CDN
allows CSS / JS resources that are referenced on all pages to be served from
https://www.optimizecdn.com
. If set to OFF, the system will use relative paths from the domain, but if turned ON, it speeds up the delivery of resources vs. the relative path of the domain name.
To activate the setting, go to Settings >> Advanced Settings:
Image CDN
The
Front-End Optimization: Use Content Delivery Network (CDN) For Images
advanced setting allows user to enter a URL to use a service like imagekit.io to serve images from an image CDN with automatic optimization and real-time transformation. Images that are served from a relative path will be updated to include your inputted CDN. For example, an image that is set to /images/logo.png will be served from
https://ik.imagekit.io/your-account-id/images/logo.png
.
To activate the setting, go to Settings >> Advanced Settings:
External CDN (e.g., Cloudflare)
Another great option is to use
CDN like Cloudflare
to both reduce page load time and reduce the bandwidth used by the site.  Cloudflare caches the images and files used by the website in its servers around the world and serves those resources to users from a location close to them.  This is a free tool that can help speed up the loading of web pages for users around the world.
Front-End Optimization Features
Mobile Preloader
When the advanced setting Front-End Optimization: Mobile Preloader (front_end_optimization_mobile_preloader) is enabled, the first page visited from a mobile device will display a brief loading screen. This feature helps improve perceived page speed and performance metrics. The loading screen appears only once per device during the initial visit and does not display again while navigating the site from the same device.
An example of this behavior is illustrated in the GIF below:
To activate the setting, go to Settings >> Advanced Settings:
Lazyload iframe Embeds
The Front-End Optimization: Lazyload iframe Embeds
advanced setting defers the loading of embedded iframe content, such as videos, audio players, and social media widgets, until the visitor scrolls near the embed or interacts with it. This reduces initial page weight and improves load times, especially on content-heavy pages.
To activate the setting, go to Settings >> Advanced Settings:
Convert User Uploaded Images to WebP
The
Front-End Optimization: Convert User Uploaded Images to WebP
advanced setting automatically converts uploaded images to WebP format and optimizes them to reduce file sizes and improve performance.
When enabled, images uploaded through the member dashboard (such as profile photos, logos, and post images) are converted to WebP and compressed based on the selected quality level (default: 80%).
This setting is enabled by default and does not apply to Media Manager uploads, images added via the editor (Froala), or admin-uploaded images.
To activate the setting, go to Settings >> Advanced Settings:

title: Tracking Member Sign-Ups Events With Facebook Pixel
content:
Standard events are predefined visitor actions that correspond to common, conversion-related activities, such as searching for a product, viewing a product, or purchasing a product.
This article explains how to track completed purchases on the site.
Detailed information about conversion tracking can be found in the article below:
Conversion Tracking
Step 1:
Ensure the pixel's base code is installed on every page where conversions will be tracked. This process is explained in detail in the article below:
Facebook Pixel
Step 2:
Customize the
Bootstrap Theme - Conversion Tracking Codes
widget to call the
fbq('track')
function which tracks completed purchases on the site.
The following example code is provided by Facebook Pixel:
<script>
fbq('track', 'Purchase', {currency: "USD", value: 30.00});
</script>
The next step is to replace the specified parameter values with the default variables. All of the available variables can be found in the
Bootstrap Theme - Conversion Tracking Codes
widget:
The resulting code would look like this:
<script>
fbq('track', 'Purchase', {currency: "USD", value: <?php echo $conversion_tracking['amount']; ?>});
</script>
Then add the code to the specified widget below line 38:
When this function is called, the event is tracked as a purchase event in Events Manager:

content:

It is possible to add more than one widget from the same post type as a homepage streaming widget. This is super important when the post types were cloned and the owner of the site wants to stream the new posts on the homepage.
For example, let's say the Member Articles post type was cloned 2 times, so there are 3 posts types total:

Member Articles (Clone 1)
Member Articles (Clone 2)
In the "Select Content to Display", there is only one option to select the "Member Articles" post type. So, this will apply to one of the post types but the section cannot be cloned to add the other 2:

In order to add the other 2 post types to the homepage, some customization is required but it can be done by following the steps below:

Toolbox >> Widget Manager

Bootstrap Theme - Display - Recent Articles
" widget.

It will show the widget code, copy the name of the widget:
Bootstrap Theme - Display - Recent Articles
Then go to Toolbox >> Widget Manager >> Right-click on "Open link in
new tab
".
NOTE:
It is important to open it on a new tab because we are going to need both tabs open.

7. Go back to the first tab and copy the default code:

8. Then go to the new widget page and paste the code.

301_redirects

Developer Hub >> 301 Redirects
page in the Admin area.
admin_roles
Custom Admin Roles added through the
Admin Role Permissions
page in the Admin area.

Admin Role Permissions

category
Deprecated

Private Member Chat Add-On

title: Troubleshooting: No Sub or Sub-Sub Level Categories Displaying in the Member Dashboard Forms
content:
By default, the Sub and the Sub-Sub Level Categories will display under the Additional Details tab under Member Dashboard:
If these categories are not displaying as is shown above, this may due to a couple of reasons.
1) No Sub or Sub-Sub Level Categories Added to the Site Yet
This sounds simple but it is always a good idea to double-check if there are any Sub and the Sub-Sub Level Categories added to the site. The easiest way to check this would be under
My Members
>>
Member Categories
in the admin:
2) The Top-Level Category Member Selected Does Not Have Any Sub or Sub-Sub Level Categories Assigned
There could be a scenario where the site indeed has Sub and the Sub-Sub Level Categories but the one member selected under their Contact Details form does not.
Let's use real examples. The member down below selected the Top-Level Category called Virtual Events:
But if we use the built-in filter to search for the Sub-Level Categories with a parent category (Top-Level Category) Virtual Events, we can see that there aren't any:
Another way to visualize this would be checking the default /categories page:
3) Specialties Option Was Not Enabled Under the Membership Plan Post Publishing Tab
Under
Membership Plan settings
>>
Post Publishing
tab, "Specialties" option might not be enabled yet:
4) The Category Selection Widget Was Deleted From Listing - Additional Details - Member Form
The widget named "
Bootstrap Theme - Account - Select Categories
" can be found on the default
Listing - Additional Details - Member
form and is necessary for members to select their specialties:
5) Custom Code Related Issues
There might be an instance where the category options are not displaying due to custom code added to the site. To make sure this is not the case, please refer to the article down below that talks about the basic troubleshooting steps user can take:
Beginner’s Guide To Troubleshooting Website Errors

title: Member Credits System
content:
Incentivize members to take action by rewarding them with credits and preserve revenue by issuing credits instead of processing refunds.
Manually assign credits to member accounts or give credits to members automatically after signup or an upgrade. Credits take the form of the website’s primary currency and can be used as payment for future purchases on the site.
Easily add or deduct credits from specific members and quickly identify which member payments were made with credits – all from the website’s admin area.
How To Get This Add-On
Websites with the VIP Add-Ons Club automatically have this add-on available:
Join The VIP Add-Ons Club
Purchase Individually:
Member Credit System Add-On
How Credits work
Available credits will
automatically
be used for the member’s next payment(s)
Credits work for all purchases (renewals, upgrades, lead & post purchases, etc.)
Using the Add-on
With the Member Credits System add-on, admins can manually add or deduct credits from individual member accounts as needed.
Credits can also be automatically added to a member’s account after they sign up or upgrade to a new plan.
From the member’s perspective, credits can be used as a form of site currency to access features or make purchases, depending on how the system is set up.
Important
Locate the setting
enable_credit_system
and ensure that it is turned on:
Add & Deduct Credits
Go to
My Members » Search Members
(1) and search for the member (2):
Search for the member that will receive or be deducted credits then click on Actions > Payment History:
On the member’s
Transactions
tab, click
Credits
(1), then
Add Credit
(2). A
Deduct Credit
button also appears there when the member already has a credit balance:
A pop-up form will open with the following fields:
Credit Options:
Shows
Add Credits
or
Deduct Credits
, depending on which button was clicked.
Credit Amount
: Add the numerical value of the credits that will be applied or deducted using the website currency.
Internal Note
: Add a note for internal use, for future reference.
Automatically Add Credits After Signup Or Upgrade
Go to Finance > Membership Plans > select the plan > Edit:
Under the
Sign Ups & Upgrades
tab, scroll down to the 5 credit options:
1.
Display Available Credits Inside Member's Dashboard?
: If YES, the member will see the credit balance inside their member dashboard on the billing details page.
2.
Reward Credits to Assign After Sign Up:
Entering a value greater than $0 will assign credits to this member after successful sign-up. There is a checkbox with the option to only assign credits when referred by another member.
3.
Reward Credits After Successful Membership Plan Change:
Entering a value greater than $0 will assign credits that will be added to the member’s account after they change to this plan from inside their member dashboard area.
4.
Assign Referral Credits to Members Who Refer New Sign Ups:
If enabled, an input field on sign-up pages to enter a referring member's ID number:
5.
Credits Assigned to Referring Member:
Entering a value greater than $0 will add credits to the
referring
member's account for new member sign-ups who use the referring member ID number.
Important Note:
Credits can't be assigned or awarded for "completed tasks" like filling out forms, publishing posts or uploading documents, etc.
Credits for Digital Products
In combination with the
Sell Digital Products & Services add-on
, the admin will have two additional fields in the Digital Products form:
Credits to Add After Initial Purchase (1):
Buyers will receive this credit amount one time after initial purchase. Leave blank if no credits are granted.
Allow Use of Existing Credits for Purchase? (2):
Select 'Yes' to allow buyers to use existing credits towards this purchase, or 'No' to require the use of a payment method.
Search For Members with Credits
To look for members that have credits available in their profile go to
My Members » Search Members
(1), open
Transaction Types
(2), tick
Credits Available
(3) and click
Search Members
(4):
Member credit balances can also be included in a member export: select the
member_credit_balance
field when exporting from Search Members. See
Export Member Data
.
Credits History
For the member to see the available credits, the
option
Display Available Credits Inside Member's Dashboard?
needs to be set to YES (1) in their Membership Plan:
These members will be able to see the number of credits available in their Billing Information section (1) and see the historical usage of the credits in the
Credits History
tab (2).
The
Payment History
,
Subscriptions
and
Credits History
tabs only appear when the advanced setting
Enable Member Account Billing History
(
enable_member_billing_history
) is turned on.
Log in as a member >Account > Billing Information
Credits Usage
Available credits will
automatically
be used for the member’s next payment(s)
Credits work for all purchases (renewals, upgrades, leads, digital products, post purchases, etc.)
This means that the next purchase that this member tries to process will automatically use the credits available.
If the amount of credits cover the full amount of the renewal, upgrade, post or lead purchase it will automatically be deducted.
Example #1
A member has 3.00 in credits and wants to publish an article that costs 1.00. The
Review Order
