This setting allows the administrator to set the title for the recent reviews section. The title can be customized by entering the desired text in the provided input field.
2. Title Color
The title color setting enables the customization of the title's color. Administrators can choose a color by inputting the desired color code or using the color picker tool provided.
3. Display Options
This setting controls the number of recent member reviews displayed. Administrators can select from a range of options, from 1 to 24 results. Additionally, the layout can be adjusted to show a specific number of results per row, ranging from 2 to 4 results per row.
4. Enable Carousel Slider
The carousel slider option allows recent member reviews to be displayed in a sliding carousel format. This can be toggled on or off using the provided dropdown menu.
5. Hide On Mobile
This setting allows administrators to choose whether the recent member reviews section should be hidden on mobile devices. It can be enabled or disabled using the dropdown menu.
6. Only Show Members With Photo
Administrators can choose to display only those members who have a profile photo. This setting ensures that members without photos are excluded from the recent member reviews list.
7. Show "View All" Button
The "View All" button allows users to see all recent member reviews. This setting can be toggled on or off using the dropdown menu.
8. Hide If No Posts Exist
This setting allows administrators to choose whether the recent member reviews section should be hidden if no posts exist. It can be enabled or disabled using the dropdown menu.
9. Only Include Posts from Active Members
This setting specifies whether only posts from active members should be included. Administrators can choose to include posts from active members only or from all members.
10. Include Posts from Non-Searchable Members
This setting allows administrators to choose whether to include posts from non-searchable members. It can be enabled or disabled using the dropdown menu.
11. Include Posts from Members in These Plans
This setting allows administrators to limit the displayed posts to specific membership plans. Administrators can select the desired membership plans from the provided list.
12. Limit One Review per Member?
This setting specifies whether only one review per member should be displayed. Administrators can choose to display one review per member or allow multiple reviews from the same member.
13. Display Order
The display order setting determines the order in which recent member reviews are shown. Options include newest reviews first, newest reviews last, and random order. This can be customized by selecting the desired option from the dropdown menu.

to the Admin
Dashboard

Start Here
section

title: Dedicated Server Hosting
content:
Not everyone needs enterprise-level hosting, but if your website traffic is increasing, we have premium hosting solutions to scale with your business needs.
Get This Service
Visit our website:
Dedicated Server Hosting
Pricing
Here are the pricing details, along with a brief explanation of what is included with each server option.
Dedicated
Server Specs
Server CPU: 8 Core Intel Xeon 2620v4
Server RAM: 16 GB

Ideal For Up To: 10 Websites †

Enterprise Server Specs

Server Bandwidth: 15 TB / Month*
Dedicated IP: 1 IPv4 Address / Server
Ideal For Up To: 50 Websites †
Included SSLs: 10 SSLs for 10 Websites
Your own dedicated server for use with up to 10 websites.
Upgraded hardware compared to Dedicated Server: Dual 8 Core Xeon CPU, 2X more RAM and faster SSD storage.
Important Notes
Each Dedicated Server and Enterprise Server has a one-time setup fee of $247, regardless of configuration. Transfer of your website(s) from our standard website hosting to your dedicated server typically takes 5–10 business days.
* Additional bandwidth usage for Dedicated Servers or Enterprise Servers surpassing the 15 TB monthly limit is charged at a rate of $0.09 / GB.
† The number of websites hosted on each Dedicated Server or Enterprise Server is dependent on total server bandwidth usage. Greater usage may result in fewer website properties per server. Cancellation of a Dedicated Server or Enterprise Server hosting plan requires 30 days notice. Dedicated Servers and Enterprise Servers must be purchased for a minimum of 3 months.
Premium Hosting Benefits
Cost Efficient
You can save money by having your own dedicated server with a large allocation of storage space and bandwidth that you can grow into, rather than pay for additional bandwidth allocation for your sites without any of the other advantages.
Uptime + Security
With a dedicated server your websites are completely isolated from other websites. That means if something goes wrong on a website in the standard hosting environment it will not impact the websites on your server, reducing the risk of downtime & security issues.
Faster Load Times
Websites load faster. All server resources will be dedicated to serving your websites – no other websites will be sharing the resources as they do in our standard website hosting.
High Bandwidth
Dedicated Servers and Enterprise Servers comes with a total allocation of 15 TB of bandwidth per month, which should cover significant growth for all of your sites without paying anything extra.
General Information
24/7 Monitoring
All of our dedicated servers are setup, monitored, and maintained 24/7 by our Server Management Team – the same team that monitors the entire Brilliant Directories network. The cost of this service is included in all of the prices above.
Network Connection
Each dedicated server has its own dual-redundant Gigabit Network Connection to the internet. This reduces latency when compared to websites sharing the same internet connection on our standard website hosting.
Cutting Edge Data Center
These servers are installed in our rack in the Hurricane Electric data center in New York. They are directly hardwired to our network, separate from the other servers in the data center.
Need a Custom Server Configuration?
Not a problem! To receive a customized dedicated server quote, please contact us at the following link with the server specifications you are interested in.

title: Clone My Website
content:
Want to make an exact copy of your Brilliant Directories website? Purchasing the Clone My Website service will direct our team to promptly clone your existing website and duplicate it to another website that you currently own with Brilliant Directories.
This saves you the time of starting a new website from scratch and allows you to copy over all your customized work and data to a new website with ease – perfect for launching similar websites in varying industries or regions.
Get This Service
Visit our website:
Clone My Website
Key Features to Boost Sales & Conversions
Quickly create similar websites
Maintain consistency through all of your websites
Every aspect of your existing website will be cloned
All custom coding will be cloned
NOTICE
: Typical turnaround time to have your website cloned is one business day or less. You must already own an additional Brilliant Directories website that you would like your existing website copied to.
Who Is This For?
The Clone My Website service is a time-saving resource that can be used with any Brilliant Directories website. We especially recommend this service if you create many similar websites with the Brilliant Directories platform.
This is the service for you if you answer “
Yes
” to at least one of the following questions
Question 1
Are you a web developer who’s customers often want their websites to look or function like your previously developed websites?
With the Clone My Website service, the Brilliant Directories team will quickly clone one of your existing websites to another one of your websites. All of the content, from images to custom code, will be cloned.
Question 2
Are you launching multiple websites that serve the same purpose, but marketed to different industries or locations?
You can establish your desired design and functionality of your flagship site and then have it cloned to your other websites. All you will need to do is update the industry or location data on these other websites to fit their intended market.
Additional Licenses
This service requires you to have an additional, unused website plan with Brilliant Directories. One of your websites can then be cloned to your additional, unused website plan.
For Brilliant Directories website plans and pricing please click
HERE
.
For additional information please call +1 (800) 771-9332.
Add-Ons Information
Premium add-ons
will not be cloned to your new website unless they have been purchased for your new website as well.
Example
: If you wish to have your Easy Coupon Codes cloned from your old site to your new site, you must repurchase the Easy Coupon Codes add-on for the new website. This applies to all add-ons as well as the VIP Add-Ons Club.

Your website will be reverted to the state it was in when you first received it – all of your current information and settings will be permanently deleted.
Question 2
Did your initial business idea not pan out quite as well as you had hoped it would? The Reset My Website service turns your website back to a completely blank slate for you to start fresh. This allows you to try again and improve your original idea, or you can focus on a completely different industry or website idea! It’s an entirely fresh start!
Add-Ons Information
Premium add-ons will not be removed from your website. All premium website add-ons that are currently installed on your Brilliant Directories website will remain after your website has been reset. There is no need to repurchase any website add-ons that you already own.

title: Allow the facebookexternalhit Bot in the Robots.txt File
content:
Facebook uses the
facebookexternalhit
crawler to retrieve website content when links are shared. To allow this crawler, add the following directives to the Robots.txt file.
User-agent: facebookexternalhit
Disallow: /api/
Allow: /
Navigate to
Developer Hub
.
Select
Robots File
.
Add the following directives above the default rules at the end of the Robots.txt file.
Bandwidth
IMPORTANT
: Allowing the
facebookexternalhit
crawler can significantly increase a website's bandwidth usage.
Internal testing has shown that the
facebookexternalhit
crawler may consume substantially more bandwidth than other common crawlers, such as Googlebot and Bingbot. This increase in traffic may result in higher bandwidth usage and, in some cases, reduced website performance.
For this reason, the
facebookexternalhit
crawler is not allowed by default. It should only be enabled when Facebook link previews are required.
The following example illustrates the difference in bandwidth usage between the
facebookexternalhit
crawler and other common crawlers over the same time period:
For these reasons, we do not allow this bot by default, and only recommend allowing it when absolutely necessary.

Member Dashboard URL: Home
The portion URL of the Member Dashboard that will display when a member is on their Member Dashboard Home Page.

A portion of the URL used when a member fills out the "Contact Details" form in the Member Dashboard.

A portion of the URL used when a member uploads their Profile Photo, Logo, and/or Cover Photo in the Member Dashboard.

The root URL of the Member Dashboard that will display when a member is logged in to their account. By default this URL is /account/.

The portion of the URL of the Member Dashboard that will display when a member is viewing their Leads page in their Account. By default this URL is leads.

Portion of the URL that will display when a member is verifying their account in the Member Dashboard. By default is promote/verify.

Portion of the URL that will display when a member wants to modify their password in their account on the Member Dashboard. By default, it is /password.
Member Dashboard URL: Billing
Portion of the URL that will display when a member visits the Billing Information section of their account on the Member Dashboard. By default, it is /billing.

title: Enhancing Security with Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)
content:
In the coming weeks, 2FA will be gradually implemented for admin account logins. If the feature is not visible yet, admins are encouraged to wait a bit longer. A prompt will soon be provided to enable this feature for admin accounts. Any further questions can be directed to the support team, who are available to assist.
The Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) feature is an advanced security measure that adds an extra layer of protection, ensuring that only the authorized user can access their account, even if their password is compromised.
What is Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)?
Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) is a security process that requires two distinct forms of identification before granting access to an account. Unlike traditional single-factor authentication, which relies solely on a password, 2FA incorporates an additional verification step to enhance security.
Note
: 2FA is optional—the admin of the website has the choice to either use it or skip it according to personal preference.
Setting Up 2FA
Getting started with 2FA is straightforward. Users should follow these steps:
Log In: Begin by entering the username and password.
Provide Additional Verification: After the initial login, users will be prompted to provide a second form of verification. This will involve receiving a code via email, which is required to log in to the admin section of the website.
If users wish for the browser to remember their password for the next 7 days, they can select the checkbox to remember the device. If the user logs in from a different device, the system will prompt for the code sent via email once more.
The One Time Passcode will be sent to the Username email.

title: Google Analytics 4: Tracking Membership Plan Sign-Ups Using Key Events (Conversions)
content:
Understanding user interactions, such as sign-ups for different membership plans, is crucial for assessing website performance and optimizing user engagement. Integrating BD websites with Google Analytics 4 (GA4) enables effective tracking of membership plan sign-ups. Here’s a detailed guide on how to set up this tracking.
Part 1: Set Up Tracking on The Brilliant Directories Website
1. Create a New Custom Widget
Begin by accessing the BD website dashboard and creating
a new custom widget
.
2. Name the Widget
Assign a simple nickname to the widget, such as "Track Sign Ups - Membership Plan Name," to facilitate identification.
3. Insert the Tracking Code
Paste the following code into the widget’s code area on the HTML tab:
<script>
gtag("event", "bronze_plan_sign_up", {
method: "sign_up"
});
</script>
This code configures a custom event in GA4 to be triggered whenever a sign-up for the specified membership plan occurs.
IMPORTANT:
Replace
bronze_plan_sign_up
with the name of the membership plan you're tracking.
NO SPACES
NO SYMBOLS
USE UNDERSCORES _
If there are any spaces or symbols, the tracking will not work
Example change:
premium_plan_sign_up
4. Save Changes
Ensure that the widget is saved to apply the changes.
5. Edit the Membership Plan
Go to Finance > Membership Plans, edit the plan that will have the tracking code, find the "Successful Sign Up / Upgrade Conversion Tracking Code Widget" setting in the first tab of the page, and select the widget created for the tracking code.
Part 2: Set Up Key Event to Track in Google Analytics 4 (GA4)
1. Copy the Event Name
Use the exact event name from the inserted code, for example,
bronze_plan_sign_up
.
2. Access GA4 Admin Settings
Navigate to Google Analytics for the website and click on the ADMIN blue icon located at the bottom-left of the page.
3. Navigate to Key Events
Find the
DATA DISPLAY
section in the sidebar, and click on
KEY EVENTS
.
4. Create a New Key Event
Click on
NEW KEY EVENT
and enter the copied event name, such as
bronze_plan_sign_up
IMPORTANT:
The KEY EVENT name
MUST MATCH EXACTLY
the event name defined in the tracking code in the widget.
5. Save the Key Event
Click
SAVE
to finalize the event setup.
Events can be viewed under Reports > User Engagement & Retention > Events.
After adding a new event in GA4, it typically takes about 24 to 48 hours for the event to appear in the Events report. This delay is due to the time required for data processing and reporting updates within Google Analytics 4.
To see the new event sooner, checking the
Realtime
report might provide immediate insights, though the full data and detailed reports will still be updated within the 24 to 48-hour time-frame.
With the tracking for membership plan sign-ups configured, monitoring these events directly in Google Analytics 4 becomes possible.
For different membership plans, the process can be repeated with unique event names for each plan.
By following these instructions, valuable insights into user engagement with various membership plans can be obtained, enabling data-driven decisions to enhance website performance.

title: Website Terms and Conditions
content:
A website's Terms of Use (also known as Terms and Conditions or Terms of Service) is basically a set of rules that users agree to follow when they interact with a website. Think of it as the "house rules" that the website owner sets to protect both themselves and the users. These terms cover everything from how the content on the site can be used, to what users can and can't do while they're there, and even what happens if someone violates those rules.
Here's a quick rundown of what might be included:
User Conduct
: Guidelines on what behavior is acceptable or prohibited (e.g., no spamming, no illegal activities).
Intellectual Property
: Details about who owns the content on the site (text, images, videos) and how it can be used.
Privacy
: Information on how user data is collected, stored, and used by the website.
Disclaimers
: Statements that limit the website's liability for errors, inaccuracies, or damages that might occur from using the site.
Governing Law
: The legal jurisdiction that governs the terms (e.g., laws of a specific state or country).
Termination
: The right of the website owner to suspend or terminate a user's access for violating the terms.
These terms create a legal framework that helps ensure everyone knows what’s expected, keeping the experience smooth and safe for all involved.
Terms of Use Page
All Brilliant Directories websites come with a Terms of Use page:
domain.com
/about/terms
Example:
https://www.demobootstrap.com/about/terms
Accepting Terms of Use
Users will agree to the Terms and Conditions upon sign up, whether it is a FREE or PAID account.
Notes
The Terms are accepted upon sign up once. Currently there is no setting to renew/accept Terms & Conditions agreement on a daily, weekly, monthly or yearly basis.

title: How to Optimize the Bandwidth Usage of a Site
content:
How to Optimize the Bandwidth Usage of a Site
High bandwidth usage can affect website performance and can require additional capacity. The tools below help measure traffic and reduce unnecessary transfer.
Viewing Bandwidth Usage
Domain Manager
Open
Settings > Domain Manager > Usage
for the current usage summary. The displayed limit includes the website license and any capacity purchased through the
VIP Add-Ons Club
or
Bandwidth Boost Add-Ons
.
The Usage tab compares current consumption with the website’s plan limits.
cPanel
Open
Developer Hub > cPanel Dashboard
, then select
Bandwidth
under Metrics. cPanel includes historical totals and separates traffic such as HTTP, FTP, IMAP, POP3, and SMTP.
AWStats
AWStats identifies traffic sources and the bandwidth each source consumed. See
Identifying Sources of Bandwidth Usage with AWStats
.
General Strategies
Set Up Cloudflare
Cloudflare can cache static files and filter unwanted traffic, reducing requests to the origin server. See
Connecting a Site to Cloudflare
.
Optimize Images
ImageKit can resize and optimize images for the requesting device. See
Use a Content Delivery Network for Images
.
Remove Unneeded Screenshot Previews
Disable screenshot previews in admin areas where they are not useful, including Dashboard, Web Page Builder, Edit Post Settings, Form Manager, and Domain Manager.
Address Specific Traffic Sources
Use AWStats before blocking traffic. For sites using Cloudflare, its
WAF custom rules
can restrict selected countries or request patterns. Other sites can use the
Block Traffic by Country
tool.
Restore the default crawler rules or add deliberate custom rules through the
robots.txt documentation
. Blocking legitimate search crawlers can reduce indexing.

title: Identifying Sources of Bandwidth Usage with AWStats
content:
AWStats, a powerful web analytics tool integrated into cPanel, offers a wealth of information about a website's traffic. Let's delve into how to leverage AWStats to pinpoint traffic sources and identify which ones are consuming the most bandwidth.
Accessing AWStats
In the Admin area of the website, navigate to the Developer Hub > cPanel Dashboard to log into your cPanel
Navigate to the "Metrics" section and click on the "AWStats" icon
Select the domain you want to analyze from the dropdown menu and click "View."
At the top of the screen, there is an option to choose the "Reported Period". Choose "Monthly" and the month and year to view.  The current month will be selected by default.
Identifying Sources of Bandwidth Consumption
Once in the AWStats interface, there is a lot of information about the traffic to the website.  The following sections are the most important when trying to find the primary sources of bandwidth consumption.
"Summary" Section
This section gives a high level overview of how much traffic a site received from
humans
("Viewed traffic") and
bots
("Not Viewed Traffic").
Key Takeaways / Action Items
One critical piece of information here is the "Bandwidth" column, which gives an indication of how much bandwidth has been consumed by humans vs bots.
If the majority of the traffic is coming from humans, checking the "Locales" and "Hosts" sections below will provide more information about the specific sources of that traffic and if there are opportunities to block specific IPs or countries.
If the majority of the traffic is coming from bots, the
"Robots/Spiders visitors" section below will list the specific bots that are consuming the traffic.  This will help identify bots that can be blocked in the robots.txt file to prevent future bandwidth usage.
"Locales" Section
This section provides a breakdown of visitors based on their geographical location. You'll see the number of visits and the percentage of total traffic each country contributes.
Key Takeaways / Action Items
If a lot of visitors are coming from outside of the website's target market,
blocking traffic from outside of those countries
can have a large impact on the bandwidth usage of the site.
"Hosts" Section
This is a list of IP addresses that have accessed the site. This can help identify the specific IPs, companies, organizations, or internet service providers (ISPs) consuming bandwidth on the site.
Key Takeaways / Action Items
Specific IPs can sometimes consume an outsized portion of a site's bandwidth. Use a tool like
https://www.ip2location.com/
to search for a specific IP and find information about what country it is from, if it is associated with a specific company or ISP, and more.
If a single IP is identified to be consuming a large amount of bandwidth and it is not a desirable source of traffic,
the IP can be blocked
.
Note: If a website is using Cloudflare, Securi, or other DNS hosts that act as a proxy, the IPs listed here will be from the DNS host rather than the original user that made the request.  More information about the IPs accessing the site can be found in the DNS host account.
"Robots/Spiders visitors" Section
This section shows the "user agent" of bots that have visited the site, and how much bandwidth has been consumed by each bot.
Key Takeaways / Action Items
If the "Summary" section described above indicates that most of the bandwidth usage of the website is coming from bots, this section will help identify which specific bots are consuming the bandwidth so a decision can be made whether to block them or not.
Once an undesirable bot is identified, it can be blocked in the
robots.txt file
.
The default robots.txt file blocks ALL bots except for Google, Yahoo, Bing, and Twitter / X. Using the default robots.txt rules is recommended for most websites and will prevent a large number of undesirable bots from crawling the site and consuming bandwidth.
Important
: Facebook has a bot called "facebookexternalhit". This bot must be allowed in the robots.txt file in order for pages on the website to be shared on Facebook. However, this bot is known for consuming an enormous amount of bandwidth, far beyond what is required to share content on Facebook, and is blocked by default. Find more information about the
facebookexternalhit bot
.

title: Changelog - August 2024
content:
Enhancements / Fixes:
We fixed an issue which was affecting the ability to create pre-styled buttons using the Froala WYSIWYG in some cases.
We fixed an issue which was causing the counter that displays next to the Manage Posts sidebar menu item in the Admin to incorrectly calculate the number of posts that were pending approval in some cases.
We implemented a security update to the Bookmark My Favorites and Community Comments Add-Ons.
We fixed an issue which was preventing the Google Maps Location logic from being triggered after performing a frontend location search on mobile devices in some cases.
We added support for dashes in the names of coupon codes.
We fixed an issue which was causing the system to include CSS styles in messages sent via the "3rd Party Lead Matched Notifications (SMS)" Lead Setting in some cases.
We fixed an issue which was causing the system to display unnecessary HTML entities code after successfully purchasing a Member Post on the Member Dashboard in some cases.
We updated the display of One-Click Social Login buttons in sidebar modules to make them better aligned.
We fixed an issue which was preventing the system from using the correct text label for a form's submit button in the Member Dashboard in some cases.
The RSS Feed for Posts Add-On date format is now compatible with the Date Format Setting.
The Subscription Name is now available for all members when exporting members to a CSV file from the Admin.
We fixed an issue which was preventing the name of forms from displaying when using the "Show Widget" feature when viewing a website as an Admin.
We made several small bug fixes and UI improvements to the new Import Business Data tool in the Admin.
We fixed an issue which was preventing the Recent Transaction widget in the Member Dashboard from displaying the total amount for invoices in some cases.
We fixed an issue which was affecting the ability to display the Multi-Photo Post Type description data on member profile pages in some cases.
We implemented an update to prefill the Sub Categories dropdown in the Website - Lead Form - Get Matched form after clicking the "Request Information" button on the Specialties tab on member profile pages.
We we fixed an issue where invoices were labeled as being "Past Due" in the Payment History table in the Member Dashboard when a member has an upcoming invoice and is currently on a free trial.
We
made several security updates to the Admin.
We fixed an issue that was causing images in email templates from displaying correctly on mobile devices in some cases.
Stripe no longer allows directly migrating user credit card information to their platform, so we removed the support we had for that functionality as well.
We fixed an issue which was affecting the ability to accept an Admin Email Invite when using Chrome as a web browser in some cases.
We updated the links on the Categories and Location pages to make it compatible with the "Reduce Category Canonical Tags" and "Localize Canonical Tags" Advanced Settings.
We fixed an issue which was preventing the "Canonical", "Prev" and "Next" meta URLs from working properly on search result pages in some cases.
We updated the Brilliant Directories Zapier App to allow selecting an option without a value for all dropdown fields that are not required to have a value.
We fixed an issue which was preventing the Admin area from working properly when using Safari as web browser in some rare cases.
We fixed an issue that was preventing the "Maximum Uses" Coupon Code Setting from working properly on the frontend of sites.
We fixed an issue with the Send Newsletter feature which was preventing the system from updating the status of a campaign to "Sent" after the campaign was completed in some cases.
We implemented an update to display the default member photo and logo image on member profiles when the "Enable Profile Photo Upload" and "Enable Logo Upload" Membership Plan settings are disabled.
We
fixed an issue which was preventing the "Limit Canonical Tags To One Country" setting from working properly in some cases.
We added a new CSS class called "featured-post". This CSS can be used to target the "featured" / "pinned" posts on post search results pages.
We fixed an issue causing the GDPR Consent Fields checkboxes to display slightly misaligned in the member lead contact modal in some cases.
We fixed an issue which was preventing the Search Members page from returning results after performing a location search using the "Include Service Areas" checkbox in some cases.
We fixed an issue that was preventing the "Prioritize Profile Cover Photo as Social Share Image" Advanced Setting from working properly on the frontend of sites in some cases.
We updated the Match Lead page in the Admin to always display the member to whom a lead was submitted as the first suggested result when manually matching a lead in the Admin.
We fixed an issue which was preventing the Brilliant Directories API from fetching custom member data as expected.
We improved the performance of the member search when using the "Find Duplicates" filter field on the Search Members page in the Admin.
We fixed an issue which was preventing "Date" and "Date & Time Picker" form fields from working properly when the "Date Format" is set to "YYYY/MM/DD" in some cases.
We updated the Business Data Importer in the Admin to allow searching for locations in both English and the language of the website.
In all, over 50 feature enhancements and software updates were released this month.

title: Using CSS to Target Featured Posts
content:
Previously, customizing the appearance of
Pinned Featured Posts
required modifying PHP in specific widgets.
Brilliant Directories now adds a dedicated CSS class to featured posts, making it much easier to customize their appearance using CSS instead of PHP.
This article demonstrates how to target featured posts with CSS and provides an example of how to customize their appearance.
CSS Classes for Featured Posts
Each featured post includes a CSS class that can be targeted based on its post type.
The following examples show two different post types and their corresponding CSS classes:
https://bootstrap.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000051517-pin-featured-posts
In this example will change the Background Color of the post on the search results page with the CSS code below:
.featured-post, .featured-post .img_section, .featured-post .mid_section, .featured-post .grid_element {
    background-color: aliceblue;
}
After saving the changes, featured posts will display with the new background color on the search results page.

title: Member Export Fields Overview
content:
Below is a breakdown of the essential data fields that are used for creating and managing listings within the system.
The number of export fields differs from site to site, because the list is built from the member fields each site stores, plus any add-on fields that are active. The
Export Members
window shows the count above the field list (in the screenshot below it reads
Showing 1 to 105 of 105 entries
). The
user_id
and
email
fields are always exported and are not part of that count:
Custom fields are added to the export fields list too, once at least one member has a value saved in them. Type the field name into the search box (1) to find it (2):
These fields ensure that each listing is represented accurately and comprehensively, capturing both personal and professional details as well as social media and business information. Here's a detailed explanation for each field in the listings data.
Listing & Company Import Fields
The table includes various columns designed to capture all the necessary information for a comprehensive listing. These columns help build a detailed profile that encompasses both personal identifiers and business-related data.
These also ensure that users can interact with, locate, and learn about the profiles in an organized manner.
listing_type
: The type of listing, such as business or individual.
logo
: URL of the logo associated with the listing.
profile_photo
: URL of the profile photo of the listing.
first_name
: The first name of the individual associated with the listing.
last_name
: The last name of the individual associated with the listing.
name
: The full name of the individual or business.
email
: The email address for the listing.
company
: The name of the company associated with the listing.
phone_number
: The best contact phone number for the listing.
fax_number
: The fax number for the listing.
address1
: Primary street address.
address2
: Secondary street address, if applicable.
city
: The city where the listing is located.
zip_code
: The postal or ZIP code for the listing.
state_code
: Two-letter abbreviation of the state.
country_code
: Two-letter abbreviation of the country.
country_name
: Full name of the country, if applicable.
website
: The URL of the listing's website.
twitter
: Full URL of the listing’s Twitter account.
facebook
: Full URL of the listing’s Facebook page.
linkedin
: Full URL of the listing’s LinkedIn profile.
youtube
: Full URL of the listing’s YouTube account.
instagram
: Full URL of the listing’s Instagram account.
pinterest
: Full URL of the listing’s Pinterest account.
snapchat
: Full URL of the listing’s Snapchat account.
tiktok
: Full URL of the listing’s TikTok account.
whatsapp
: Full international phone number link for WhatsApp.
blog
: Full URL of the listing’s external blog, if applicable.
quote
: A short quote that represents the listing, suitable for social media.
experience
: The year the listing's career or business began.
affiliation
: Any associations the listing is a part of.
awards
: Any awards received by the business or individual in the listing.
published
: Any publications where the listing has been featured.
education
: Additional education information related to the listing.
software
: Any software used by the business or individual in the listing.
about_me
: General information about the listing that doesn't fit into other categories.
password
: The password used by the member to log in to the system.
position
: The title of the individual represented in the listing.
profession_name
: The top-level profession category the listing belongs to.
services
: Sub-level services associated with the listing, separated by commas.
google_plus
: Full URL of the Google Plus page associated with the listing.
search_description
: A short description that appears in search results.
parent_id
: ID of the parent member if the listing is a sub-account.
lat
: The latitude of the listing's location, used in Google Maps.
lon
: The longitude of the listing's location, used in Google Maps.
verified
: Type "1" if the listing is verified, leave blank if not verified.
More information:
How To Import Members Via CSV File
Listing & Company Export Fields
These fields are additional attributes that are included in the export file to provide a more detailed profile. These capture various elements ranging from personal details to social media presence and business information.
about_me
: A section that provides a brief description or biography of the listing.
active
: Indicates whether the listing is currently active (1 for active, 0 for inactive).
address1
: The primary street address of the listing.

affiliation

1
means the member’s profile URL is locked and is never regenerated automatically, which corresponds to the

checkbox on the member edit form. The field name is historical and has nothing to do with Bitly link shortening.
blog

city

company

country_code

cover_photo

credentials

cv

email

experience

facebook

facebook_id
: Facebook ID associated with the listing, if applicable.
featured
: Indicates if the listing is featured (1 for featured, 0 for not featured).
filename
: The filename of any uploaded files related to the listing.
first_name

position

profession_name

rep_matters

signup_date

state_ln

subscription_id

token

total_paid_invoices

total_pastdue_invoices

total_refunded_invoices
: The total number of refunded invoices for the listing.
twitter
: Full URL of the Twitter profile associated with the listing.
user_consent
: Indicator of whether the user has given consent for their data (1 for yes, 0 for no).
user_id
: The unique ID of the user associated with the listing.
verified
: Indicates if the listing has been verified (1 for verified, 0 for not verified).
website
: The URL of the website associated with the listing.
work_experience
: A description of the work experience of the individual or company in the listing.
youtube
: Full URL of the YouTube account associated with the listing.
zip_code
: The postal or ZIP code for the listing's location.

title: Brilliant Directories API Endpoints Technical Reference
content: The Brilliant Directories API provides a set of endpoints for interacting with and managing various aspects of a directory website. It supports API key authentication and offers operations for creating, reading, updating, and deleting data from the website. The API is designed to facilitate integrations and customizations by providing access to essential website functions through RESTful commands.

title: How to Set the Total Number of Member Search Results per Page
content:
To determine the number of search results displayed on your search pages, follow these steps:

My Content

post type.

title: How to "DELETE" a Member through the API using Zapier
content:
This article shows an example of how a Google Spreadsheet can be used to delete member data using the site's API.
Checklist Before Moving Forward With This Example
1) Make sure to generate a unique API Key using the documentation down below as a guideline. Please make sure to save the API Key in a safe place as it is not accessible after it has been created:
How To Generate an API Key

This process typically involves integrating a third-party cookie consent solution into a website. Such tools streamline the process by providing pre-built scripts and customizable interfaces to manage user consent.
Select a Cookie Consent Tool
Choose a reliable third-party provider that aligns with the website's privacy requirements. Popular options include Cookiebot, OneTrust, and
Osano
(
click for example
). These tools offer comprehensive features, such as banner customization, consent tracking, and integration support.

To integrate cookie consent functionality in a Brilliant Directories website, follow these steps:
Access the
Brilliant Directories Admin Dashboard
.

Navigate to the
Toolbox
section and select
Widget Manager
.

Search for the
Bootstrap Theme - Cookie Consent Code
widget.

Insert the third-party snippet in the HTML editor.
Open the widget in the editor and paste the provided cookie consent code snippet into the appropriate section of the HTML.
Save the changes.
Click on
Save Changes
to finalize and implement the updates on the website.

title: Unsubscribe API - Unsubscribe Members from Email Campaigns
content:
It is possible to
Unsubscribe a member
from receiving email using the api, only 1 member can be updated at a time.
Using the API there are 4 Unsubscribe actions that can be achieved:
/api/v2/unsubscribe_list/get/{id}
/api/v2/unsubscribe_list/create
/api/v2/unsubscribe_list/update
/api/v2/unsubscribe_list/delete
We will break down these actions and explain how to achieve an end results with each one. The examples shown in this article are completed using
https://www.postman.com/
Unsubscribe Get API
/api/v2/unsubscribe_list/get/{id}
Using this action is simple, add the url above but replace {id} with the actual member ID. This will fetch the member information from the website
Unsubscribe Create API
/api/v2/unsubscribe_list/create
With this action, by sending the email, it will add the member to the unsubscribe list.
Unsubscribe Update API
/api/v2/unsubscribe_list/update
With this action it is possible to update the unsubscribed list. Replace {id} with the member ID that will be updated from the unsubscribed list.
Unsubscribe Delete API
/api/v2/unsubscribe_list/delete
Use this action URL to delete a a member from the unsubscribed list, replace {id} with the member ID that will be removed from the unsubscribed list.

title: Checklist when Changing the Domain of a Live Website
content:
Changing an existing website's domain affects its address, email identity, and services that authorize a specific domain. Use this checklist before and after the
Switch Over
stage in
Settings > Domain Manager
.
Before the switch
Confirm access to the new domain's registrar and DNS provider.
Record the current DNS and mail-provider settings.
Preserve access to existing mailboxes and back up any messages that must be retained. Confirm the mailbox migration plan before changing a domain used for BD-hosted email.
Plan old-domain redirects separately. Changing the website address does not, by itself, establish a redirect from every old address.
List integrations restricted to the old domain, including Google Maps, reCAPTCHA, Google/Facebook login, payment callbacks, image delivery, and other connected services.
Confirm the Managed SSL entitlement or the plan for installing a third-party certificate.
Connect the new address
Open
Settings > Domain Manager > Domain
.
Click
Change my domain name
.
Follow
the connection walkthrough
through address validation and DNS pointing.
Review the old and new addresses on
Switch Over
.
Confirm the switch only when the new address and remaining consequences are understood.
After the switch
Open the new address to confirm the intended website loads.
Check
SSL
for the new hostname.
Check
Emails > Sender Authentication
for the new domain.
Complete any manual SPF or DKIM instructions shown.
Confirm the default sending address and the administrative contact email. The switch moves a sending address that used the old domain or a placeholder to the new domain, keeping the part before the @; an address at another domain is left unchanged.
Confirm incoming mail routing in
Mailboxes
and at the mail provider.
Test sending and receiving email.
Update domain-restricted integrations at their providers.
Test maps, protected forms, social login, checkout, and important member workflows.
Update branding, externally stored links, and relevant search/analytics properties.
Verify the old-domain redirect if one was configured.
The completion screen lists
What to do next
: the email records, the security certificate request, and the integration keys that need the new domain. It can report that email records were already published when the connected DNS service accepted them. Still check the
Emails
result and test delivery. A changed domain does not automatically update every external provider's authorized-domain list.
Completion means the new website loads securely, outgoing authentication and incoming mail work, the required integrations pass their checks, and any intended old-domain redirects work.

title: How to "Search"  for members through the API
content:
In this article, we will be going over how to "Search" members using the /search API .
What this API endpoint allows to do is to send information to the endpoint, just like it would emulate the functionality of using one of the member search features on the site.
How to "Search" Members
The user search API leverages various parameters to retrieve data displayed the same way as on member search results pages on the site.
Parameters
There are 10 parameters that can be used to filter the results.
dynamic:
Set to 1 to simulate a Dynamic Category Filter search.
q:
Enter a keyword to search for in member data.
pid:
Enter member Top Level Category ID to search for. Enter a comma-separated list of IDs if the Dynamic Category Filter search is enabled.
tid:
Enter member Sub Level Category ID to search for. Enter a comma-separated list of IDs if the Dynamic Category Filter search is enabled.
ttid:
Enter member Sub-Sub Level Category ID to search for. Enter a comma-separated list of IDs if the Dynamic Category Filter search is enabled.
address:
Enter the location to search for. Example: Los Angeles, California, United States.
output_type:
Enter the type of response to receive. Valid options - html, array. By default the results will show in HTML similar to the search results page on the site. If set to Array the results will show in a JSON array.
limit:
Enter the maximum number of search results to return per page of results.
sort:
Set the Order the data would be display. The options here are :
reviews, name ASC, name DESC, last_name_asc, last_name_desc
page:
Enter the page number of results to return. For Example, enter 2 to return the second page of results.
Example with Postman
When endpoint is sent by default the results will show in the HTML format, the same as the search results page:
When selecting Array as the output_type, the results will show in a Json Array format:
Important Note
When using the address field, it is required for the site to have the Pretty URL advanced setup enabled. For more information on how to do so:
Set Up Pretty URLs with Google Maps

title: How to Get Member Transactions Through the API
content:
In this article, we will be going over how to Read members transactions using the Transactions API .
What this API endpoint allows to do is to gather transaction information from 1 member at the time.
How to get member transactions
The Transactions API leverages a single parameter (member ID or Client ID) to retrieve  all the transactions data.
/api/v2/user/transactions
Parameters
Only 1 parameter is needed to run the API: It can either be the
Member ID
or the
Client ID
(The id of the tblclients table in the billing database)

title: Top Sidebar Widgets
content:
This article highlights the top sidebar widgets frequently used across various site pages, including profile pages, search results, and post pages. It is designed to help site admins select the best widgets to enhance page sidebars and improve user experience.
While it doesn't include every widget option available, it focuses on the most popular and effective choices.
Adding Widgets to a Sidebar
To search for and add widgets to sidebars:
Go to
Toolbox
Select
Sidebar Manager
Find the desired sidebar and click "
Edit
"
Search
for the widget
Drag and drop it into the sidebar
Save
Throughout this article, each widget is listed with its reference in the format
[widget=...]
. This is the widget's name — search for it in the Sidebar Manager to find and add it.
More information:
Sidebar Alignment:
Design Settings » Sidebar Alignment Options
Sidebar Manager Overview
:
Toolbox » Sidebar Manager
How to Create a Sidebar
Universal Sidebar Widgets
These widgets can be added to any page and will retain their intended functionality.
Share this Page
Displays social sharing buttons for the current page.
[widget=Bootstrap Theme - Module - Social Share]
Join Our Community
Invites users to get listed on the site.
[widget=Bootstrap Theme - Module - Member Join Offer]
Join Newsletter
Allows members and users to join the site's newsletter.
[widget=Bootstrap Theme - Module - Newsletter Sign Up Form]
Sidebar Videos & Text Boxes
Enhance the website sidebars with videos and custom text boxes to showcase important content, promotions, or helpful resources.
Video
Add videos to sidebars by creating a new widget and inserting the embed code:
How to Add a Video in a Sidebar
Text Box
Add a custom text box to sidebars by creating a new widget and inserting the text content:
How to Create a Text Box to Display Text in a Sidebar
Banner Ads on Sidebars
The process of adding banners to any sidebar can be found here:
Adding Banners to Sidebars
Global Search Results
The default sidebar used on this page is
Global Website Search
.
Global Search
This widget allows users to search more keywords across the entire site.
[widget=Bootstrap Theme - Module - Global Website Search]
Member Profiles
The default sidebar used on this page is the
Member Profile Page
default sidebar.
Contact Form
This widget allows users to contact the member.
[widget=Bootstrap Theme - Module - Member Contact Form]
Related Searches
This widget shows related searches based on the member's information.
[widget=Bootstrap Theme - Module - Member Related Searches]

With this widget, the Facebook Feed streams all of the latest posts and updates from a specific Facebook account.
Only Facebook Company Pages or Fan Pages will stream content.

default sidebar.
Search Module
This widget finds members based on keywords and/or location.
[widget=Bootstrap Theme - Search Module - Keyword_Location]
Recent Reviews

Post
Search Result

title: Setting Up Razorpay
content:
As of February 1st, 2025, Razorpay is available as a native payment gateway integration in Brilliant Directories. Follow the steps below to generate the necessary credentials and complete the setup process.
Step 1: Access the Razorpay API Section
Log in to the
Razorpay Dashboard
at
https://dashboard.razorpay.com
.
Click
Account & Settings
from the left sidebar.
Navigate to
API Keys
under
Website and App Settings
.
Step 2: Generate the Razorpay API Key
If an API Key has not been created yet, click
Generate Key
.
Note whether the system is in
Test
or
Live
mode. Test mode keys work only for test transactions. If these keys are for the live website, ensure Live mode is selected before generating keys.
Step 3: Copy the Key ID and Key Secret
After generating the keys, a pop-up will display the
Key ID
and
Key Secret
.
Copy the
Key ID
. This will be required to complete the integration.
Copy the
Key Secret
. The
Key Secret
will only be displayed once, so ensure it is securely saved.
IMPORTANT:
If a new API Key is ever created in the future, make sure to update the Brilliant Directories website with the new
Key ID
and
Key Secret
to ensure uninterrupted payment processing.
Step 4: Add Razorpay as a Payment Gateway in Brilliant Directories
Log in to the
Brilliant Directories Admin
.
Navigate to
Finance
→
Payment Settings
.
Click
Add a New Payment Gateway
.
Select
Razorpay
from the list of available payment gateways.
Step 5: Enter the Razorpay Keys and Save
In the Razorpay setup popup, paste the
Key ID
into the designated field.
Paste the
Key Secret
into the corresponding field.
Click
Save Changes
to complete the integration.
Step 6: Verify the Integration
Process a test transaction to confirm that payments are being processed correctly.
Check the
Razorpay Dashboard
for transaction logs.
If any issues arise, refer to Razorpay’s official support documentation or contact Brilliant Directories support for assistance.
IMPORTANT: Required Razorpay Settings
The following settings must be configured correctly for the integration to work properly:
Under General Settings >> Locatlization >> Website Currency Set To: Indian Rupee
Ensure these settings are verified before completing the setup. Incorrect configurations may cause payment issues.
Live Mode vs. Test Mode
Razorpay offers two modes:
Live Mode
and
Test Mode
.
Live Mode:
Use this mode to process actual transactions. The
Key ID
and
Key Secret
generated in Live Mode are separate from those in Test Mode.
Test Mode:
Use this mode for testing purposes. Transactions in Test Mode do not involve real payments, but the Test Mode Key ID and Key Secret must be used.
Ensure the appropriate mode is selected based on the intended use of the integration.
After completing these steps and verifying the configuration, transactions will be securely processed through Razorpay, ensuring a seamless payment experience.

title: Managing Leads From A Member's Perspective
content:
Members can manage leads directly from their dashboard. Depending on the lead settings configured by the site administrator, members may be able to:
Purchase a lead
Accept a free lead
Decline a lead
This article explains how each action works and how members can track the status of their assigned leads.
Purchasing Leads
Please find all the relevant information here:
Purchasing Leads
Accepting Free Leads
An email notification is sent when a lead is assigned. The email contains a link to view the lead details.
The link included in the email automatically logs into the dashboard and opens the assigned lead. Clicking on "
View Details
" will open the lead:
If lead notifications are configured to display a preview only, Accept Lead must be selected before the full contact information becomes available.
After the lead is accepted, the complete lead information becomes available, including contact details such as email address and phone number.
Declining Leads
The member will receive an email notifying them that they have a lead. A link to view the lead is included in the email template:
Clicking on the link will AUTOMATICALLY log that member into his dashboard and take them straight to the lead itself facilitating the purchasing process. Clicking on "
View Details
" will open the lead:
The member will click on "
Decline
Lead
" to not accept it:
The system will display a pop-up asking for feedback on why the lead was not accepted. This question is optional.
The lead will appear as "Declined" in this section:
View Declined Lead Reason
The owner of the site views the declined lead reason in the Leads details of the admin:
Member Assigned Lead Status
When a lead is accepted, the following lead statuses will be displayed:
Deal Won
Deal Lost
In Progress
Needs Contact
These statuses are designed to help members efficiently manage their leads on the dashboard.
This appears in its own column when viewing all leads:
Lead Status Text Labels
These are text labels which can be found and edited within the
Settings » Text Labels
:
lead_user_status_won
lead_user_status_deal_lost
lead_user_status_in_progress
lead_user_status_needs_contact

title: Widgets API - How to edit widgets data with API Calls
content:
The API allows getting, creating, updating, deleting, rendering, and posting widgets on the website. However, only one widget can be updated at a time. Available API Endpoints Below is a list of the available endpoints for Widgets: https://example.com/api/v2/data_widgets/get/{id} https://example.com/api/v2/data_widgets/create https://example.com/api/v2/data_widgets/update https://example.com/api/v2/data_widgets/delete https://example.com/api/v2/data_widgets/render Using the API, the following actions can be performed: Get a Widget Read the data of a single widget based on the widget_id. Legacy widgets are not returned. The Default widgets included in a /get list response are limited to those supported by the current version of the software. Default widgets that belong only to legacy versions are no longer included, so API responses may contain fewer widgets than in previous versions. This is expected and does not affect the Widget Manager or any existing website. Widgets that support the current version along with older versions are still returned. The filter checks whether the current version is included in the widget's supported versions, not whether it is the only supported version. Customized widgets are also returned regardless of the versions they list, and reading a single widget by its widget_id is not filtered. Endpoint : GET https://example.com/api/v2/data_widgets/get/{id} curl -H "Authorization: YOUR_API_KEY" \ "https://example.com/api/v2/data_widgets/get/{id}" Example Request: GET https://example.com/api/v2/data_widgets/get/?property=widget_id&property_value=29 Query Parameters: property The property key (eg., widget_id). property_value The value associated with the property. Example Response: { "status": "success", "message": [ { "widget_id": "29", "widget_name": "Hello World", "widget_data": "

", "widget_style": ".hello{color:green}", "date_updated": "2025-02-13 10:32:20", "revision_timestamp": "2025-02-13 11:32:20", "widget_javascript": "", } ], "total": "1", "current_page": 1, "total_pages": 1 } Create a Widget Add a new widget to the database. Parameter Notes : The widget_id will be assigned by the system. Endpoint : POST https://example.com/api/v2/data_widgets/create curl -H "Authorization: YOUR_API_KEY" \ "https://example.com/api/v2/data_widgets/create" Example Request: { "widget_name": "Hello World", "widget_data": "

", "widget_style": ".hello{color:red}", "widget_javascript": "" } Query Parameters: widget_name The name of the widget. widget_data HTML + PHP. widget_style CSS. widget_javascript JS. Example Response: { "status": "success", "message": { "widget_id": "28", "widget_name": "Hello World", "widget_data": "

", "widget_style": ".hello{color:red}", "date_updated": "2025-02-13 10:11:19", "widget_javascript": "", } } Update a Widget Update a widget record and their related data from the database. Parameter Notes : Use widget_id or widget_name . Endpoint : PUT https://example.com/api/v2/data_widgets/update curl -H "Authorization: YOUR_API_KEY" \ "https://example.com/api/v2/data_widgets/update" Example Request: { "widget_id": 28, "widget_name": "Hello Amazing World", "widget_data": "

", "widget_style": ".hello{color:green}", "widget_javascript": "" } Query Parameters: widget_id The ID of the widget. widget_name The name of the widget. widget_data HTML + PHP. widget_style CSS. widget_javascript JS. Example Response: { "status": "success", "message": { "widget_id": "28", "widget_name": "Hello Amazing World ", "widget_data": "

", "widget_style": ".hello{color:green}", "date_updated": "2025-02-13 10:11:19", "revision_timestamp": "2025-02-13 11:11:19", "widget_html_element": "", "widget_javascript": "", } } Delete a Widget Delete a widget and their related data from the database. Parameter Notes : Use widget_id or widget_name . Endpoint : DELETE https://example.com/api/v2/data_widgets/delete curl -H "Authorization: YOUR_API_KEY" \ "https://example.com/api/v2/data_widgets/delete" Example Request: { "widget_id": 28 } Query Parameters: widget_id The ID of the widget. widget_name The name of the widget. Example Response: { "status": "success", "message": "data_widgets record was deleted" } Render a Widget Render widget content of specific widget. Parameter Notes : Use widget_id or widget_name . The widget needs to be customized to get the widget output. Endpoint : POST https://example.com/api/v2/data_widgets/render curl -H "Authorization: YOUR_API_KEY" \ "https://example.com/api/v2/data_widgets/render" Example Request: { "widget_id": 31, "widget_name": "Bootstrap Theme - Homepage Search - Yellow Pages Search" } Query Parameters: widget_id The ID of the widget. widget_name The name of the widget. title: My Members Search Members » Search Filters
content:
The search filters enable refining the results based on specific criteria, helping to locate members efficiently.
Search Filters
There are 23 different search filters,
1. Search by Name, ID, URL, or Token
Allows searching for a member using their name, unique ID, profile URL, or token.
2. Membership Plan
Filters members based on their assigned membership plans.
3. Top-Level Category
Enables filtering by the primary category assigned to a member.
4. Joined Date Range
Filters members based on the date they joined the platform.
5. Search by Email Address
Allows locating a member by their registered email address.
6. Account Status
Filters members based on their account status, such as active, inactive, or on hold.
7. Sub-Category Selection
Allows refining searches further by selecting a sub-category relevant to a member.
8. Login Date Range
Filters members based on their last login activity within a specified date range.
9. Verified Status
Filters members based on whether they have been verified on the platform.
10. Transaction Types
Filters members based on their payment history, such as No Transactions, Paid, Stopped / Cancelled, Past Due, Refunded, Upcoming, Credits Available. (Includes filter for
members with available credits
)
11. Sub-Sub Category
Allows for further refinement by selecting a sub-sub category for the member.
12. Joined Via
Filters members based on how they registered, such as Admin, API, Import CSV, Business Data Import, Self Signup, Self Signup Via Facebook, Self Signup Via Google, and Self Signup Via Claim Listing.
13. Search by Location
Filters members based on their geographic location.
14. Member Type
Filters results by member type, such as individual or company.
15. Forms Submitted
Filters members based on the forms they have completed and submitted.
16. Forms Not Submitted
Filters members based on the forms they have not yet submitted.
17. Profile Status Filter
(Complete or Incomplete; only available if the
Require Complete Profiles
setting is turned on)
18. Find Duplicates
The
Find Duplicates
filter enables the administrator to locate members based on selected fields. If multiple options are chosen, the filter will seek duplicates across all selected criteria.
19. Choose Sales Rep. Name
This dropdown will display all the sales representatives that are added to members of the website. Available with the
Sales Representative Tracking
advanced setting.
20. User IP Country
Filters members based on the country associated with their IP address.
21. User IP
Allows searching members based on their last recorded IP address.
22. Member Tags
Filters members using custom tags assigned to them. (Available with the
Member Tags & Tag Groups
Add-on)
23. Profile Images
The
Profile Images Filter
has two options:
Image Exist
: Shows members who have the selected image(s) in the filter.
Image Missing
: Shows members who are missing the selected image(s).
Profile Photo Image:
Filters members based on whether they have uploaded a profile picture. This option is typically relevant for individual listings.
Company Logo Image:
Filters members based on whether they have uploaded a company logo. This option is relevant for company listings.
Profile Cover Image:
Filters members who have uploaded a cover image for their profile. Cover images help personalize a profile and enhance its visual appeal.
Important
This is an "AND" search, meaning if all three image types (
Profile, Logo, and Cover Image
) are selected, the system will look for members who have all three images. Only members meeting all three criteria will appear in the search results.
Searching by Multiple Member IDs
The
Member Name, ID, or URL
filter allows to search for multiple member IDs simultaneously. To do this, add a
#
to the search query, followed by a comma-separated list of member IDs. (see screenshot)
Example:
#44871,44866,44858
Note:
This field has a character limit. If the search exceeds the limit, no results will be displayed. In that case, try reducing the number of IDs in the search.
Location Search and Multi-Location Add-On
If the
Multi-Location Add-On
is active on the site, an additional checkbox option called
Include Service Areas
will appear.
If
Service Areas
are excluded, only the members who added the specified location to their contact details form will appear.
If
Service Areas
are included, members who added the specified location to their contact details form and those who added the specified location to their service areas will appear.
Multi-Option Filters
All dropdown filters on the Search Members page support selecting multiple options. Simply select the desired values within a filter to include them in the search results.

title: My Members » Search Members » Members Table
content:
Search Results Members Table
This is the search results table of all the members in the website. The table will vary its content based on the search parameters used in the search filters.
1. Status
This section explains the different account statuses available in the platform, defining what each status represents and how it affects a member's access and functionality. It also includes the profile image if the listing is set as an individual or the company logo if the listing is set to company.
For a detailed list of the different account statuses and how to edit them, refer to the following article:
Account Status
2. Contact Information
This section provides details about the member's contact information, including their name, listing type, email, phone number, location, and social media accounts.
Name (Individual) / Company Name (Company)
Displays the full name if the member is an individual. If the listing is set as a company, this field will show the registered company name.
Listing Type
Indicates whether the listing is an individual profile or a company account.
Email Address
Shows the registered email address associated with the member.
Company or Member Alternative Name
For individual listings, this field displays the company name if provided. For company listings, it shows the primary contact person’s name.
Phone Number
Displays the primary phone number associated with the member.
Geocoding Information
Includes geographic coordinates associated with the member’s location, helping to identify their approximate position on a map.
Social Media Accounts
Lists links to the member’s social media profiles, such as Facebook, LinkedIn, Twitter, or other platforms.
3. Actions Menu
The actions menu provides quick access to essential account management options for each member. These actions allow for profile updates, account maintenance, and communication.
The following article describes each option available in this menu:
My Members » Search Members » Actions Dropdown
4. Profile Views
If the
Profile Statistics Add-On
and setting are enabled, the amount of views the profile has received, will be displayed here. This setting is setup per membership plan.
5. Membership
The results table displays members who match the applied search criteria. Each row represents a member and contains key details.
Member ID
: A unique identification number assigned to each member.
Membership Plan
: Displays the membership plan associated with the member.
Join Date
: Indicates when the member joined the platform.
Last Login
: Shows the most recent login date of the member.
Category
: Displays the primary category under which the member is classified.
Parent Account ID
: If the
Multi-Member Manager
add-on is activated on the site, this field shows the ID of the parent account.
6. Revenue
This column is a financial overview of the member. It displays information like:
The total of any past due payments.
Credits available
.
The revenue generated by the member.

title: My Members » Search Members » Sorting Options
content:
Sorting Options
The sorting options enable organizing the member results table based on various attributes.
Sort Name A-Z
Arranges members in alphabetical order by name.
Sort Name Z-A
Arranges members in reverse alphabetical order.
Sort ID Highest
Displays members by descending order of their ID numbers.
Sort ID Lowest
Displays members by ascending order of their ID numbers.
Sort Newest First
Displays the most recently joined members first.
Sort Oldest First
Displays the longest-standing members first.
Sort Most Revenue
Sorts members based on the highest revenue generated.
Sort Least Revenue
Sorts members based on the lowest revenue generated.
Sort Most Credits
Displays members with the highest credit balance first.
Sort Least Credits
Displays members with the lowest credit balance first.
Sort Most Likes
Sorts members based on the number of likes received.
Sort Least Likes
Displays members with the fewest likes.
Sort Most Views
Sorts members based on the highest number of profile views.
Sort Least Views
Displays members with the lowest number of profile views.

title: Users API - How to Manage Users with API Calls
content:
The API allows for creating, reading, updating, deleting, and searching users within the database. Below is a list of available endpoints and their usage.
To search for members by address, enable the setting:
Enable All Location Features for "Pretty URL" Search Results Pages (Additional Google Maps API Cost)
in the site's
Advanced Settings
.
For detailed instructions, please refer to the guide here:
Set Up Pretty URLs with Google Maps
.
Available Endpoints
Below is a list of the available endpoints for managing users:
https://example.com/api/v2/user/get
(list / filter users)
https://example.com/api/v2/user/get/{user_id}
(get a single user by ID)
https://example.com/api/v2/user/create
https://example.com/api/v2/user/update
https://example.com/api/v2/user/delete
https://example.com/api/v2/user/search
https://example.com/api/v2/user/transactions
Get a Single User by ID
Retrieve the full record for one user using their
user_id
in the URL path.
Parameter Notes
: Pass the
user_id
as a path parameter.
Endpoint
:
GET https://example.com/api/v2/user/get/{user_id}

curl -H "X-Api-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" "https://example.com/api/v2/user/get/3"
Returns the full user record wrapped in a one-item array under
message
.
List / Filter Users
List users or filter them by any field. This endpoint returns
all matching records
(paginated) — it is NOT limited to a single result. Use it any time you need to find members by
email
,
first_name
,
last_name
,
subscription_id
,
profession_id
,
active
,
city
,
country_code
, or any other field on the user record.
Parameter Notes
: Call with no parameters to enumerate all users (paginated). Add
property
+
property_value
to filter by a specific field. Optionally add
property_operator
to control the match type (defaults to
=
).
Endpoint
:
GET https://example.com/api/v2/user/get
Example Requests:
# Enumerate all users (paginated, default 25 per page)
GET https://example.com/api/v2/user/get

# Find every user named John (exact match, any number of results)
GET https://example.com/api/v2/user/get?property=first_name&property_value=John

# Find one user by exact email
GET https://example.com/api/v2/user/get?property=email&property_value=jane@example.com

# Partial match using LIKE with % wildcards
GET https://example.com/api/v2/user/get?property=email&property_value=john%25&property_operator=LIKE

# Filter users on a specific membership plan
GET https://example.com/api/v2/user/get?property=subscription_id&property_value=3

# Control page size
GET https://example.com/api/v2/user/get?limit=50
Query Parameters:
property
The field name to filter on. Any user-record field works (e.g.,
user_id
,
email
,
first_name
,
last_name
,
subscription_id
,
profession_id
,
active
,
city
,
country_code
).
property_value
The value to match against the chosen field.
property_operator
Match type. Defaults to
=
(exact match). Use
LIKE
with
%
wildcards in
property_value
for partial matches (e.g.,
property_value=john%25
to find emails starting with "john"). URL-encode
%
as
%25
.
limit
Maximum results per page. Default 25.
page
Page number for paginated results.

Managing Profile Images via API
The following parameters are accepted:
cover_photo
,

,

.
Re-importing an image replaces the one on the profile straight away. Each import writes the file under a new unique name, so browsers and any image CDN fetch the new picture rather than continuing to serve a cached copy of the old one. Removing the existing image first is not required in order to replace it.
To delete an image outright, use the
images_action
parameter with one of the following values:
remove_all
- Removes all images.
remove_cover_image
- Removes only the cover photo.
remove_logo_image
- Removes only the logo.
remove_profile_image
- Removes only the profile photo.
Important:
Use auto_image_import = 1.
Profile URL Changes and 301 Redirects
When an update changes the member's profile URL, a 301 redirect is created automatically from the old URL to the new one, the same way the admin member edit screen does. Previously the API changed the URL without creating a redirect, so the old address returned a 404. To skip the redirect on a single request, send
create_301_redirect = 0
.

title: Understanding and Editing Schema Markup in Brilliant Directories
content:
What is Schema Markup?
Schema markup is a type of structured data that helps search engines understand the content of a webpage more effectively. Implementing schema correctly can improve search visibility and enhance rich snippets in search results.
Does Brilliant Directories Automatically Add Schema?
Brilliant Directories includes some schema markup by default in various parts of the website, but users can also add or modify schema based on their needs. Additionally, schema can be added anywhere on the website where structured data is needed, providing full flexibility for customization.
When a member profile has approved reviews, aggregateRating and review are added to that profile's LocalBusiness schema automatically — no widget change or custom markup is required.  All search results pages automatically include ItemList Schema.
Where Can Schema Be Edited in Brilliant Directories?
If customization or additions to schema markup are required for a Brilliant Directories website, the following are the main areas where schema can be edited:
Widgets
Schema markup is included in several system widgets that control how information is displayed on different pages:
Bootstrap Theme - Member Profile - Display Member Address
Bootstrap Theme - Function - Display Breadcrumbs
Bootstrap Theme - Social Media Links
Bootstrap Theme - Global Website - Schema Markup
Bootstrap Theme - Footer - Scripts
Bootstrap Theme - Detail Page - Schema Markup - Community Article
Bootstrap Theme - Detail Page - Schema Markup - Website Blog Article
Bootstrap Theme - Detail Page - Schema Markup - Event Post Type
Bootstrap Theme - Detail Page - Schema Markup - Jobs Post Type
Bootstrap Theme - Detail Page - Schema Markup - Video Post Type
Bootstrap Theme - Detail Page - Schema Markup - Property Listing Post Type
Bootstrap Theme - Detail Page - Schema Markup - Product Post Type
Add-On - Bootstrap Theme - Global Search - Sitesearch HEAD Schema
Add-On - Bootstrap Theme - Posts - Comments UI
Bootstrap Theme - Single Post Page
Post Types
The search results pages of these post types have the schema markup directly in the post type code by default:
Member Article
Website Blog Article
Videos
Jobs
Events
Coupons
Soundcloud
Discussions
Properties
Products
Photo Albums
Classified
Digital Products
This can be seen directly in the edit post setting section in the search results tab. Below the example for the Member Articles:
Note:
This part of the post type default code. If the code marked below is not showing, it will be required to restore the Default code following the guide below:
How to Reset to Default Post Types Code
Reviews Post Type Code: This can be edited in the
Profile Page Design tab
.
SEO & Static Pages
Schema markup can be added to all
SEO pages
and
static pages
within Brilliant Directories.
Quick Edit Section
Unique schema can be added per member in the head section via the
Quick Edit
feature.
How to Add or Modify Schema Markup
To add or modify schema markup, consider the following methods:
Editing the relevant widget within the Widget Manager.
Adding schema directly into the SEO Templates for specific page types.
Utilizing the Quick Edit option to add schema per member profile.
Adding schema manually into the head section of pages where necessary.
Implementing schema markup correctly can improve search rankings and provide search engines with better-structured data. Leveraging the available options in Brilliant Directories ensures the website is optimized for better visibility and user experience.
Note:
By default, Website & Organization Schema are now included in footer for all BD sites in the widget
Bootstrap Theme - Footer - Scripts
. This can be viewed by using a tool like Schema Validator (
https://validator.schema.org
)
Structured Data Testing Guide
After adding or editing schema markup in your Brilliant Directories website, it's essential to
test and validate the structured data
to ensure it's correctly implemented and eligible for rich results in Google Search.
Below are step-by-step instructions to test your schema using
Google's Rich Results Test
and how to apply these tools to member profile pages or post pages.
Using Google's Rich Results Test
This tool checks whether your page supports rich results (like star ratings, events, or FAQs) in Google Search.
Go to
Google’s Rich Results Test
.
In the
“Test your URL”
field, enter the full link to a
member profile or post
on your BD website (e.g.,
https://yourdomain.com/jane-doe
).
Click
"Test URL"
.
Wait a few seconds while the page is analyzed.
Review the results:
If your page is eligible for rich results, you'll see a success message and the types detected.
If there are errors or warnings, they will be displayed with guidance for fixing them.
Pro Tip:
Use this tool to verify that common schemas like
LocalBusiness
,
Article
, or
Event
are working as expected.

title: Changelog - March 2025
content:
New Features:
Added functionality to search for multiple members by ID using comma-separated notation in the keyword search filter on the Search Members page in Admin. For example, searching for the keyword "#1,2,3" will return the members with IDs 1, 2, and 3.
Added support for the Finnish language
.
Added support for 6 new languages to the Default Website Language setting: Ukrainian, Spanish (Spain), Russian, Slovenian, Slovak, and Albanian.
Enhancements / Fixes:
Implemented bug fixes and performance enhancements to the Import Business Data tool in Admin.
Resolved an issue preventing the Billing Cronjob from executing correctly in some scenarios.
Enhanced compatibility between the "Chat Messages" sidebar link in Member Dashboard and the "Enable Private Chat Messages" Membership Plan Setting.
Fixed Date Picker functionality when creating or editing posts with customized "Member Dashboard URL: Add Post" and "Member Dashboard URL: Add Multi-Photo Post" Advanced Settings.
Made several improvements to the Change Domain Wizard tool in the Domain Manager section of Admin panel.
Modified the Froala Email WYSIWYG editor to use rendered image dimensions (width/height attributes) instead of the original image size when uploading images to Email Templates.
Resolved an issue affecting Digital Product purchases when using the Razorpay payment gateway.
Enhanced the "Google Website Translator" Add-On to prevent translation of member names on public-facing pages.
Fixed an issue that prevented the "Predictive Keyword Search" Add-On from functioning correctly in specific scenarios.
Resolved a bug affecting selecting a country as a Service Area in the Member Dashboard.
