keeps date values in the format the platform expects for post group dates, so date handling behaves consistently. Leaving the column on the older type does not break the current site, but it keeps the column out of step with the expected structure.
How to Run It
From the admin dashboard, find the
Install New Updates
module and click
Check For Updates
.
If the column type needs correcting,
Update Expire Date for Posts
appears in the list. Click
Install
.
After it completes, click
Check For Updates
again to confirm the entry is gone.
After Running
Nothing changes visibly on the website. The
group_date
column is now stored as a
TIMESTAMP
, and the existing group records are preserved. There is nothing to reconfigure afterward.

title: Menu Migration - Dashboard Installer
content:
The
Install New Updates
module on the admin dashboard lists one-time platform installers that still have pending steps on the site. Clicking the green
Check For Updates
button refreshes the list — an installer only appears when the site actually has something left to install, and it disappears from the list once its steps are complete.
What Menu Migration Does
This installer modernizes how the website stores menu settings. It has two separate steps, and each one runs only if the database still needs it.
Migrate menu disable data
: older sites recorded whether a menu was turned off in the general settings table (
users_meta
, as rows where
database
is
menus
and
key
is
disable
). This step moves that setting onto the menu itself by writing the
menu_active
column on the
menus
table, then deletes the old
users_meta
rows. A menu that was marked disabled becomes
menu_active = 0
and one that was not becomes
menu_active = 1
, so the menus keep the same on/off state, just stored in the newer location.
Update menu title column
: this step makes sure the
menu_title
column on the
menu_items
table is a
VARCHAR(255)
field with Unicode (utf8) support, so menu titles up to 255 characters and special characters are stored correctly. If the
menu_items
table does not exist, this step is skipped.
Why It Appears
The installer appears when either step still has work to do. The first step is pending when the
users_meta
table still contains menu
disable
rows that have not been moved yet. The second step is pending when the
menu_title
column is not yet a
VARCHAR(255)
field. If there is no leftover disable data and the menu title column is already correct, the installer does not appear.
These are legacy conditions. Sites created before menu settings moved to their current storage will see the installer offered, while newer sites already have both in place. Seeing it does not mean anything is broken; it means the database predates one or both of these updates.
Why It Matters
Moving the disable setting onto the
menus
table keeps each menu's on/off state with the menu itself, which is where newer platform features read it from, and it clears stale rows out of
users_meta
. Widening the menu title column prevents long menu titles or special characters from being cut off. Skipping the installer will not immediately break the menus, but it leaves menu settings on the older structures that newer features are not built for.
How to Run It
From the admin dashboard, find the
Install New Updates
module and click
Check For Updates
.
If the site has pending steps,
Menu Migration
appears in the list. Click
Install
.
After it completes, click
Check For Updates
again. The entry disappears once both steps are done.
If Menu Migration does not appear in the list, the website is already up to date, so there is nothing to do.
After Running
Nothing changes visibly on the website. The menus keep the same on/off state and the same titles; only where those settings are stored changes. There is nothing to reconfigure afterward.
Each step re-checks the database before running: the migration step only runs while leftover disable rows exist and reports that the data was already migrated once they are gone, and the title-column step is offered only while the column still needs widening. Because of these checks, the installer is safe to run even if part of the update was already applied earlier.

title: Coming Soon Page - Dashboard Installer
content:
The
Install New Updates
module on the admin dashboard lists one-time platform installers that still have pending steps on the site. Clicking the green
Check For Updates
button refreshes the list — an installer only appears when the site actually has something left to install, and it disappears from the list once its steps are complete.
What Coming Soon Page Does
This installer adds a ready-made Coming Soon page template to the site, the kind of pre-launch page that invites visitors to pre-register while the directory is still being built. It runs two steps: one creates the template and its design settings, the other makes sure the new template sorts to the front of the template list. It adds a new template, it does not change the existing pages.
The two steps do the following:
Create the template
: inserts a new row into the
list_seo
table with
seo_type
set to
coming_soon_page
. The template ships with a headline of
We Are Launching Soon
, a nickname of
Coming Soon Page
, and page content that includes a two-column layout with a pre-register form (
[form=coming_soon_form]
) and a list of reasons to join. It then inserts a set of
users_meta
rows tied to that template that hold the hero section design settings, including
enable_hero_section
, heading font sizes, weights and colors, hero alignment and column width, top and bottom padding, the hero background image (
/images/freshbg.jpg
), and overlay color and opacity.
Fix template order
: if there are templates with an empty filename and the Coming Soon template is not the first of them by ID, this step assigns new higher IDs to the other empty-filename templates so the Coming Soon Page template sorts first, updating the matching
users_meta
rows to keep them linked.
Why It Appears
The installer runs two status checks and appears whenever at least one has work to do. In plain terms, it shows up when the
list_seo
table has no row with
seo_type
=
coming_soon_page
, or when templates with an empty filename exist and the Coming Soon template is not sorted first among them.
Seeing it does not mean anything is broken, it means the site does not yet have the Coming Soon page template, or that template is not yet in its expected position in the list.
Why It Matters
The template gives the site a pre-built launch page with a pre-registration form and a styled hero section, so interest can be collected before the directory goes fully live without building the page from scratch. The ordering step keeps the new template positioned as expected in the template list. Skipping the installer simply means this ready-made Coming Soon page will not be available to use.
How to Run It
From the admin dashboard, find the
Install New Updates
module and click
Check For Updates
.
If the site has pending steps,
Coming Soon Page
appears in the list. Click
Install
.
After it completes, click
Check For Updates
again. The entry disappears once all steps are done.
If Coming Soon Page does not appear in the list, the website is already up to date. The module only shows installers with pending steps, so there is nothing to do.
After Running
A new Coming Soon Page template is available in the site's templates, complete with the launch headline, the pre-register form, and the hero section design settings. The existing pages and templates are untouched.
The create-template step inserts the new template without first checking whether one already exists, so it should be run only when the module offers it rather than forced, to avoid creating a duplicate. The ordering step does re-check the template order before making any change. Once the template is present, the module stops listing the installer, so clicking
Check For Updates
again is the safe way to confirm the work is done.

title: Revision Count - Post Types Update - Dashboard Installer
content:
The
Install New Updates
module on the admin dashboard lists one-time platform installers that still have pending steps on the site. Clicking the green
Check For Updates
button refreshes the list — an installer only appears when the site actually has something left to install, and it disappears from the list once its steps are complete.
What Revision Count - Post Types Update Does
This installer makes three small database structure changes that newer post type features rely on. It adds a save-counter column to the post tables and relaxes two real estate fields so they can be left empty. It changes how data is stored, it does not delete or rewrite the posts.
The three steps do the following:
Revision count column
: adds a
revision_count
column (BIGINT, default 0) to both the
data_posts
table and the
users_portfolio_groups
table, placed after the
state_sn
column. This column counts how many times a post has been saved.
Property square footage
: changes the
property_sqr_foot
column on the
users_portfolio_groups
table to
DECIMAL(10,2)
that allows empty (NULL) values, so the field can be left blank.
Property price
: changes the
property_price
column on the
users_portfolio_groups
table to
DECIMAL(20,2)
that allows empty (NULL) values, so the field can be left blank. If the site does not have a
property_price
column at all, this step reports nothing to run and is skipped.
Why It Appears
The installer runs three status checks against the database structure and appears whenever at least one still has work to do. In plain terms, it shows up when
revision_count
is missing from either
data_posts
or
users_portfolio_groups
, when the
property_sqr_foot
column does not yet allow empty values, or when the
property_price
column does not yet allow empty values.
These are legacy conditions. Databases created before these column updates became standard will see the installer offered. Seeing it does not mean anything is broken, it means the database predates one or more of these structure updates.
Why It Matters
The
revision_count
column gives the platform a place to track how many times a post has been saved, which post type features use. Allowing the property square footage and property price fields to hold empty values means members can leave those fields blank instead of being forced to enter a number, which matters for real estate style post types. Skipping the installer will not break the current site, but it leaves the database on the older structures that these features expect.
How to Run It
From the admin dashboard, find the
Install New Updates
module and click
Check For Updates
.
If the site has pending steps,
Revision Count - Post Types Update
appears in the list. Click
Install
.
After it completes, click
Check For Updates
again. The entry disappears once all steps are done.
If Revision Count - Post Types Update does not appear in the list, the website is already up to date. The module only shows installers with pending steps, so there is nothing to do.
After Running
Nothing changes visibly on the website. The updates are internal database structure changes: the posts keep their existing data, the new
revision_count
column starts at 0, and the two property fields can now be saved empty. There is nothing to reconfigure afterward.
The revision count step re-checks both tables before adding the column, and the two property field steps re-apply the same column definition, so the installer is safe to run even if part of the update was applied earlier. Click
Check For Updates
again and the entry disappears once all three checks pass.

title: Clean Unused Data from users_clicks - Dashboard Installer
content:
The
Install New Updates
module on the admin dashboard lists one-time platform installers that still have pending steps on the site. Clicking the green
Check For Updates
button refreshes the list — an installer only appears when the site actually has something left to install, and it disappears from the list once its steps are complete.
What Clean Unused Data from users_clicks Does
This installer is a database cleanup task. The
users_clicks
table stores click and view tracking records tied to member listings. Over time it can hold rows for members who no longer exist, and this installer removes those orphaned rows.
Specifically, it deletes every row from
users_clicks
whose
user_id
has no matching row in the
users_data
table (the main member listing table). In plain terms, it clears out click tracking for members that have been deleted. Click records that still belong to existing members are left in place.
Why It Appears
The installer runs a check that joins
users_clicks
against
users_data
and looks for click rows with no matching member. If it finds one or more of these orphaned rows, the installer is offered. If every click row still maps to a real member, it reports that the table contains no unused data and does not appear.
Why It Matters
Orphaned click rows are dead weight. They reference members that are gone, so they cannot be used for anything, and clearing them keeps the
users_clicks
table smaller and cleaner. Nothing on the live website depends on them, so removing them has no visible effect.
How to Run It
From the admin dashboard, find the
Install New Updates
module and click
Check For Updates
.
If the site has orphaned click rows,
Clean Unused Data from users_clicks
appears in the list. Click
Install
.
After it completes, click
Check For Updates
again to confirm the entry is gone.
After Running
Nothing changes visibly on the website. The click rows for deleted members are removed, and tracking for the site's current members is preserved. Because the installer re-checks for orphaned rows every time it runs, it is safe to run again; if none remain, there is simply nothing to remove.

title: Folder Permissions Security - Dashboard Installer
content:
The
Install New Updates
module on the admin dashboard lists one-time platform installers that still have pending steps on the site. Clicking the green
Check For Updates
button refreshes the list — an installer only appears when the site actually has something left to install, and it disappears from the list once its steps are complete.
What Folder Permissions Security Does
This installer is a filesystem cleanup, not a database change. It connects to the website's hosting account, scans the folders under the site's
/public_html
directory (the web root where the files live), and finds any folders whose permissions are not set to the secure standard. It then resets those folders to permission mode
0755
. It only adjusts folder permissions; it does not move, rename, or delete any files or folders, and it does not touch the content.
In practical terms:
The installer opens a connection to the hosting account using the site's stored hosting credentials.
It walks the folders under
/public_html
and collects every folder that is not already at the correct permission.
It sets each of those folders to
0755
— the standard secure permission for web directories, where the account owner can read, write, and open the folder, and everyone else can only read and open it.
Why It Appears
Each time
Check For Updates
is clicked, this installer connects to the hosting account and scans
/public_html
for folders that are not at the secure permission. It appears in the list only when that scan finds at least one folder that still needs adjusting. If every folder is already set correctly, the installer reports that everything is fine and does not offer anything to install.
Folders can drift out of the secure setting for ordinary reasons — files uploaded through certain tools, restores, or migrations can leave folders with looser permissions than the platform standard. Seeing this installer does not mean the site has been tampered with; it means the scan found folders that are not yet locked down to the recommended setting.
Why It Matters
Folder permissions control who is allowed to read and change the files inside a directory on the server. Folders left with permissions looser than
0755
can be writable or accessible more broadly than they should be, which is a security weakness. Tightening every folder under the web root to the
0755
standard closes that gap and keeps the site's files under the correct level of protection. It is a security hardening step; it will not change how the website looks or behaves for visitors.
How to Run It
From the admin dashboard, find the
Install New Updates
module and click
Check For Updates
.
If the site has folders that need adjusting,
Folder Permissions Security
appears in the list. Click
Install
.
After it completes, click
Check For Updates
again — the entry disappears once every folder is at the secure permission.
If Folder Permissions Security does not appear in the list, the folders are already secured — the module only shows installers with pending steps, so there is nothing to do.
After Running
Nothing changes visibly on the website. The files, folders, and content are all left exactly where they were; only the permission settings on the affected folders are tightened to
0755
. There is nothing to reconfigure afterward.
The installer re-scans the folders every time it runs and only adjusts the ones that are still out of compliance, so it is safe to run again. Click
Check For Updates
after installing, and the entry disappears once the scan finds no remaining folders to fix.

title: Convert tables From MyISAM to INNODB - Dashboard Installer
content:
The
Install New Updates
module on the admin dashboard lists one-time platform installers that still have pending steps on the site. Clicking the green
Check For Updates
button refreshes the list — an installer only appears when the site actually has something left to install, and it disappears from the list once its steps are complete.
What Convert tables From MyISAM to INNODB Does
This installer modernizes how the website's database tables are stored. It finds any tables still using the older
MyISAM
storage engine and converts them to
InnoDB
, the modern engine that newer database versions and platform features expect. It changes the storage engine only; it does not delete, rewrite, or reorder the data inside the tables.
How the conversion works:
The installer connects to the website database and looks up every table still on the
MyISAM
engine.
It converts them to
InnoDB
with a standard
ALTER TABLE ... ENGINE=InnoDB
operation, processing the
smallest tables first
.
Each run works within a
45-second time budget
. If there are large tables and the budget is reached before every table is done, the remaining tables are left for the next run. This is deliberate: it keeps large log tables from causing the request to time out.
Two tables —
website_layouts
and
website_layouts_old
— are intentionally skipped. Their rows are too wide for InnoDB's row-size limit and cannot be converted without schema changes, so the installer leaves them on MyISAM by design.
Why It Appears
Each time
Check For Updates
is clicked, this installer counts the tables in the database that are still on the
MyISAM
engine (ignoring the two skipped layout tables). It appears in the list only when that count is greater than zero — that is, when at least one convertible table is still on MyISAM. Once every eligible table has been converted to InnoDB, the count is zero and the installer no longer appears.
This is a legacy condition. Databases created before InnoDB became the platform standard will have MyISAM tables to convert, while newer databases are already on InnoDB throughout. Seeing this installer does not mean anything is broken; it means the database still has one or more tables on the older engine.
Why It Matters
InnoDB is the modern MySQL storage engine and the one newer database server versions and platform features are built for. It supports row-level locking and transactional integrity that MyISAM does not, which makes tables more reliable under concurrent activity and better protected against corruption. Converting the remaining MyISAM tables brings the database in line with the current standard. Leaving them on MyISAM will not break the current site, but it keeps those tables on an engine that newer features are not designed around.
How to Run It
From the admin dashboard, find the
Install New Updates
module and click
Check For Updates
.
If the database still has MyISAM tables,
Convert tables From MyISAM to INNODB
appears in the list. Click
Install
.
After it completes, click
Check For Updates
again — the entry disappears once every eligible table has been converted.
If the installer does not appear in the list, the tables are already on InnoDB — the module only shows installers with pending steps, so there is nothing to do.
After Running
Nothing changes visibly on the website. The data in the tables is preserved exactly as it was; only the underlying storage engine is switched from MyISAM to InnoDB. There is nothing to reconfigure afterward.
Because each run works within a time budget and processes tables smallest-first, a database with large tables may not finish in a single pass. When that happens, the installer reports how many tables still remain and stays in the list — simply run it again to continue where it left off. Each run re-checks which tables are still on MyISAM before converting, so it is safe to run repeatedly until none remain and the entry disappears.

title: BD Butler: Scheduled AI Tasks, Skills and Routines
content:
BD Butler can create website content as a one-time task or automatically on a recurring schedule.
Scheduled tasks run in the background through Brilliant Directories. The website admin does not need to remain open, and the computer does not need to stay turned on while a task is running.
This article expands on the main
BD Butler
article and covers the Tasks, Skills, and Routines available inside BD Butler PRO.
[Read] BD Butler
[WATCH] AI Website Automation: Schedule Content Creation
[WATCH] Scheduled AI Tasks: Create Website Content While You Sleep
Understanding Skills, Tasks and Routines
BD Butler uses three connected components:
Skill:
A predefined job BD Butler knows how to complete, such as creating a blog article, event, or job listing.
Routine:
A saved Task that runs repeatedly according to a selected schedule.
Task:
A single execution of a selected Skill.
For example, the
Create a Job Listing
Skill can be run once as a Task or saved as a Routine that searches for and creates new job listings every week.
Available Skills
The following 3 built-in Skills are currently available.
Create a Blog Article
Researches a topic related to the website and
creates an article
that can include:
SEO-focused written content
An article image
Internal links to related website content
Links to relevant external sources
Post and SEO details
Create an Event Post
Searches for a real upcoming event and creates an
event post
using information from the event’s official source.
The instructions can focus the search by:
Location
Industry
Event type
Audience
Date range
Create a Job Listing
Searches for an active
job opportunity
and creates a formatted job listing.
The instructions can focus the search by:
Job title
Industry
Location
Experience level
Employer type
When information is available, the generated listing can also include compensation details and a link to the employer’s official job page.
Create a New Task
Click the
New
Task
tab.
Select the
Skill
to run:
Blog, Event, Job
Enter a nickname for the Task.
Add Custom Instructions
Custom instructions tell BD Butler what type of content to create.
This field is optional. Without additional instructions, BD Butler can review the website name, URL, menus, categories, footer links, and recent content to determine a relevant topic.
Adding instructions provides greater control over the results.
Blog Article Example
Create articles about preparing for a first half marathon. Cover training plans, recovery, nutrition, and choosing a running coach.
Event Post Example
Find upcoming small-business networking events in Austin, Texas. Only include events with an official registration page.
Job Listing Example
Find active remote marketing manager positions at software companies in the United States.
Instructions can also define the preferred structure, including:
Article length
Sections to include
Locations to target
Topics to avoid
Preferred audience
Whether FAQs or bullet points should be included
Internal or external linking preferences
For recurring Routines, use instructions broad enough to produce different results during future runs while remaining focused on the same subject.
Choose the Number of Posts
Select how many items BD Butler should create during each run.
Available quantities include:
1 post (2 credits)
2 posts
(4 credits)
3 posts
(6 credits)
A maximum of three posts can be created during one Task. Keeping each run within this limit helps maintain consistent research and content quality.
For a Routine, the selected quantity will be created each time the Routine runs.
For example, a weekly Routine set to create three blog articles will attempt to create three new articles during every weekly run.
Choose Draft or Published Status
Select how the generated content should be saved.
Publish Live
The content is published automatically after the Task is completed successfully.
Before using this option with a recurring Routine, run the Task at least once in draft mode and review the results.
Save as Draft
The content is created but does not appear publicly until it is reviewed and published manually.
Draft mode is recommended when testing a new Skill, prompt, or recurring Routine.
Choose the Post Author
Select the member or admin account that will be assigned as the author of the generated content.
The selected author will appear as the content owner when the post is created. One author can be selected for each Task or Routine.
Schedule the Task
A Task can run once or be placed on a recurring schedule.
Run Once Now
Runs the Task one time immediately.
This option is useful for:
Testing new instructions
Reviewing the type of content produced
Creating a single article, event, or job listing
Confirming the selected author and post status
Hourly
Runs the Task approximately once every hour.
Daily
Runs the Task approximately once each day.
Weekly
Runs the Task on selected days of the week.
Different Routines can be assigned to different days. For example:
Monday: Industry blog articles
Wednesday: Upcoming events
Friday: New job listings
Scheduled Tasks may run up to approximately 15 minutes before or after the selected time. This built-in offset helps distribute scheduled processing and means a Routine may not always begin at the exact minute shown.
Set the Number of Runs
Recurring Routines can continue until they are manually stopped or can be limited to a specific number of runs.
A run limit can be useful for short content campaigns.
Once the selected number of runs has been completed, the Routine stops automatically.
Manage Existing Routines
Saved Routines can be managed from the Routines list.
Available actions can include:
Start or stop a Routine
Edit the Routine settings
Run the Routine manually
Clone the Routine
Review previous runs
Edit a Routine
Editing a Routine changes the settings used during its next run.
This can be used to update:
Custom instructions
Content quantity
Author
Publishing status
Schedule
Run limit
Previously completed Tasks and content are not changed.
Clone a Routine
Cloning creates a copy that can be adjusted without changing the original Routine. For example, an existing job listing Routine can be cloned to target a different city, job title, or experience level.
Run a Routine Manually
A saved Routine can be run manually without waiting for its next scheduled time. This creates an additional Task using the Routine’s current settings.
Completed
The
Completed
tab provides a history of AI Tasks that are finished, currently processing, or were stopped before completion.
Each task card can display:
The task nickname
The selected Skill
Whether it was a manual or scheduled run
The date and time it started
The processing time
The number of credits used
The admin account that initiated the task
The current task status
Although the tab is labeled
Completed
, it also includes tasks that are still running or were stopped.
Filter the Task List
Use the available filters to locate a specific task.
The status dropdown includes:
Any Status
Done
Running
Stopped
Enter a task nickname in the
Filter by name
field to narrow the results further.
Click
Refresh
to check for updated task statuses.
Running Tasks
A task that is still processing displays a blue
Running
status.
Running tasks include a
Stop
button that can be used to cancel the task before it finishes.
The BD Butler window and browser do not need to remain open while a task is processing. Return to the Completed tab later and click
Refresh
to check its progress.
Completed Tasks
A successfully completed task displays a green
Done
status.
Completed task cards can also show:
How long the task took to complete
How many credits were used
A
Re-Run
button
An arrow for opening additional task details and results
Use
Re-Run
to repeat the task using the same configuration.
Stopped Tasks
A canceled task displays a red
Stopped
status.
The task card includes a message confirming that the task was canceled. When applicable, it will also confirm that no credits were used.
Stopped tasks can be run again by clicking
Re-Run
.

title: Create Custom Checkout And Sign Up Forms
content:
This article explains how to assign a custom signup or checkout form to each membership plan.
Edit Checkout Pages: Overview
This feature allows different membership plans to collect different information during signup. For example, a free member plan can use a short basic signup form, while a paid professional plan can collect additional business, billing, or profile details during checkout.
Overview
By default, websites include signup forms for different membership signup and checkout flows. These forms control which fields display when a new member signs up for a membership plan.
There are three default signup forms available:
Member - Sign Up - Free
Member - Sign Up - Paid
Member - Sign Up - External Payment
Each form is designed for a specific type of membership plan or checkout flow.
Difference Between On-Site and Off-Site Payment Gateways
Form Name
Shortcode
Used For
Member - Sign Up - Free
[form=signup_free]
Free membership plans
Member - Sign Up - Paid
[form=whmcs_signup_paid]
Paid membership plans using onsite checkout
Member - Sign Up - External Payment
[form=whmcs_signup_external]
Paid membership plans using an *
off-site
payment gateway, such as PayPal
Step 1: Clone the Signup Form
Start by cloning the existing signup form that matches the type of membership plan being customized.
How To Clone a Form
Clone
Member - Sign Up - Free
for a free membership plan.
Clone
Member - Sign Up - Paid
for a paid membership plan using onsite checkout.
Clone
Member - Sign Up - External Payment
for a paid membership plan using an *
off-site payment gateway
.
The cloned form will include the required signup fields and system settings from the original form.
Step 2: Rename the Cloned Form
After cloning the form, rename it so it can be selected inside the membership plan settings.
The form name must start with:
Member - Sign Up
Naming examples:
Member - Sign Up - Free - Basic Plan
Member - Sign Up - Free - Community Plan
Member - Sign Up - Paid - Professional Plan
Member - Sign Up - Paid - Business Plan
Member - Sign Up - External Payment - Sponsor Plan
Use a clear name that identifies which membership plan the form is intended for.
If the form name does not start with
Member - Sign Up
, it will not appear as an option in the membership plan signup form setting.
Step 3: Customize the Form Fields
After the form has been cloned and renamed, edit the form fields as needed.
How To Customize a Form
Fields can be added, removed, renamed, reordered, or marked as required based on the information that should be collected during signup.
When editing the form, keep the following in mind:
Do not remove required system fields needed for signup or checkout.
Do not remove payment fields from paid signup forms.
Do not add payment fields to free signup forms.
Do not change the checkout flow by using the wrong form type.
Keep the form focused on the information needed at signup.
Save the form after making changes.
Important:
If a required checkout or registration field is removed, the signup process may not work correctly.
Step 4: Assign the Form to a Membership Plan
After the custom signup form has been created, assign it to the membership plan.
Go to
Finance >> Membership Plans
.
Click
Edit
for the membership plan that needs a custom signup form.
Use the admin search field at the top of the page and search for
Sign Up Form
.
In the
Sign Ups & Upgrades
section, find the
Sign Up Form
setting.
Select the signup form from the dropdown.
The selected form will now be used when new members sign up for that membership plan.
Note:
For a form to appear as an option in the dropdown, the form name must start with
Member - Sign Up
.
Keep Signup Forms Short for Better Conversions
When customizing signup forms, it is best to keep the form as short and focused as possible.
5 Ways to Optimize Checkout Pages to Increase Membership Sign Ups
Create a Signup Form That Works!
Long checkout forms can reduce signup conversions because they create extra work before the user has completed registration. If a form feels too long, repetitive, or tedious, users may exit before finishing the signup process.
A shorter form helps users complete signup faster and creates a smoother checkout experience.
Recommended Signup Form Guidelines
Only ask for information that is needed during signup.
Move non-essential profile details to the member dashboard after signup.
Avoid asking for the same information in multiple ways.
Use clear field labels so members understand what to enter.
Keep required fields limited to the most important information.
Use optional fields for details that are helpful but not required.
For example, a paid business plan may need the member’s name, email, company name, phone number, billing information, and payment details at checkout.
However, details such as a full business description, social media links, extra images, certifications, or extended profile content can often be collected later from the member dashboard.
Important Form Requirements
Do not assign the free signup form to a paid membership plan. Paid plans need the correct paid or external payment form so the checkout process can work properly.
Do not assign the onsite paid signup form to a free membership plan. Free plans do not require payment fields, and adding payment fields to a free signup can create confusion during the signup process.
Do not assign the onsite paid signup form to a plan that uses an
off-site payment gateway
. Off-site payment plans need the external payment signup form so the off-site payment flow works as expected.
Common Mistakes to Avoid
Creating a new form from scratch:
Clone the existing free, paid, or external payment signup form instead.
Using the wrong form type:
Free plans should use free signup forms. Paid plans should use the correct paid or external payment signup form.
Using the wrong form name:
The form name must start with
Member - Sign Up
.
Making the form too long:
Long forms can reduce completed signups.
Removing required checkout fields:
Removing required system fields can break registration or checkout.
Not testing the signup flow:
Always test the form after assigning it to a membership plan.

title: How to Migrate a Domain Connection from A Record to CNAME
content:
A CNAME connection uses the site's unique
directoryup.com
target instead of tying a hostname to a server IP. This allows the connection to follow the website when its hosting server changes.
Before starting
Have access to the DNS provider that currently hosts the domain's records. Record the existing values, confirm the website being connected, and preserve email and unrelated service records. This procedure changes DNS pointing; it does not require changing the website's domain name.
Update www or another subdomain
Open
Settings > Domain Manager > Domain
.
Locate the site's connection details.
Copy the unique
directoryup.com
target.
Open the current DNS provider's record editor.
Replace the conflicting address record for the intended hostname with a CNAME to the copied target.
Save the change.
Return to Domain Manager and click
Check again
.
Type:
CNAME
Name:
www, or the exact subdomain being connected
Value:
The site's unique directoryup.com target copied from Domain Manager
Remove only the record that conflicts at that hostname. A CNAME cannot share its hostname with ordinary A/AAAA records or other data. Do not remove unrelated MX, TXT, or mailbox records.
Handle the root domain separately
The root domain is the address without a prefix, such as
example.com
. DNS does not allow an ordinary CNAME record on the root, so the right record depends on the company that runs the domain's DNS. Do not delete a working root record before its replacement is ready.
Brilliant Directories nameservers:
nothing to change; the records are managed for the website.
Cloudflare:
Cloudflare flattens a CNAME on the root, so the root takes the same CNAME as www, pointing to the site's unique target.
GoDaddy:
GoDaddy does not allow a CNAME on the root. When the website uses the www version, keep the www CNAME and turn on GoDaddy
Domain Forwarding
so example.com forwards to https://www.example.com with
Permanent (301)
. When the website uses the version without www, the root keeps an A record instead, and forwarding must stay off.
Namecheap:
replace the root record with an
ALIAS
record for
@
pointing to the site's unique target. Namecheap does not allow an ALIAS alongside an existing A, AAAA, CNAME, or redirect record for the same host, so delete the current root record first.
Other DNS providers:
the root keeps an A record pointing to the server address shown in Domain Manager. An A record points at a fixed address, so if the website moves to a different server in the future, that one record needs the same update. Moving the domain's DNS to a free Cloudflare account avoids this.
Step-by-step instructions and the exact records for each case are in
Point the root domain
in the connection guide.
Verify the result
Confirm both the intended hostname and the root-domain behavior. The
Domain
tab can report separate results for each address. If Cloudflare proxying is enabled, a public DNS lookup may show Cloudflare addresses rather than the underlying CNAME; inspect the record in the connected Cloudflare DNS editor as well.
Finally, open the website over HTTPS and confirm email still works. See
DNS records in Domain Manager
for the distinction between editable records and a public DNS view.

title: Content » Web Page Builder » Draft System (Autosave)
content:
While editing a page in the Web Page Builder, the system automatically saves work in progress as a
draft
every few seconds. If the tab closes accidentally, the browser crashes, or the editor is closed before clicking Save, the changes aren't lost, the draft is offered back so editing can continue right where it left off.
This article explains how the draft system works, what counts as a change, and how to discard one.
How It Works
As edits are made in the Web Page Builder, the system silently saves a draft copy of the page every 2 seconds. A status badge next to the Save button reflects the current state, for example:
Saving Draft
— the draft is being written
Draft saved Just now
— the latest changes are saved as a draft
What Counts as a Change
The draft system captures any edit made in the page editor, including:
Typing or editing text (including single keystrokes, like adding a space)
Rearranging or restyling content
Inserting an image
Inserting a video
Changing Page Details and Page Options settings
Any of these will trigger the autosave and update the draft badge.
Drafts Don't Go Live
Saving a draft is
not
the same as publishing. Nothing written to a draft ever appears on the live, front-facing page until Save is explicitly clicked on the page.
This means edits can be made freely, experimenting, stepping away, or losing connection mid-edit, without any risk of half-finished changes showing up for site visitors. Clicking Save publishes the changes and clears the auto-saved draft, since it's no longer needed once the page is saved.
Discarding a Draft
To discard a draft, click the
"Discard Draft"
button. This deletes the draft and reverts the page back to its last saved (original) state.
How to Disable This Functionality
If needed, this functionality can be disabled under
Settings » Advanced Settings
by disabling the
Auto-Save Drafts
advanced setting.

title: Brilliant Directories Mobile App: Manage Your Website From Anywhere
content:
The Brilliant Directories mobile app gives website admins a convenient way to monitor important website activity directly from an iPhone. View member information, revenue, form submissions, account activity, and website statistics without needing to log in to the full Admin Dashboard from a browser.
The app is designed primarily for quick access and monitoring while away from a computer, making it easier to keep an eye on day-to-day website activity from one streamlined mobile dashboard.
Download and Log In to the Brilliant Directories App
The Brilliant Directories app can be downloaded from the Apple App Store by searching for
Brilliant Directories
. After installing the app, log in using the email address and password associated with a Brilliant Directories admin account.
https://apps.apple.com/app/brilliant-directories/id898641614?l=en-GB
On supported devices, the app can also use
Face ID
for faster sign-ins. When prompted, select whether to allow Brilliant Directories to use Face ID. This permission is optional and can also be managed through the device settings.
The app may also request permission to send notifications. Allowing notifications makes it possible for the app to display alerts as supported notifications become available. Notification permissions can be changed later through the iPhone settings.
APP
Face ID
Allow Notifications
View the Website Dashboard
After logging in, the
Home
screen provides a quick snapshot of the selected Brilliant Directories website.
The dashboard includes:
Members Snapshot:
View the total number of members along with activity for today, the last 7 days, and the last 30 days.
Revenue:
See total revenue along with revenue totals for today, the last 7 days, and the last 30 days.
Website Snapshot:
Confirm the website name, domain, Site ID, country, and current website status.
This screen is useful for quickly checking the overall status of a website without opening individual reports.
Switch Between Brilliant Directories Websites
Admins who manage more than one Brilliant Directories website can switch between sites directly from the app.
Tap the website selector near the top of the screen to open the website list. The search field can be used to locate a specific website, while the star icon identifies a favorite website for easier access.
Each website is displayed with its website name and Site ID, helping distinguish between multiple sites with similar names.
View Members
The
Members
tab provides quick access to member accounts associated with the selected website.
Each member entry displays basic information such as the member name, listing type, and account status. Tap the
+
icon to expand the member record and view additional information.
Expanded member details can include:
Email address
Phone number
Address
Revenue associated with the member
Tap the
−
icon to collapse the member details again.
A search field at the top of the screen can be used to filter the displayed member records when working with larger databases.
Monitor Revenue
The
Revenue
tab provides a mobile view of transactions associated with the website.
Each entry can display the transaction amount, payment status, and the membership plan or product connected with the payment. For example, an entry may show a
$100 Paid
transaction for a particular membership plan or a smaller payment associated with a one-time purchase.
Tap the
+
icon beside a transaction to view additional information when available.
Filter Revenue Records
The revenue search tools make it easier to locate a specific payment when multiple transactions are available.
Revenue records can be filtered using options such as:
User Email
User Name
Product Name
For example, selecting
User Email
and entering a member's email address can quickly narrow the transaction list to payments associated with that member.
Review Inbox Form Submissions
The
Inbox
tab provides access to website form submissions received through supported forms.
Each inbox entry identifies the form that generated the submission along with basic information such as the submitter's email address and submission date.
Tap the
+
icon to expand a submission and review the information submitted through the form. Depending on the form, this can include fields such as:
Name
Email
Phone Number
Message
For example, a submission from the website's Contact Us form can be expanded to view the visitor's contact information and message directly from the app.
Review Website Activity
The
Activity
tab provides a chronological view of activity recorded for the selected website.
Entries are organized by date and activity type, including categories such as
System
,
Admin Accounts
, and
Admin Action
.
Tap the
+
icon beside an activity entry to expand it and review additional details when available. This provides a quick way to check recent administrative or system activity while away from the full Admin Dashboard.
Search and Filter Information
Several sections of the app include a
Filter search
field that can be used to narrow the records currently displayed.
This is especially useful when a website contains a large number of members, transactions, form submissions, or activity records. Instead of scrolling through the complete list, enter identifying information to locate the relevant entry more quickly.
The bottom of applicable screens also displays how many records are currently loaded compared with the total number of available entries.
Access Account Options
Tap the profile icon in the upper-left corner of the app to open the account menu.
From this menu, admins can access:
Privacy Policy
Terms and Conditions
Log Out
Current app version information
The email address associated with the logged-in admin account is also displayed in this menu.
When to Use the BD App vs. the Full Admin Dashboard
The Brilliant Directories app is useful when an admin needs quick access to important website information without opening the full Admin Dashboard.
For example, an admin could use the app to check whether a new member has joined, confirm recent revenue, review a Contact Us submission, or see recent website activity while away from a computer.
For more extensive website configuration, content management, design changes, billing administration, or other advanced management tasks, the full Brilliant Directories Admin Dashboard remains the primary workspace.

title: Authorize.net Payment Gateway - Frequently Asked Questions
content:
1. If I update my
Authorize.Net
payment gateway to a new
Authorize.Net
account in BD, then for existing recurring members whose payment information is currently stored within Brilliant Directories, would BD continue to have access to the existing stored payment credentials after I configure the new Authorize.Net gateway?
Yes. The cards are stored encrypted in your site's billing system. Saving new Authorize.Net credentials only updates the gateway's own settings (the Login ID and Transaction Key). It does not change any member's stored card or any member's subscription.
2. When an existing member's next recurring invoice becomes due, would BD submit that member's existing stored payment information through the new Authorize.Net gateway, without requiring the member to re-enter their card information?
Yes. Each renewal is charged by sending the member's stored card to whichever Authorize.Net credentials are configured at the time the invoice is charged. Once the new credentials are saved, renewals go to the new account with nothing required from members.
3. If the existing stored payment information remains valid, would recurring billing therefore continue normally through the new gateway?
It should, as long as the new Authorize.Net account accepts the charges. That depends on the new account's own settings, which we can't see from our side, so before switching we recommend confirming these three things in the new account:
It accepts charges submitted without a card security code (CVV). Security codes are never stored, so renewals are always sent without one. If the new account declines transactions that have no security code, renewals would be declined.
Its address verification (AVS) filter won't decline renewal charges. On your current account, every renewal comes back with address verification marked as not applicable, so address checks have not been applied to your renewals so far.
Every card brand your members use is enabled. This includes American Express, which about a third of your members with a stored card use, and which some merchant accounts require enabling separately.
If one of these settings did cause declines, the fix would be adjusting that setting in the new Authorize.Net account. Members would not need to re-enter their cards.
4. Under what circumstances, if any, would an existing recurring member be required to re-enter or update their payment information solely because the Authorize.Net gateway account was changed?
For members with a stored card, none. Changing the account does not remove or invalidate their stored cards.
5. Please distinguish this from an underlying processor change on the same Authorize.Net gateway. My question specifically concerns replacing the existing Authorize.Net gateway account in BD with an entirely new Authorize.Net gateway account and new gateway credentials.
A processor change behind your existing Authorize.Net account keeps the same Login ID and Transaction Key, so nothing changes on the Brilliant Directories side and billing continues as it does today.
Replacing the account with a new Authorize.Net account and new credentials is the scenario covered above: stored cards stay in your site's billing system, and renewals start going to the new account.
On the ARB point: Brilliant Directories does not use Authorize.Net's recurring billing (ARB) subscriptions. Your site keeps its own renewal schedule and sends each renewal to Authorize.Net as an individual charge, so the ARB data that can't be migrated is not something your site relies on.
If you do decide to switch, it's done by editing the existing Authorize.net entry under
Finance > Payment Settings
in your admin and replacing the Login ID and Transaction Key.

title: Settings » Domain Manager » DNS Records
content:
The
DNS
tab in
Settings > Domain Manager
shows the records used by the website domain. Depending on where DNS is hosted, this tab is either an editor for the connected zone or a read-only view of public records.
Identify which mode is available
DNS arrangement
Available behavior
Connected Cloudflare account and matching domain
Read and edit records in the connected Cloudflare zone, including supported proxy controls.
Brilliant Directories nameservers and an available hosted zone
Read and edit the domain's BD-hosted DNS records.
Third-party DNS with the domain pointed at the BD site
Inspect public records. Make changes at the external DNS provider.
The tab may be absent when the website still uses a free platform address or the domain has no supported connection to inspect. Check
Domain
first.
On a website whose address is a subdomain, such as
members.example.com
, the tab shows the parent domain's zone (
example.com
). If the subdomain has been given its own separate DNS zone, its records are not listed here; manage them at the DNS provider for that zone.
Search and inspect editable records
Open
Settings > Domain Manager > DNS
.
Review
All DNS records
.
Use the search box to find a name or value.
Filter by record type when needed.
If a required record is not listed, click the
Show all
button below the list (for example,
Show all 31 records
). The default view lists the most relevant records first; a search or type filter always includes every matching record.
Refresh
reloads the record list. Copy controls help transfer an exact value without retyping it. Records can also be sorted by their name or type.
Brilliant Directories DNS example: selfautomated.com
A BD-hosted DNS zone filtered to CNAME records. Use the record filter and search to locate the required entry.
Cloudflare DNS example: demotailwind.com
This is a separate domain using the Cloudflare editor. It illustrates the alternative DNS arrangement, rather than the next step for selfautomated.com. On a Cloudflare-connected site, the DNS tab also shows the Cloudflare connection,
Point your domain with a different DNS host
, and
Email delivery records
above the record list.
The connected Cloudflare DNS editor exposes the proxy controls. Website records are proxied in this example; sender-authentication records remain Direct.
Add or change a record
Confirm that the displayed zone is the intended domain.
Choose the add-record action, or the edit action on the existing record.
Select the required record type: A, AAAA, CNAME, TXT, or MX.
Enter the name and value supplied by the service being configured.
For supported Cloudflare address records, choose
Through Cloudflare
or
Direct
as appropriate.
Save the record.
Refresh the list and confirm the saved values.
The add-record form shown here returns to the selfautomated.com example with Brilliant Directories DNS. Expand Add a record to enter the values supplied by the service being configured.
For MX changes that require a specific priority, use the authoritative DNS provider’s full DNS editor. The basic record form does not expose a separate priority field. To move incoming email to a different provider, follow the checks in
Mailboxes and Email Routing
.
Website pointing records should use the site-specific instructions in
the connection guide
. Email-authentication records should use the values generated in
Emails > Sender Authentication
. Avoid generic examples for either task.
Changes affect the live domain.
Editing or deleting a record can interrupt the website, email, or another service. Keep the original values and remove only the intended record. Do not proxy mail-service or sender-authentication records that need Direct / DNS only access.
Inspect public records at another provider
Open
Public DNS records
.
Click
Check again
.
Review the record's purpose, value, and
Seen by
result.
Make any required correction at the DNS provider.
Return to the tab and recheck after the provider publishes the change.
The public view compares answers from Google and Cloudflare resolvers for the records it checks, including nameservers, web addresses, mail servers, SPF, other TXT records, DKIM, DMARC, and DNSSEC delegation records.
Google + Cloudflare
indicates agreement;
Needs attention
can indicate a missing record or differing answers. This view does not enumerate every possible hostname or grant editing access to the provider's zone.
Success means the intended value is saved in the authoritative DNS editor and the public checks reflect the required configuration. Public resolvers can temporarily disagree while cached answers expire.

title: Settings » Domain Manager » Cloudflare Connection and Settings
content:
The
Cloudflare
tab connects a Cloudflare-managed domain to Domain Manager. A connected account can support website pointing, DNS record management, email-authentication publication, and Cloudflare settings from the BD admin area.
Before starting
Use a custom domain that exists in an accessible Cloudflare account.
Have permission to authorize that account and domain.
Keep a record of the current DNS and email settings.
Use Sign in with Cloudflare to authorize your account and connect your domain to Domain Manager. For a free directoryup.com address, use the domain connection wizard to authorize Cloudflare and choose a custom domain.
For creating the Cloudflare zone and moving nameservers, see
Connecting a Site to Cloudflare
. Authorizing Domain Manager is separate from registering a domain or changing its nameservers.
Connect a domain while changing the website address
Open the domain connection wizard.
Select
Use a domain from my Cloudflare account
.
Sign in and authorize the intended account.
Filter the domain list and select the intended domain.
Choose the main address or enter the required subdomain.
Click
Use this address
to prepare its DNS records.
Review
Switch Over
, then complete its separate confirmation.
A domain whose main address is already in use can still offer an available subdomain. Selecting the main address also points the root domain; selecting a subdomain leaves other addresses on that domain unchanged.
The Cloudflare connection wizard offers the main domain or a subdomain after authorization.
Alternative: connect an account for the current domain
Use these steps when the website already has its domain and Cloudflare still needs to be connected. If the wizard above already connected the account, continue to the next section.
Open
Settings > Domain Manager > Cloudflare
.
Click
Sign in with Cloudflare
.
Sign in to the appropriate Cloudflare account.
Review and authorize the requested access.
Return to Domain Manager.
Confirm that
Connected to Cloudflare
shows the intended domain.
If sign-in cannot find the domain or authorization is unavailable, check the account and domain access before making changes. Do not continue using a connection associated with a different domain. A connection made earlier with a Cloudflare API token shows
An API token
under
Signed in using
, with a
Switch to signing in with Cloudflare
link. New connections use Cloudflare sign-in only.
A successful authorization identifies demotailwind.com as the connected Cloudflare domain.
Point the website and publish email records
Review the connected domain and the website's displayed target.
Use
Point my domain at my website
when that action is needed.
Review the resulting connection status.
Under
Email delivery records
, use
Add my email records to Cloudflare
when offered.
Open
Emails
and recheck sender authentication.
For changing the website to a different domain, follow the separate
connection wizard
. Pointing records and switching the website's primary address are distinct actions.
Manage DNS records
Use the
DNS
tab to inspect, add, edit, or delete supported records.
Through Cloudflare
sends supported website traffic through the Cloudflare proxy.
Direct
exposes the underlying DNS destination. Email-related records must use the mode required by the mail provider; sender-authentication CNAME records should remain Direct. See
DNS Records
.
Review Cloudflare settings
Set recommended defaults
applies the Domain Manager's recommended configuration. Review the current settings and the confirmation before applying it, especially when the domain already has a custom configuration.
Always use https
controls redirection to HTTPS.
Security level & bot fighting
controls the available security level.
Minimum encryption version
sets the lowest accepted TLS version.
The recommended defaults enable Always use https and insecure-image HTTPS rewrites, select Full encryption, set minimum TLS to 1.2 and security to Medium, enable HTTP/3, faster repeat visits, Brotli, Early Hints, and Smart Tiered Cache, and turn off Hotlink protection. Bot Fight Mode is not changed by this action. Check the result for any setting the Cloudflare account does not allow to be updated.
The Settings card with the recommended values shown: Always use https on, security level Medium, and minimum TLS 1.2. Set recommended defaults applies them in one step.
Page caching
Find
Page caching
.
Review the displayed caching behavior.
Set the offered cache lifetime within the supported 30–3600 second range.
Click
Turn on page caching
.
Review the saved status.
Use
Clear cached pages
when cached pages need to be refreshed. Check important public and signed-in workflows after changing caching behavior.
Page caching has its own lifetime and activation controls. This example shows caching turned off.
Advanced settings
Click
Show
beside
Advanced settings
to inspect HTTP/3, faster repeat visits, compression, Early Hints, Smart Tiered Cache, encryption mode, insecure-image handling, Bot Fight Mode, and hotlink protection. Availability and allowed changes can depend on the Cloudflare account and the current site configuration.
Full (strict)
requires a trusted certificate for the website hostname on the origin server. Review
SSL > Certificate on your server
before changing encryption mode. If the panel refuses an unsafe change, resolve the stated prerequisite instead of forcing the setting at another screen.
Show expands the advanced settings. Encryption mode, marked, is the one setting here that can take the website offline if it is wrong; Full is recommended. Unavailable controls depend on the Cloudflare connection.
Disconnect
Disconnect
stops Domain Manager from managing Cloudflare. Existing DNS records remain in place, and existing Cloudflare settings and proxying continue until separately changed. Reconnect the account to resume management from Domain Manager.
The wizard can publish website sender-authentication records without creating incoming mailboxes or their MX records. Review
Mailboxes
separately if the domain will receive email.
A completed setup shows the correct connected domain, the expected website connection, and verified email-authentication records. Test the website and email after applying any settings.

title: Settings » Domain Manager » Mailboxes and Email Routing
content:
The
Mailboxes
tab in
Settings > Domain Manager
identifies where incoming email is delivered and provides the available mailbox controls. It is separate from the outgoing sender-authentication checks in
Emails
.
Before starting
Use a custom domain and confirm which provider should receive its email. The visible actions depend on the domain's DNS connection and whether local mailboxes are supported. Moving mail to another provider requires that provider's account, mailbox setup, and exact records. Back up messages before removing mailboxes or changing a mail-hosting arrangement.
Check the current mail provider
Open
Settings > Domain Manager > Mailboxes
.
Read
Who handles your email
.
Review the provider and routing result before changing any mailbox.
MX records decide where new incoming mail goes. A locally listed mailbox does not prove that the domain currently delivers new mail to it. If the domain uses Google, Microsoft, Cloudflare Email Routing, or another provider, manage the active inboxes at that provider unless a deliberate migration is being performed.
The example uses selfautomated.com with Brilliant Directories-hosted mail throughout. Who handles your email (1) reports where new mail for the domain is delivered.
Add and manage a local mailbox
Find
Mailboxes
.
Click
Add a mailbox
when offered.
Enter the requested mailbox details and password.
Set the storage limit.
Save the mailbox.
Click
Refresh
and confirm it appears.
Each mailbox displays space used and its limit, with
Open webmail
,
Set up
, and
More
buttons.
Open webmail
is described under
Open a mailbox in webmail
.
Set up
shows the connection settings and can email them with
Email these instructions to
.
More
holds
Change the password
,
Change the storage limit
, and
Delete this mailbox
. A limit of
0
means no individual mailbox limit; the website's hosting capacity still applies.
Use
Set up
for the exact connection settings for Outlook, Apple Mail, or a phone. Confirm the recipient before sending setup instructions.
Set up
(1) expands the connection settings (2) for the existing matt@selfautomated.com mailbox. It displays the exact connection settings without exposing the password.
Deleting a mailbox also deletes its stored messages.
Deletion requires confirmation of the full email address and cannot be undone from Domain Manager. Preserve any messages that must be kept first.
Open a mailbox in webmail
Open webmail
opens the mailbox's inbox in a new browser window, already signed in, without the mailbox password. It works the same way as
Check Email
in cPanel.
Find the mailbox under
Mailboxes
.
Click
Open webmail
.
Read and send mail in the new window.
A mailbox row: the Catch-all label (1) marks the mailbox that receives mail sent to addresses that do not exist, and Open webmail (2) opens its inbox signed in.
Signing in without the password is available to administrators whose role can open the website's cPanel. For other administrators,
Open webmail
opens the ordinary webmail sign-in page, which asks for the mailbox password.
If the browser blocks the new window, a message asks to allow pop-ups for the page; allow them and click
Open webmail
again.
If the mail server cannot sign in to the mailbox, the new window shows the webmail sign-in page instead, and a message explains that the mailbox password is needed there.
Each signed-in opening is recorded in the website's notifications as
Webmail opened for
the mailbox. The sign-in itself is never placed in a link or the browser address.
A mailbox marked
Catch-all
receives email sent to addresses at the domain that do not exist; see
Handle unrouted email
. When that mail is kept in the account's own mailbox, that mailbox is listed too, as
The account's own mailbox
with the
Catch-all
label. It has no address at the domain and no usage figures (
Not reported
). For administrators whose role can open cPanel it offers only
Open webmail
, because webmail is the only way to read that mail; for other administrators it has no buttons.
Set the website's sending address
Email from your website
controls the domain-based sending address offered by this panel. Use an address that is monitored and can receive replies, then recheck the outgoing authentication in
Emails
. This card appears when the domain has mailboxes on Brilliant Directories servers; otherwise, set the sending address under
Emails
with
Your "from" address
.
Also check
Emails > Your mailboxes' signature (DKIM)
. Its
Fix it
action provides the signature record for mail sent from hosted mailboxes; this is separate from the website’s sender-authentication setup.
Handle unrouted email
Send all unrouted email for the following domain
controls messages addressed to names without an existing mailbox. Choose one of three options, then click
Save
:
Bounce it back
rejects these messages. This is the safer choice, because a sender who mistypes an address finds out.
Keep in the catch-all mailbox
holds them in the account's own mailbox, which is then listed under
Mailboxes
with
Open webmail
.
Send it to
delivers them to the address entered below it. When that address is one of the domain's own mailboxes, it is marked
Catch-all
in the mailbox list.
When mail is currently kept in the account's own mailbox, the card says so (
Right now it is kept in the catch-all mailbox
, followed by its name). If no option is selected,
Save
asks for a choice instead of saving. Confirm the destination before saving so mail is not collected in an unintended inbox.
Send all unrouted email offers Bounce it back, Keep in the catch-all mailbox, and Send it to (1); the note below explains each choice (2). Here, mail to addresses that do not exist goes to matt@selfautomated.com.
Change the incoming email provider
Prepare the destination provider's account and mailboxes.
Open the
DNS
tab and keep a copy of the domain's current MX, SPF (TXT), and autodiscover records.
Open
Change your email provider
.
Click
Change
.
Select
Our mail servers
,
Google Workspace
,
Microsoft 365
, or
Somewhere else
.
Enter or review the required provider values.
Click
Point my email here
.
Read the confirmation before approving the MX change.
Refresh the provider result.
Open the
DNS
tab and confirm the result: only the new provider's MX records remain, and the SPF and autodiscover records are still present. Remove any MX record left from the previous provider, and restore any missing record from the copy.
Test incoming email at the destination.
Check the DNS records after every provider change.
The automated change can leave an MX record from the previous provider in place or remove the domain's SPF or autodiscover record. A leftover MX record can keep sending some incoming mail to the old provider, and a missing SPF record can send the website's email to spam. Compare the records with the copy taken before the change.
After
Change
is clicked,
Change your email provider
offers four choices (1):
Our mail servers
,
Google Workspace
,
Microsoft 365
, and
Somewhere else
.
Cancel
closes it without changes.
The automated action replaces the existing MX records where the panel has the required DNS access. For externally hosted DNS without that access, update the records at the DNS provider. Use the destination provider's exact hostname rather than a generic example. This changes delivery routing; it does not migrate stored messages or create a paid account at the destination provider.
If the panel identifies a mismatch between local mail delivery and server routing, it may offer
Deliver my mail here
. Use that only when the local server is the intended mail destination.
The reverse case, where the domain's mail goes to another provider but this server still keeps mail for the domain, shows
This server still delivers your mail to itself
with a
Send my mail to
button for that provider. If an old Brilliant Directories MX record outranks the provider's records, the panel removes it where it manages the DNS, or explains how to remove it at the DNS provider.
Completion means new mail reaches the intended provider, outgoing website mail passes authentication, and mailbox applications can connect with the displayed settings.

title: Settings » Domain Manager » Diagnostics
content:
The
Diagnostics
tab in
Settings > Domain Manager
runs additional website checks and shows relevant certificate and update details. It helps identify the next action when a general status message is not enough to explain a problem.
Before starting
The administrator must have permission to view website resources. Review the
Domain
and
SSL
findings first so an address or certificate problem is not confused with a pending software update.
Run the checks
Open
Settings > Domain Manager > Diagnostics
.
Find
Is anything on this website broken?
.
Click
Check everything
.
Wait for the results.
Expand the relevant details for any reported finding.
The checks cover website launch status, purchased items awaiting installation, certificate problems, and pending updates. A result describes the checks available to this tool; it is not a full audit of every custom page or integration.
Review certificate attempts
Certificate attempt history
appears when relevant records are available. Review the latest result and expand the detail when needed. Repeated earlier attempts can help explain what happened, while the current
SSL
result shows the website's present certificate state.
Use an offered repair
Depending on the finding, the page may offer
Fix these for me
or
Run the certificate self-heal
. Read the explanation and confirmation before applying the action. Re-run the checks afterward and verify the public website.
Review pending updates
Find
Updates waiting for your website
.
Click
Check for updates
.
Review the listed updates.
Choose the specific update or
Install all
when that is intended.
Read and confirm the installation prompt.
Recheck after installation completes.
Installation applies changes to the website.
The confirmation identifies changes that cannot be undone from this screen. Review the update list before proceeding.
If a repair fails or the public website remains affected, contact support with the site ID, domain, exact result, and the action already attempted. Avoid repeatedly running a repair without reviewing its latest result.

title: Settings » Domain Manager » Speed Tests
content:
The
Speed
tab in
Settings > Domain Manager
runs Google PageSpeed Insights tests for the website homepage and keeps previous results for comparison.
Before starting
The website must have a successfully detected HTTPS certificate, and the administrator must have permission to view website resources. If the tab is missing, check
SSL
and the administrator's access permissions first.
Run a performance test
Open
Settings > Domain Manager > Speed
.
Find
PageSpeed Insights
.
Click
Run the test
.
Keep the page open while the mobile and desktop tests complete.
Review both sets of results.
A run normally takes around half a minute, but the testing service can take longer. The panel allows one combined mobile-and-desktop run every 24 hours per website. If a recent result is already available, use it and the saved history instead of repeatedly starting another run.
Read the results
Compare the mobile and desktop scores separately. Review the metrics, flagged issues, and suggested improvements below the scores. Scores describe the test conditions at that time; they are not a guarantee of every visitor's experience or a promised search ranking. Alongside performance, the results show Google's
Accessibility
,
Best practices
,
SEO
, and
Agentic browsing
scores.
Use the history to compare measurements after a website change. If a test fails, confirm that the homepage loads over HTTPS and review the error before retrying when permitted.
Example test results. A comparison graph becomes available after a second saved test.
Improve and measure again
Start with the specific large files, loading delays, or other issues identified in the result. Retest after the change when the next test is available. See
bandwidth optimization
for related advice on resource use.
The Speed tab uses Google PageSpeed Insights to test the website’s performance and track results over time. If you need help investigating an issue, the Brilliant Directories support team may use additional diagnostic tools to take a closer look.

title: Account Dashboard » Update Profile
content:
The
Update Profile
page in the Account Dashboard holds the contact details of the signed-in admin account: profile photo, name, job title, company, contact email and phone number, additional email addresses and phone numbers, email signature, and website and social profile links. The Brilliant Directories support and billing teams use these details to know who they are talking to and where to send replies.
The page edits only the account that is signed in. Other admins on a website update their own profiles from their own accounts.
Before Starting
Sign in to the
Account Dashboard
.
The
Sign-in email
cannot be changed from this page. Contact support to change it.
How to Open Update Profile
In the Account Dashboard, click the admin name at the top right.
Select
Update Profile
.
Update Profile
is also listed in the
Account
menu on the left of every account page, together with Notification Settings, Login Settings, Verified Users and Change Password.
Profile Settings
Profile photo
– Click
Upload photo
and choose a JPG, PNG, GIF or WebP image up to 5MB. The image is cropped to a square and saved as soon as it uploads. Once a photo is set,
Change photo
replaces it and
Remove
deletes it.
Full name
– Required. The name of the person who uses this admin account.
Job title
– Optional.
Company
– Optional.
Sign-in email
– The email address used to sign in. It is shown for reference only (
Contact support to change
).
Email address
– The address where Brilliant Directories should reach the admin. The star button next to an email address marks it as the
primary email address for billing & support replies
. The line under the field shows which address is currently the primary one.
Phone number
– The main contact phone number, marked with a star as the primary phone.
Additional emails & phone numbers
– Click to expand. The list loads from the account's support records. Click
Add another address
or
Add another number
to add one, click the star next to an entry to make it the primary one, or remove an entry with its remove button.
Email signature
– Click to expand. The signature is appended to emails sent from the account. Use the editor toolbar for formatting; text colour, size and alignment are not kept.
Website & social profiles
– Click to expand. Enter full addresses starting with
http://
or
https://
.
Save Changes
– Saves every field except the photo, which saves on upload.
After Saving
The message
Your profile has been saved.
appears once the changes are stored.
When a different address is chosen as the primary email, the line under
Email address
adds
pending review
. The Brilliant Directories team reviews profile changes before applying them to the account's support records, so the new primary email, additional emails and photo reach support records after that review.
Related Articles
Account Dashboard » Login Settings
Account Dashboard » Verified Users
Account Dashboard » Change Password
