title: Account Dashboard » Login Settings
content:
The
Login Settings
page in the Account Dashboard controls how the signed-in admin account signs in: two-factor authentication, the available sign-in methods, and the ManageMyDirectory.com mobile app for notifications on a phone.
Before Starting
Sign in to the
Account Dashboard
.
Turning on two-factor authentication requires access to the inbox of the account's sign-in email, since the one-time codes are sent there.
How to Open Login Settings
In the Account Dashboard, click the admin name at the top right.
Select
Login Settings
.
Login Settings
is also listed in the
Account
menu on the left of every account page.
Login Settings Sections
Two-Factor Authentication
– Shows whether two-factor sign-in is
On
or
Off
. With two-factor on, a one-time code is emailed to the sign-in email whenever the account signs in from a new device, so a password alone is not enough to sign in.
Sign-in Methods
– Lists the ways this account can sign in.
Email and password
shows the sign-in email and an
Active
badge.
Google
and
Apple
are marked
Coming soon
and are not available yet.
Get Notifications on Your App
– The
App Store
and
Google Play
buttons open the ManageMyDirectory.com mobile app. After the app is installed and signed in once, the devices that are signed in and receiving notifications are listed here with the time each was last seen.
Notification Settings
opens the page that controls which notifications are sent.
Turn On Two-Factor Authentication
In the
Two-Factor Authentication
section, click
Turn on two-factor
. A one-time code is emailed to the account's sign-in email right away.
Under
Enter your code
, type the code from the email.
Click
Verify & turn on
.
If the email does not arrive, click
Resend code
. The code expires shortly, so use the most recent one.
When the code is accepted, the confirmation
Two-factor is on
appears and the section shows the
On
badge. From then on, signing in from a new device asks for a one-time code sent by email. For more about how two-factor sign-in works, see
Enhancing Security with Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)
.
Related Articles
Account Dashboard » Update Profile
Account Dashboard » Change Password
Account Dashboard » Notification Settings

title: Account Dashboard » Verified Users
content:
The
Verified Users
page in the Account Dashboard lists the people the Brilliant Directories support and billing teams may contact about the account's websites, and what each person can discuss. A website owner can give a colleague, partner or assistant access here directly, instead of asking support to add them.
Each verified user gets one of three access levels:
Billing & Support
– Can be contacted about both billing and support matters.
Billing Only
– Can be contacted about billing matters only.
Support Only
– Can be contacted about support matters only.
Before Starting
Sign in to the
Account Dashboard
with the account that owns the websites. The page is for website owners: an account that does not own any active, suspended or pending website sees a message explaining there is nothing to set.
Verified users are stored in the account's support records. If the page shows
We could not reach your support record just now
, saving may not work until the record is available again; try later or contact support.
Verified users are contacts for support and billing. Adding someone here does not give them a login to the website admin. To add an admin login, see
Settings » Admin Accounts
.
How to Open Verified Users
In the Account Dashboard, click the admin name at the top right.
Select
Update Profile
(or any other account page).
In the
Account
menu on the left, click
Verified Users
.
Add a Verified User
Email address
– Enter the person's email address. It can be an email already on the account or a new one for someone else.
Access level
– Choose
Billing & Support
,
Billing Only
or
Support Only
.
Websites
– Click to choose which websites this person is a contact for. Search by name, URL or ID, tick the websites, then click
Done
.
Select all shown
and
Clear
tick or untick the whole list.
Remove
– The trash button removes the person from the list.
All my websites
– Makes the person a contact for every website on the account, including any website added later.
Add another email
– Adds a row for another person.
Save changes
– Saves the list. Adding, changing or removing a person takes effect only after saving.
Every person needs at least one website, or
All my websites
. A person with no websites is not saved, and a message names them.
After Saving
The message
Verified users were saved.
confirms the change. The support and billing teams then use this list to confirm who may be contacted about each website, and at which access level.
Contacts that the Brilliant Directories team entered earlier appear under
On file with our support team
. They cannot be changed on this page, but they show the full list of people on file. Contact support to change one of them.
Related Articles
Account Dashboard » Update Profile
Account Dashboard » Login Settings

title: Account Dashboard » Change Password
content:
The
Change Password
page in the Account Dashboard sets a new password for the signed-in admin account. Changing the password here also signs the account out of every session, on every browser and device, so anyone still signed in with the old password loses access.
Before Starting
Sign in to the
Account Dashboard
.
The current password is required. If it is not known, use the
forgot password
link on the admin sign-in page instead.
Have the new password ready before continuing: the current browser is signed out as soon as the password changes.
How to Open Change Password
In the Account Dashboard, click the admin name at the top right.
Select
Login Settings
(or any other account page).
In the
Account
menu on the left, click
Change Password
.
Change the Password
Enter the
Current password
.
Enter the
New password
.
Check the requirements under the field. Each one is marked as it is met:
At least 10 characters
A letter and a number, or 16+ characters
Different from your current password
Both new password fields match
Enter the same password again in
Confirm new password
.
Click
Change password
. The button becomes available once every requirement is met.
The new password is also refused if it is one of the most commonly guessed passwords, matches the admin's name or email address, was used before on this account, is longer than 72 characters, or starts or ends with a space. The page shows a message explaining which rule was not met.
After the Password Changes
The message
Your password has been changed. Signing you out so you can sign in with it.
appears, and the sign-in page opens with
Please sign in with your new password.
Every session for the account is signed out, including the current one. Other browsers and devices must sign in again with the new password.
Any
reset your password
links sent to the account earlier stop working.
A confirmation email is sent to the account's sign-in email, so an unexpected change is noticed straight away.
Too many incorrect attempts.
After several incorrect current passwords, the page stops accepting attempts for 15 minutes. Wait, then try again, or use the forgot password link on the sign-in page.

Account Dashboard » Login Settings
Admin Sessions

title: How to Capture a HAR File and Console Screenshot for Support
content:
Some problems only happen on one computer or in one browser: a button that does nothing when clicked, a save that seems to work but does not keep the changes, a form that will not submit, or a page that keeps loading. When the support team cannot make the problem happen on its own computers, a recording from the browser where it does happen shows exactly what went wrong.
This article explains how to make that recording and send it to support. It takes about five minutes and does not change anything on the website.
What Support Needs
The browser name and version
, EG Chrome 154 on Windows 11. See
How to Find the Browser Version
at the end of this article.
A HAR file.
This is a log of everything the browser sent and received while the problem happened. The file name ends in
.har
.
A screenshot of the Console tab
, taken right after the problem happens. Error messages from the page show up here in red.
A list of active browser extensions or assistant tools
, EG Grammarly, ad blockers, password managers, translation tools, or AI assistants and sidebars. These tools can change how a page behaves.
The page address and the steps that cause the problem
, EG "Settings > General Settings, change the Website Name, click Save Changes".
Keep the HAR file private.
A HAR file can contain anything typed into forms on the page, and in some browsers the admin login session. Attach it only to the support ticket, never to a public post or a group email. Sign out of the Admin Area after sending it, which ends the login session recorded in the file.
Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge
Chrome and Edge use the same developer tools, so the steps are the same. Button names can differ slightly between versions.
Open the page where the problem happens.
Press
F12
(on a Mac,
Option + Command + I
), or right-click anywhere on the page and choose
Inspect
. The developer tools open on one side of the window.
Click the
Network
tab. If it is not visible, click the
»
arrows next to the tab names to find it.
Tick
Keep log
so the list is not cleared when the page reloads or moves to another page. Older versions of Chrome call this option
Preserve log
.
Repeat the steps that cause the problem, EG click the button or submit the form. New lines appear in the list while the browser works. Wait until the problem has happened.
Click the
Export HAR
button (the downward arrow in the Network toolbar), choose where to save the file, and click
Save
.
Click the
Console
tab and take a screenshot of it, including any lines shown in red. On Windows, press
Windows + Shift + S
. On a Mac, press
Command + Shift + 4
.
Sanitized HAR files:
Chrome saves a sanitized HAR file by default. It leaves out the browser's login cookies but keeps everything support needs to investigate. If a menu appears with two choices, choose
Export HAR (sanitized)
. In older versions of Chrome, the same file can also be saved by right-clicking the list of requests and choosing
Save all as HAR with content
.
Mozilla Firefox
Open the page where the problem happens.
Press
F12
(on a Mac,
Option + Command + I
), or right-click anywhere on the page and choose
Inspect
.
Click the
Network
tab.
Click the gear icon at the right end of the Network toolbar and select
Persist Logs
, so a check mark appears next to it.
Repeat the steps that cause the problem and wait until it has happened.
Click the gear icon again and choose
Save All As HAR
, then save the file. The same option appears when right-clicking the list of requests.
Click the
Console
tab and take a screenshot of it.
Firefox has no sanitized option, so its HAR files include the login cookies. Signing out of the Admin Area after sending the file ends that session.
Safari (Mac)
Safari hides its developer tools until they are turned on. This only needs to be done once.
Choose
Safari > Settings
, click
Advanced
, and tick
Show features for web developers
. A
Develop
menu appears in the menu bar.
Open the page where the problem happens, then choose
Develop > Show Web Inspector
(or press
Option + Command + I
).
Click the
Network
tab. Click the round filter icon next to
All
and choose
Preserve Requests
, so the list is not cleared when the page reloads.
Repeat the steps that cause the problem and wait until it has happened.
Click
Export
at the right end of the Network toolbar and save the file.
Click the
Console
tab and take a screenshot of it.
How to Send the Files
Attach the
.har
file and the Console screenshot to the support ticket, either by replying to the ticket email or through the support portal. If the HAR file is too large to attach, compress it into a
.zip
file first.
In the same reply, include the browser name and version, the list of active extensions or assistant tools, the page address, and the steps that cause the problem.
Sign out of the Admin Area, then sign back in.
How to Find the Browser Version
Chrome:
open the three-dot menu and choose
Help > About Google Chrome
.
Edge:
open the three-dot menu and choose
Help and feedback > About Microsoft Edge
.
Firefox:
open the menu (three lines) and choose
Help > About Firefox
.
Safari:
choose
Safari > About Safari
.

title: 10/02/2026 - Software Updates
content:
We made updates to several default widgets this week. If you customized any of these widgets and want to update them, you can find the latest code in the corresponding default widget. Please remember that if you have a custom version of any of these widgets, the latest updates will not be pushed to your website.
Released a new
Account
area in the
Admin
where each
Admin
can manage their own login. Profile details such as name, phone, company, timezone, photo, email signature and social links can now be edited there, the password can be changed from the same place, and notifications can now be set per delivery channel - website, desktop and mobile - either for all websites at once or website by website. In addition, a website owner can now grant another email address Billing and Support access to their websites from the same area. Along with this, the handling of Admin login sessions was hardened.
Improved the
Google Maps alert
in the Admin so it now reports the exact problem Google returned, such as billing not being enabled, a restricted referrer or an API that was never turned on, instead of one generic message for every case. Both the website key and the server-side key used for member geocoding are now checked, and the key is also tested on the website's own domain so the result reflects what visitors actually see. In addition, the website key, the server key and the New Google Maps Places API switch can now be edited and validated from inside the alert, and a key Google rejects is not saved.
Improved the
domain connection wizard in the
Domain Manager
in the Admin so connecting a root domain now shows the recommended instructions for that domain's DNS provider: domain forwarding for GoDaddy and an ALIAS record for Namecheap, with the A record kept only as the fallback for other providers.
Improved the
SSL tab of the

title: How To Display Custom Post Fields In the Post Details Page
content:
This article explains how to display custom post field values on the post details page.
Custom post fields can be added to a post form and displayed on the front-end post details page using the
Post Meta Details
widget.
Overview
When a custom field is added to a post form, the field can collect additional information from members when they create or edit a post.
The widget used for displaying post field details is:
Bootstrap Theme - Module - Post Meta Details v2.0
To display that custom field value on the post details page, the field must be set to display on the view page, and the correct widget must be added to the post details layout.
Step 1: Customize the Post Form
Start by editing the form used by the post type.
Go to
Toolbox >> Form Manager
.
Find the form connected to the post type.
Click
Customize
if the form has not been customized yet.
Click
Edit
if the form has already been customized.
The form editor will open so custom fields can be added or updated.
How To Customize a Form
Step 2: Add the Custom Post Field
Add the custom field that should display on the post details page.
Examples of custom post fields include:
Event location
Price
Service area
Start date
Requirements
Contact instructions
Download link
After adding the field, review the field label, database variable, field type, and required field settings.
Step 3: Enable Display View for the Field
For the custom field value to display on the post details page,
Display View
must be enabled for the field.
Open the custom field settings.
Find the
Display Settings
for the field.
Enable
Display View
.
Save the form changes.
Important:
If
Display View
is not enabled, the field value may be saved with the post but will not display on the post details page.
Step 4: Add the Post Meta Details Widget to the Sidebar
The custom post field values can be displayed in the sidebar of the post details page by adding the Post Meta Details widget to the post sidebar.
Go to
Toolbox >> Sidebar Manager
.
Find the
Post Single Page
sidebar.
Click
Customize
if the sidebar has not been customized yet.
Click
Edit
if the sidebar has already been customized.
Find the widget named
Bootstrap Theme - Module - Post Meta Details v2.0
.
Drag and drop the widget into the sidebar layout.
Click
Save Changes
.
Toolbox » Sidebar Manager
The custom post field values will display in the sidebar when viewing the post details page.
Alternative: Add the Widget to the Post Details Content
The Post Meta Details widget can also be added directly inside the post details page layout using the widget shortcode.
Content » Edit Post Settings
Use the following shortcode:
[widget=Bootstrap Theme - Module - Post Meta Details v2.0]
When this shortcode is added to the post details layout, the custom field values can display below the main body of the post instead of in the sidebar.
Where the Custom Field Values Display
Custom post field values can display in different areas depending on where the widget is added.
Location
Setup
Result
Post sidebar
Add the widget to the
Post Single Page
sidebar.
Custom post fields display in the sidebar of the post details page.
Post details content area
Add the widget shortcode to the post details layout.
Custom post fields display below the main post content.
Important Notes
The custom field must be added to the correct post form.
Display View
must be enabled for the field.
The post must have a saved value for the custom field before it can display on the post details page.
The
Bootstrap Theme - Module - Post Meta Details v2.0
widget must be added to the sidebar or post details layout.
If the field is blank for a post, there may be no value to display.
Custom fields may display differently depending on the field type and the post details page layout.
Common Reasons the Field Does Not Display
Display View is not enabled:
Open the field settings and enable
Display View
.
The wrong form was edited:
Confirm the custom field was added to the form used by the correct post type.
The widget was not added:
Add
Bootstrap Theme - Module - Post Meta Details v2.0
to the sidebar or post details layout.
The post field is empty:
Edit the post and add a value to the custom field.
The sidebar is not assigned:
Confirm the correct sidebar is being used by the post details page.

title: Common Breadcrumb Variables to be used on the Website
content:
A breadcrumb is a navigational aid used on websites to show the user's location. On Brilliant Directories, these are automatically generated on different sections of the software and can be edited if desired.
These are the most common variables and areas where breadcrumbs can be edited:
1. Static Web Pages
Navigate to My Content >> Web Page Builder >> Search for the desired web page to add/edit the breadcrumbs and click on Edit:
Once on the page, move to the Page Options tab and add/edit the breadcrumbs:
The accepted format for custom breadcrumbs under Web Page Builder is:
Blog | /blog > Partner | https://example.com > My Page
Format rules:
>
— Separates each breadcrumb level.
|
— Assigns a URL to the breadcrumb immediately before it. Both relative URLs (such as
/blog
) and absolute URLs (such as
https://example.com
) are supported.
How it works:
The text before the
|
is the breadcrumb label that will be displayed.
The URL after the
|
is the destination for that breadcrumb.
Each
>
creates the next level in the breadcrumb trail.
The final breadcrumb can be plain text without a URL if it represents the current page.
Example:
Blog | /blog > Partner | https://example.com > My Page
This will generate the following breadcrumb trail:
Home > Blog > Partner > My Page
Where:
Blog
links to
/blog
Partner
links to
https://example.com
My Page
is the current page and is not linked.
Note:
Do not include
Home
in your custom breadcrumb string, as it is added automatically by the system.
Do not forget to save the changes.
Here is a list of some of the common variables that can be used to edit the web page breadcrumbs for static pages on the site:
1. %website_name%
2. %%Profession%
3. %website_url%
4. %industry%
Example:
Category Page
2. Member SEO Templates
To edit the breadcrumbs of member SEO templates, navigate to My Content >> SEO Templates >> Choose a SEO template and click on Edit:
Move to the Page Options tab and edit them accordingly:
These are dynamic pages. Once the details have been edited in one SEO template, the changes will be reflected on multiple search results pages as well. A good example would be editing the SEO of a top-level category; this would affect the search result pages of all top-level categories as well.
- Profile Page SEO templates from ID #100 to ID #103:
These are the pages that show member profiles.
- Member search results #200's IDs:
Pages that will show based on a search by either category or location.
Here is a list of some of the common variables that can be used to edit the member SEO breadcrumbs of the dynamic pages of the site:
1. %country_name% – The name of the country that relates to this page
2. %city% OR %city_name% – The name of the city that relates to this page
3. %profession% – The name of the top-level category that relates to this page
4. %full_name% – The full name of the member that relates to this page
5. %service_name% – The name of the sub-level category that relates to this page
6. %company% – The name of the member's company that relates to this page
7. %location% – The city and state associated with the listing
8. %industry% – The industry variable entered on the Settings >> General Settings >> Industry tab
Examples:
SEO Template ID #100:
SEO Template #216:
3. Post Types SEO Templates
Navigate to My Content >> SEO Templates >> Choose one of the post SEO templates and click on Edit:
The changes will be reflected on either post search results pages or post detail pages.
- Post Search Results SEO Templates #300 and #301:
Pages that will show based on a search by post type.
For the post search results SEO breadcrumbs, it is recommended to only use the %%Data_name%% variable:

title: Setting Up A New Stripe Account
content:
The first step to set up Stripe as a payment gateway is to create an account in Stripe.
If the Stripe account has been created and the credentials need to be added to the admin, then follow the steps on this article:
Get Stripe Credentials - Existing Account
The keys need to be added to the admin:
Important Note #1:
The name that appears on a member's credit card statement can be edited on Statement Descriptor section above. Must be between 5 - 22 characters, have at least one letter, and cannot contain the following characters: < > \ ' " *
Important Note #2:
When adding credentials for Stripe gateway, there will be additional validation on each key field as the valid credentials should be between 25 and 255 characters and the key cannot include dots (ex: ....).
Stripe Credentials - How To Roll Key
Creating A New Stripe Account
These are the necessary steps in order to start this process:
The first step is to register a new account here:
https://dashboard.stripe.com/register
To learn how to create or connect an account, follow the steps outlined in this article:
Getting started with Stripe: create or connect an account
There are two types of API keys: Publishable and Secret.
Publishable API keys
are meant solely to identify the account with Stripe, they aren’t secret.
Secret API keys
should be kept confidential. The account’s secret API key can perform any API request to Stripe without restriction.
When the Stripe account has been set up, go to Settings >> Developers >> Manage API Keys:
In order to copy a key, hover over it and click on "Click to copy".
After the account is created, it's now time to add it to the admin.
To learn more about how to complete this process, use the following article for reference:
Finance » Payment Settings - Setting Up A Payment Gateway
Stripe Test and Live Modes
In
test mode
, payments are not processed by card networks or payment providers, and only Stripe test payment information can be used.
Genuine card information
cannot
be used in
test mode
. Instead, use any of the following test card numbers, a valid expiration date in the future, and any random CVC number, to create a successful payment.
Stripe test cards can be found here:
https://stripe.com/docs/testing
Each basic test card’s billing country is set to the U.S. If need to create test card payments using cards for other billing countries, use the
international test cards
.
In
Live mode
, payments are processed by card networks and members can use real cards.
Important Note
: If the user would like to allow Stripe to accept international payments from
India
, make sure to enable the following Advanced Setting (India Stripe Account Accept International Payments):
We recommend the following article for reference as it has plenty of useful information related to how off-site and off-site payment gateways work (Stripe: off-site / PayPal: on-site):
Stripe or PayPal Standard?
To find more information about other payment gateways compatible with Brilliant Directories, read this article:
Supported Payment Gateways
.

title: Design Settings » Homepage » Hero Background Image
content:
Hero Background Image
These settings control the main image on the first fold in the homepage of the website. We recommend using images with the following dimensions:
1800px wide by 600px high. The file size is also important; we recommend using images that are
not more than 200 KB
.
To edit the Hero Back, navigate to:
Settings
Design Settings
Homepage Tab
Visual Guide of the Hero Background Image
1. Display Background Image
Use this section to add the main image that will display above the fold on the homepage, to use the Homepage Slideshow, read the following article:
Homepage Background Slideshow Settings
Our recommended size for the image is 1800 px by 600 px.
Yes - Display Background Image
No - Hide Background Image
2. Display Hero Section on Mobile
This setting controls if the image will be viewable on mobile devices or not.
Yes - Display on Mobile View
No - Hide on Mobile View
3. Background Image Behavior
This setting controls if the background hero image will be Mobile Ready or Standard View. We strongly recommend using the Mobile-Ready View
Mobile Ready View
4. Replace / Upload Image
This setting is used to upload a new image for the hero image on the homepage's first fold.
Replace / Upload Image
Mobile Image
The image uploaded here will replace the main hero homepage image, when the website is accessed using mobile devices.
5. Top Spacing
This setting will add extra padding to the top of the main image, this will help better align the graphic elements inside the hero image. The available options go from 0px to 400px
6. Bottom Spacing
This setting will add extra padding to the bottom of the main image, this will help better align the graphic elements inside the hero image. The available options go from 0px to 400px
7. Background Movement
This setting allows the image to remain stationary while the page scrolls, or keeps it fixed in place.
Scroll (Default)
Fixed
NOTE:
Apple iOS devices automatically use Scroll, as Fixed is not supported.
8. Background Position
This setting will add extra padding to the bottom of the main image, this will help better align the graphic elements inside the hero image. The available options go from 0px to 400px
Top (Default)
Center
Bottom
9-10. Image Overlay Color + Image Overlay Visibility
These settings select how transparent or opaque the Overlay is applied to the Hero Image. This becomes very helpful when using white fonts, allowing the text to be legible on an image that has lots of colors. For dark fonts with opaque images, this setting can be used to se the background white.
Overlay 6
0 (invisible)

title: Developer Hub Overview
content:
The
Developer Hub
gathers the website's advanced tools in one place: API keys and webhooks for connecting other applications, 301 redirects, image size settings, search autosuggest, the robots.txt and .htaccess files, and direct access to the website's database and cPanel.
Opening the Developer Hub
Click
Developer Hub
in the left menu of the Admin area. The page shows one card per tool. Click anywhere on a card, or its button, to open the tool.
The Tools
Manage API Keys
: creates the API keys that let outside applications connect to the website, and sets what each key can access. See
Developer Hub » Generate and Manage API Keys
.
Manage Webhooks
: turns on webhook events and sets the links that website events (form submissions, sign ups, payments and more) are sent to. See
Developer Hub - Webhooks
.
301 Redirect Rules
(
Manage Redirects
): sends visitors and search engines from pages that moved to their new address. See
301 Redirects
.
Image Settings
(
Edit Image Sizes
): sets the maximum dimensions for images members upload. See
Developer Hub » Image Settings
.
Autosuggest Settings
(
Manage Autosuggest
): manages the keyword suggestions shown as visitors type in the search bar. See
How To Edit Keyword Search Autosuggest Settings For Member Searches
.
Robots.txt File
(
Edit Robots.txt
): customizes or resets the website's robots.txt file. See
Developer Hub » Robots File
.
HTACCESS File
(
Edit HTACCESS
): customizes or resets the website's .htaccess file. See
Developer Hub » HTACCESS File
.
MySQL Database
(
Open Database
): opens the website's database in a new browser tab. See the
MySQL Database
articles.
cPanel Dashboard
(
Open cPanel
): opens the website's cPanel in a new browser tab. See the
cPanel Dashboard
articles.
Where is the FTP File Manager?
The Developer Hub no longer has a separate FTP File Manager card. Files on the website's server are reached through the
cPanel Dashboard
card.
Cards appear according to the admin's role permissions. An admin whose role does not include a tool does not see its card, and when a role includes none of the tools, the page shows
No Developer Tools
. The Autosuggest Settings card also needs the keyword autosuggest add-on to be active.

title: 10/09/2026 - Software Updates
content:
We made updates to several default widgets this week. If you customized any of these widgets and want to update them, you can find the latest code in the corresponding default widget. Please remember that if you have a custom version of any of these widgets, the latest updates will not be pushed to your website.
Admin Design
Released more of the refreshed
Admin design. Manage API Keys, Webhooks, Image Settings, Autosuggest Settings, Text Labels and Advanced Settings
have been rebuilt in the new look, and
Developer Hub
now opens on a menu of tool cards. In addition, the .htaccess and robots.txt editors were rebuilt with an in-place Restore Default and keyboard saving, and Undo and Redo were added to every code editor. Along with this, date range pickers were added across the new pages, and the Text Labels list now responds to each keystroke in about a tenth of a second.
Domain Manager
Improved the Open Webmail link so a mailbox now opens straight into webmail without asking for the password again, and returns to the Email Accounts section afterwards.
Fixed an issue that prevented subdomain records from being added in the
DNS
editor, where every attempt reported that the name was not valid for the domain.
Fixed an issue that caused the automatic sender setup to publish an SPF record above the ten-lookup limit, and an issue that could leave a domain with two SPF records or overwrite an existing verification record.
Fixed an issue that caused changing a website's domain to only add or remove the www prefix to remove the domain's DNS records from the nameservers.
Websites & Hosting
Fixed an issue that caused domains ending in .co.uk, .com.au and similar two-part endings to be reported as Not Verified on the Enhanced Server move screen while their nameservers were pointed correctly.
Fixed an issue that caused a website launched or reset from the starter template to be given the template's connection address instead of its own.
Fixed an issue that caused the automatic bad-bot block to refuse requests from image CDNs, Bing's crawler and PageSpeed Insights.
Fixed an issue that caused the
In-App Purchase
window in the
Admin
to stay blank when the browser or the network blocked the embedded checkout. The window now offers to continue to the checkout page in its own tab.
Developer Hub & API
Added an option to the Get User request in the
API
that returns the Form Builder labels for Dropdown, Checkbox and Radio fields alongside the stored values. Without the option, the response is unchanged.
Added Post Details as a page type for
SEO
templates, so an
SEO
template for post pages can now be created through the
API
and selected in the
Admin
.
Fixed an issue that caused a
digital produ
ct whose price was updated through the API to keep charging the previous price.
Fixed an issue that prevented redirect rules from working when the Source URL contained a space, an ampersand, an apostrophe or an accented character.
Admin Access & Security
Improved how text typed into the
Admin
is stored and printed back, so values containing quotation marks or angle brackets are now kept exactly as entered on the
Admin role editor, View Contacts, the internal notes of a billing subscription and Payment Settings
. In addition, the
Default Title Text
for
Comments
Section
field no longer accepts PHP code.
Improved the
Invite Admin
form so the same invitation can no longer be submitted repeatedly in quick succession.
Improved the
Admin
so pages that were replaced by newer modules years ago are no longer reachable at their old addresses, and the side menu entries pointing to them were removed.
Form Manager
Fixed an issue that prevented a default form from being customized on websites that do not use HTTPS, where saving returned an empty error message.
Fixed an issue that caused options added to a Checkbox or Dropdown List field to be lost on save while a success message was shown.
Web Pages
Fixed an issue that caused landing pages built with
BD Butler
to lose their styling on the live page while looking correct in the Web Page Builder editor. Widget Involved: Bootstrap Theme Framework
Fixed an issue that prevented changes to the
Coming Soon
page from being saved, and an issue that reported Changes Saved when the server had refused the save.
Posts, Comments & Events
Released
Likes and Dislikes
on
post comments.
Each post type can now enable Likes only or Likes and Dislikes in Comment Settings, each comment shows its vote counts, members cannot vote on their own comments, and comments can be sorted by Most Likes, including by default. In addition, comment dates are now shown correctly on websites whose date format does not use slashes.
Widget Involved:
Bootstrap Theme - Function - Comment Handling
Fixed an issue that caused the
Social Media Shared
Image saved on an
SEO
template to replace each post's own share image.
Widget Involved:
Bootstrap Theme - HEAD
Fixed an issue that caused the events section on the home page to show the first date of a repeating event that has no End Date instead of its next date.
Widget Involved:
Bootstrap Theme - Display - Recent Events
Members & Accounts
Improved listing previews so an
Admin
can now open and review an inactive listing, marked with an
Admin
preview banner, without activating it first.
Widget Involved:
Bootstrap Theme - Member Profile
Fixed an issue that caused a profile
photo
or
logo
deleted from a member's account on the website to remain on the server and still be reachable at its direct address.
Fixed an issue that caused
member login
to fail with a server error when the browser carried a large number of cookies, and that left the Log In Now button disabled afterwards.
Widget Involved:
Bootstrap Theme - Function - Form
Fixed an issue that caused the
Profile Analytics Add-On
to discard clicks on a tracked link whose destination is not one of the member's own profile fields.
Member Search
Fixed an issue that prevented a member search from returning a member when the typed name skipped a middle name. The same change applies to the member search page, the sidebar search form, autosuggest and the reviews search.
Widgets Involved:
Get Matched Search Engine
Search - Member - Search Query
Search - Reviews - Search Query
Sign Up & Leads
Improved the link a visitor is returned to after signing up and the origin link recorded with a lead, so only addresses on the website itself are followed.
Widget Involved:
Bootstrap Theme - Success Page - Free Member Sign Up
Improved the handling of values saved from website forms and from lead submissions that include a photo, so text containing apostrophes or other special characters is stored correctly.
Fixed an issue that caused lead forms placed outside a member profile, such as Get Matched, to fail without a message on websites with many members.
Widget Involved:
Bootstrap Theme - Function - Save Form
Membership Plans
Improved the plan settings so a plan can no longer be saved with a
Sign Up Form
that does not match its
Account Type
, and the Sign Up Form field now sits next to Account Type.
Fixed an issue that caused a plan switched to Free to keep the prices that had been typed in, and an issue that caused a price pasted or filled in by the browser to be saved with its previous value.
Checkout & Billing
Removed the notice stating that invoices are generated 14 days in advance from the Transactions page.
Fixed an issue that caused a coupon to charge the member's card on the coupon's last available use.
Fixed an issue that prevented conversion tracking scripts pasted into the
Conversion Tracking Codes
settings from running when the checkout success message is shown in a popup.
Imports
Fixed an issue that caused a
Business Data
import to attach members to the top-level category only when the selected sub-category has sub-sub-categories of its own.
Fixed an issue that caused the Directory Property dropdowns on the Import Members Data Map to open behind the pop-up.
Newsletters & Email
Improved newsletter statistics. A Clicks by Link table now shows how many recipients clicked each individual link, the per-recipient timeline names the link that was clicked, and soft and hard bounces are now listed as their own events with the reason reported by the mail server. In addition, the same detail is now shown in the Email Outbox.
Website Settings
Improved the
Google Maps
server key check so the key is now tested from the website's own server, which is where member geocoding runs, instead of from the admin server. A key Google refuses for the website is now reported as refused. In addition, the way the test result is received by the Admin was hardened.
Fixed an issue that caused third-party widgets that run background workers, such as the spam check in an Elfsight form, to be blocked on websites using the CSP Headers option.
Widget Involved:
Bootstrap Theme - Function - CSP Headers

title: Changelog - September 2026
content:
New Features
Released a separate set of free trial settings for member upgrades on
Membership Plans:
"
Enable Free Trial Period (Plan Changes)", "Number of Free Trial Days (Plan Changes)" and "Free Trial Additional Options (Plan Changes)"
. Free trials can now be configured separately for new member sign-ups and for existing member plan changes. These settings are available when the Free Trials Add-On is active.
Updated the
Account Dashboard
so websites on the newer pricing plans can now install purchased add-on credits.
Released a rebuilt
Domain Manager
in the
Admin
. It now connects to Cloudflare through a one-click sign-in, sets up email deliverability records automatically, and reports real certificate and domain registration details.
Added a Web Page Setting called
"Sidebar Position on Mobile Devices"
in the Admin, so the sidebar placement on mobile can now be chosen page by page.
Added a bulk delete option for
member transactions
in the
Admin
. Selection checkboxes are now available on the Cancelled invoices tab as well.
Released a new
Account
area in the
Admin
where each
Admin
can manage their own login. Profile details such as name, phone, company, timezone, photo, email signature and social links can now be edited there, the password can be changed from the same place, and notifications can now be set per delivery channel - website, desktop and mobile - either for all websites at once or website by website. In addition, a website owner can now grant another email address Billing and Support access to their websites from the same area. Along with this, the handling of Admin login sessions was hardened.
Enhancements / Fixes:
Updated the
Text Labels
page in the
Admin
to display a "
Last Update
" date on each label. In addition, a new sort filter was added with options to order labels by name or by last edited date.
Improved the
Google Sign-in
workflow on checkout pages: when the GDPR consent checkbox has not been selected, the page now scrolls to the checkbox and highlights it instead of displaying a blocking error message.
Updated the
Admin
so it always loads over a secure connection, even on websites that do not have an
SSL
certificate installed.
Fixed an issue that caused the
API
to reject requests for a single record, even though the same key could successfully list those same records.
Applied a security update to the
Email Templates
page in the
Admin
.
Fixed an issue that caused a member image re-imported through the
API
to keep displaying the previous image, because the new file was saved with the same filename as the one it replaced.
Fixed an issue that caused visitors to be redirected to a different member's profile when a member was assigned a profile page URL that had previously belonged to another member.
Fixed an issue that prevented any setting from being saved on the
Advanced Settings
page in the
Admin
when the
include_service_area_on_pretty_url
Advanced Settings was active with an invalid key entered in the
google_maps_server_side_api_key
setting
. Now it only prevents the advanced settings from being saved when one of these settings is updated.
Fixed an issue that caused search results in
grid view
to display misaligned when a custom web page was used for the search results and its sidebar setting did not match the one selected in
Design Settings
.
Fixed an issue that prevented the
Stock Photos
window from displaying properly when selecting an image on a post form that contains more than one WYSIWYG field.
Fixed an issue that caused script tags to be removed from the
Header
and
Footer
sections when a page was saved from the code view of the
page edito
r
in the
Admin
.
Fixed an issue that prevented sub-account images from loading on profile pages on sites that serve their images through a content delivery network.
Fixed an issue that caused the message "The security check was not completed successfully" to be displayed after a member account had already been created, when the sign-up form was submitted twice and the second submission reused the same security check.
Fixed an issue that caused visitors to see a "Blocked this type of request" message instead of the
login
form, after an automated request to the login page had been stored in the server cache.
Fixed an issue that caused the Site
Activity Tracker
in the
Admin
to list lead submissions that had been rejected by the security check and were never created as leads.
Fixed an issue that caused disabled custom main menus to be listed in the Logged In Member
Main Menu
setting of a membership plan.
Fixed an issue that caused pages to load more Google reCaptcha fields than the number of forms that actually display on the page, including copies placed inside pop-up windows that visitors never opened.
Fixed an issue that caused the "
Click To Load More Results
" button in the Specialties section of a member profile to remain on "Loading" without ever displaying the remaining entries.
Fixed an issue that caused the
menu
cache to store menus that contain widget, form or member shortcodes, such as
[widget=, [form=, [me= and [member=
, so every signed-in member was shown the information of whichever member loaded the menu first.
Fixed an issue that caused the
Send Newsletter
statistics table in the
Admin
to time out and never load on websites with a large sending history, which made a campaign appear stuck even while it was sending normally.
Improved the
Activity Tracker
in the
Admin
so it now records which admin added, edited or removed a form field, and which admin changed an admin account password.
Improved front-end page loading speed by removing a duplicate download of a JavaScript file that every page was requesting twice.
Fixed an issue that prevented company member listings from being found when searching for their full name, in cases where the name was stored across the First Name and Last Name fields.
Fixed an issue that caused the website search to ignore the content of posts when the
Post Keyword Search Options
setting had never been saved for a post type, even though the post type settings screen displayed "Search Default Fields + Custom Fields" as the selected option. This applies to websites with the Search Members Keywords Add-On active.
Fixed an issue that prevented non-image files from displaying an icon in the grid view of the
Media Manager
in the Admin.
Fixed an issue that caused the Home link in the breadcrumb navigation to point to an incorrect website address in some cases.
Fixed an issue that caused member profile pages to publish a 5-star rating from one review in their structured data when the listing had no reviews at all.
Fixed an issue that prevented all
API
delete requests from reaching the
API
on websites that renamed the
"Member Dashboard URL: Delete Post"
Advanced Setting, because the request was redirected to the renamed address before the API could process it.
Fixed an issue that caused the "Try it out" tool on the
API
documentation page in the
Admin
to send requests to a different address than a real
API
call, so member images were not imported and the
Admin
session was signed out each time it was used.
Fixed an issue that prevented the security check from working on any page whose first form was hidden inside an HTML comment by the website theme, which displayed the message "The security check was not completed successfully" when visitors tried to register. In addition, the "Processing Request..." message no longer remains on screen when a form is submitted twice in quick succession.
Applied a security update to the lead request forms on the website.
Fixed an issue that prevented members imported with the
Business Data
tool from appearing in location searches on non-US websites, because the full state or province name was saved instead of its two-letter code.
Fixed an issue that caused a second Members Export to download the first export's file instead of a new file, when both exports were run without reloading the page.
Fixed an issue that caused a member's own social media links to be published as the website's official social media profiles in the structured data of the member's reviews page.
Fixed an issue that prevented Vimeo videos from displaying on post pages when the video information could not be retrieved from Vimeo, because the embedded player was built with the video's page address instead of its player address.
Fixed an issue that caused member photos imported with the "Import All" bulk action on the
Member Images
page to be saved with a file name that did not match the file actually stored on the website, on websites that convert uploads to WebP.
Fixed an issue that caused the entries loaded by the "
Click To Load More Results
" button in the Specialties section of a member profile to display without their row styling and with broken links.
Fixed an issue that caused the "Select All" bulk delete on the Manage Posts page in the Admin to report success while deleting nothing, for post types that allow multiple images.
Fixed an issue that prevented tables created with the
Froala Editor
from stacking correctly on mobile devices when their column widths or height had been adjusted by hand.
Fixed an issue that caused the description of members imported with the Business Data tool to be cut off in the middle of a word.
Fixed an issue that caused the security check error message on the login form to remain on screen after the check had already been completed successfully.
Fixed an issue that caused underscores to be replaced with hyphens in website addresses, which made the search results page point search engines to an address that returned a Page Not Found error.
Updated the default
Google Maps
, location search and geocoding features to use Google's stable release channel instead of the experimental one.
Improved the security of file uploads so files that contain hidden web code are now blocked. This covers member account uploads, form uploads, the content editor and the Admin file manager.
Improved the security of the contact details form in the
Member Dashboard
to prevent unauthorized changes to a member's account details.
Improved
Google
login
for members whose Google account is no longer linked.
The system now guides them to reset their password instead of leaving them unable to log in.
Improved the performance of the
Recent Members
widget when it is set to display members in random order.
Fixed an issue that caused child pages of a
Web Page
with Wildcard URL Rewrite enabled to use the parent page's address as their canonical and social sharing URL.
Fixed an issue that caused the member search results page to keep the default "/search_results" address in its social sharing URL and paginated canonical URL after the
Default Member Search
URL was customized.
Fixed an issue that caused page types set to noindex to be included in the sitemap in some cases.
Fixed an issue that caused the automatically generated
sitemap
to skip some search results pages on very large websites.
Fixed an issue that caused members who signed up with
Google
or
Facebook
to be placed On Hold instead of receiving the status set in their membership plan, which prevented the email verification link from activating their account.
Fixed an issue that briefly displayed the browser's broken-image icon before lazy-loaded images appeared on the
homepage
.
Fixed an issue that caused cards to display with uneven sizes on mobile devices when the card view option was enabled in the
homepage
Recent
widgets.
Fixed an issue that prevented lead form submissions from being tracked in
Profile Analytics
when the form used a redirect or notification action.
Fixed an issue that caused social media clicks to display as 0 in emails that include member
profile statistics.
Fixed an issue that caused expired posts to display in
Manage Posts
in the Admin when the status and sort filters were applied in a certain order.
Fixed an issue that displayed the schedule checkbox as checked for
Smart Lists
that were not scheduled in the
Admin
.
Fixed an issue that caused some recipients to miss a newsletter when the recipient list changed during sending, and that prevented the "Finish Sending" option from reaching them.
Fixed an issue that prevented images created with AI tools such as ChatGPT from being uploaded, displaying a "File Not Accepted" message instead.
Fixed an issue that prevented accounts scheduled to close at a later date from being closed if the scheduled day was missed, which could result in additional charges in some cases.
Updated the emoji picker in the
Froala Edito
r in the
Admin
and in the email editor so emojis can now be searched by keyword, and recently used emojis are kept for quick access.
Improved the per-plan
Sign Up Form
selection in the
Admin
so the list for each membership plan now only shows forms that match the plan's billing type, preventing a free form from being assigned to a paid plan's checkout by mistake.
Improved how print-friendly versions of pages are handled so search engines no longer index them as duplicate content.
Fixed an issue that caused location searches using a radius to include expired posts in the results total when the post type was set to hide expired posts from search results.
Fixed an issue that prevented the website preview image in the
Admin
dashboard from being updated when the
Block/Allow Country tool
was restricting the website to specific countries.
Fixed an issue that caused the editing popups in the
Froala Editor,
such as the image, link and table options, to appear far down the page and out of reach on websites that load a third-party translation script.
Fixed an issue that allowed a parent category to be selected without any sub-category, which displayed a category on the member's public profile that the member never chose.
Fixed an issue that caused the scheduled account closing process to cancel and email members again when their account had already been cancelled or had been reactivated by an
Admin
.
Fixed an issue that caused saving a membership plan to create a redirect on the checkout address in some cases, which prevented Digital Product and Pay Per Post purchases from completing.
Fixed an issue that caused the
Block/Allow Country tool
to also block integrations that connect through the API, such as Zapier and n8n.
Improved the
Google Maps alert
in the Admin so it now reports the exact problem Google returned, such as billing not being enabled, a restricted referrer or an API that was never turned on, instead of one generic message for every case. Both the website key and the server-side key used for member geocoding are now checked, and the key is also tested on the website's own domain so the result reflects what visitors actually see. In addition, the website key, the server key and the New Google Maps Places API switch can now be edited and validated from inside the alert, and a key Google rejects is not saved.
Improved the
domain connection wizard in the
Domain Manager
in the Admin so connecting a root domain now shows the recommended instructions for that domain's DNS provider: domain forwarding for GoDaddy and an ALIAS record for Namecheap, with the A record kept only as the fallback for other providers.
Improved the
SSL tab of the
Domain Manager
in the Admin. The SSL tab now shows the date a managed certificate renews instead of only stating that it renews on its own, an SPF record that repeats the same entry is now reported as a problem instead of being accepted as correct, and the Point Domain step now names the service that actually hosts the domain's DNS rather than always naming the registrar.
Fixed three issues in the
Domain Manage
r in the
Admin
: the notice explaining that the www prefix had been removed from the typed domain was never visible, the summary reported that everything looked good while the Emails tab showed rows that needed attention, and three messages pointed to an Emails screen that does not exist.
Added the
Member Credit
balance as a selectable field when exporting members from the Admin.
Added live validation to the
Additional CSS
field under
Design Settings
in the
Admin
. Errors such as a missing closing brace are now highlighted while the CSS is being edited, before they can affect how the website renders.
Updated the code editor fields used across the
Admin
, including in the
Design Settings
, the
page
and
email template editors, the robots.txt editor
and the
Post Types

Added an
optional cancellation reason when ending a member's subscription
in the Admin. The reason is now stored together with the cancellation, and it can also be entered when cancelling from the Transactions page.
Improved the speed of member search results
on websites with large member databases by removing an unnecessary duplicate-removal step from the search query whenever the search cannot return duplicate members.
Started a
UI design update for the Admin,
starting with a new side menu and header and a rebuilt
301 Redirect Rules
page in the Developer Hub. Admin pages that have not been converted yet keep their current appearance.
Fixed an issue that caused the image options popup in the
Froala Editor
to open about one screen below the clicked image when a member edited an article in the
Member Dashboard
, which put the Alternate Text control out of reach until the page was scrolled.
Fixed an issue that prevented some images from loading on websites using an image CDN.
Fixed an issue that
prevented
support tickets from being listed in the Admin
when the Admin's login email contained a plus sign.
Fixed an issue that caused a request for a single record on the
API
to report the totals and paging of the whole table, which made integrations read the response as a list instead of one record.
Fixed an issue that caused the
member category CSV import
in the Admin to silently drop a sub-category whose name was exactly two characters long and move its sub-sub-category up to take its place.
Fixed an issue that prevented a saved automatic
sitemap
update schedule from being installed on some websites, so the sitemap stopped rebuilding on the chosen frequency and the tool reported automatic updates as turned off.
Fixed an issue that caused the
Login Date in Show Active Sessions in the Admin to be displayed in Pacific time
instead of the website's own timezone.
Fixed an issue that caused the
structured data (schema)
on public pages to report a
last modified date of the first day of the current month
on every page, and to claim a last reviewed date for a review that never took place. Pages now report the date the listing, post or page was actually last saved, and the last reviewed date was removed.
Fixed an issue that caused the
Form Manager
in the
Admin
to keep the previous Primary Key after the database table that submissions post to was changed and saved.
Fixed an issue that caused deleting a member through the
API
to leave that member's Photo Album tag records behind in the website database.
Fixed an issue that caused a county chosen as a service area to be saved in the city field while the county field was left empty, which prevented that service area from being matched correctly in location searches.
Fixed an issue that caused
SVG files to fail
with a server error in the
Media Manager
, and caused a member's post image in the same format to be saved and then removed, leaving a broken image on the post.
Fixed an issue that caused the
Edit buttons on the Lead Settings page in the Admin to open an empty screen
instead of the lead action settings, which prevented the lead notification email templates from being edited.
Fixed an issue that caused the
Ready to Activate tab in the account area to display a date of Dec 31, 1969
on websites that have no start date.
Fixed an issue that caused a
member or post title containing a double quote or angle brackets to break the links and image descriptions
on search results and profile listings.
In all, over 140 feature enhancements and software updates were released this month.
